mentions.sessionTitle: Under the hood of Microsoft AI models
mentions.shortDescription: Published on the MAI website detailing how Thinking 1 was built
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft AI launched a technical report on its website the morning of the keynote, giving a detailed, over-100-page account of exactly how Thinking 1 was built from scratch. The report covers the complex architecture and training diagrams shown in the session and is organized around three governing principles: capabilities should be learned not inherited, simplicity is sustainable, and scientific rigor over shortcuts. It details data choices including the avoidance of open-source training sets and synthetic data, and the use of decontaminated benchmarks.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build the thing that builds the thing
mentions.rawName: A Discord crawler ("disk crawl") feeding a maintainer dashboard
mentions.shortDescription: Aggregates GitHub and Discord activity, serializing the data into GitHub as a backup/distribution channel so maintainers without a bot token can access it.
mentions.longDescription: To judge maintainer contributions beyond pushed code, the speaker built a Discord crawler [inferred "disk crawl"] that pulls in all Discord discussion data alongside GitHub issues for a non-public maintainer dashboard. Getting the data was framed as just another prompt-away problem, with the emphasis that building such tools is easy while maintaining them is the hard part. The integrated data feeds reports showing maintainer activity across both GitHub and Discord.

mentions.sessionTitle: Union types in C#
mentions.rawName: A `[Union]` attribute and `IUnion` interface ship in .NET 11 Preview 4
mentions.shortDescription: developers can hand-author union types for custom, non-boxing implementations or retrofit existing hand-rolled union classes.
mentions.longDescription: Under the hood, compiler-generated unions are opinionated structs, but developers can hand-author their own union types by applying a union attribute, which is already available in .NET 11 Preview 4. The attribute lets you tell the compiler that a struct or class is meant to be a union, after which the compiler enforces requirements via errors—for example a union must have a public instance `value` property of type object (backed by an auto property with an object field), and it must have at least one union creation member such as a constructor that takes a case type. This enables custom, non-boxing implementations or retrofitting existing hand-rolled union classes.

mentions.sessionTitle: Rethinking CI: Actions, AI Agents, and the End of Commit-Fail-Commit
mentions.shortDescription: An unreleased internal tool that connects an IDE directly to a live Actions runner using the Debug Adapter Protocol, allowing inspection of variables, contexts, and secrets (redacted) and running commands on the runner.
mentions.longDescription: The Actions debugger is presented as a sneak peek of a tool that lets you dig inside the Actions runner itself to troubleshoot and debug issues as they come up. It functions as a real debugger for runners, working within the context of any DAP-accepting client, allowing stepping over steps, returning variables, and running commands directly on the runner. It remains an internal project with no release date, since direct runner access raises security and abuse concerns the team is still addressing.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Build opening keynote
mentions.shortDescription: Agent control plane (Entra, Defender, Purview extensions) with Agent 365 SDK GA, plus MDASH, a 100+ agent security harness that topped the CyberGym benchmark.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft Agent 365 provides governance so every agent in an organization is managed with the same rigor as users, apps, and devices, letting admins review details, control who can talk to an agent, and monitor or block it at any time even after approval. Microsoft also highlighted MDASH, its multi-model agentic security system announced the prior month—an agent harness for security that brings together over 100 agents across frontier and custom models to find exploitable bugs better than any single model. When debuted, the harness topped the CyberGym benchmark. It runs as a standalone CLI (also usable in the GitHub Copilot app), breaks results down by vulnerability domain and severity, identifies AI-specific vulnerabilities, and generates SARIF logs and HTML reports.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build secure and enterprise-ready agents with Agent 365
mentions.shortDescription: A platform for discovering, governing, and securing agents across all platforms, built on Entra (identity), Defender (threat detection), Purview (data governance), and Intune (shadow AI detection).
mentions.longDescription: Agent 365 is positioned as the control plane for any agent an organization is building or running, spanning SaaS agents, endpoint agents, and cloud agents across different platforms and frameworks. It addresses the need to discover, manage, observe, identify, and govern agents, providing observability via inventory/registry, identity, threat protection against generative AI risks like prompt injection and intent breaking, data security against over-sharing or leaking, and governance and compliance. Kendra explains it delivers these capabilities not only for Microsoft agents but also for third-party, custom, and external agents, organized around three pillars beginning with 'observe' since you cannot govern what you cannot see.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: A consolidated console showing all agents (here, 202) regardless of origin, with Purview activity explorer surfacing queries, sensitive-data access, and AI instructions over time
mentions.longDescription: Agent 365 provides a consolidated governance view showing all agents regardless of where they originate—Foundry, Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365, or Fabric. In the demo it lists 202 agents (IQ and web agents from Foundry, a SaaS agent from Copilot Studio, data agents from Fabric), and shows which groups or users each agent is available to and which security mechanisms like Purview apply. Using the Purview activity explorer, the governance owner can go back in time (e.g., one month) to see queries, AI instructions, and where users accessed sensitive data, independent of the data's origin.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering enterprise-grade AI agents with Windows 365 for Agents
mentions.shortDescription: the MCP tools, observability, and governance for Windows 365-enabled agents surface inside the Agent 365 portal alongside all other enterprise agents.
mentions.longDescription: All of Windows 365 for Agents sits within Agent 365. The MCP tool is managed within the Agent 365 portal, and all of the observability and governance for Windows 365-enabled agents surface the same way they do for any Agent 365-enabled agent. This makes it easy for AI admins to configure Windows 365 for Agents alongside all the other agents in their enterprise tenant.

mentions.sessionTitle: Japan Wrap-up Session
mentions.shortDescription: Management of locally running agents as corporate assets, plus an SDK for building governed agents in any environment
mentions.longDescription: Building on the previously announced Agent 365, Microsoft introduced Agent 365 Local Agent, which allows management of agents running locally, such as on employee PCs, treating them as important corporate assets to detect risks and reduce exposure. Alongside it, the Agent 365 SDK lets developers create agents in any kind of environment while controlling them properly on the control plane. The motivation is governing organizations where individuals and a rapidly growing number of agents merge.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building Agents You Can Trust on Windows
mentions.shortDescription: Agents built with MXC gain integration with Microsoft Defender, Entra, and Intune (in preview) so security and IT teams can constrain local agents.
mentions.longDescription: An additional benefit of using MXC to build agents is Agent 365 native integration, which enables agents running on Windows to start secure and stay secure. This integration provides access to the full ecosystem, including Defender, Entra [inferred], and Intune (in preview), whose protections allow security and IT teams to constrain and secure local agents and make them run more securely in enterprise contexts. The capabilities were built working closely with the Copilot team and the broader ecosystem, including partners like OpenAI, Manus, NVIDIA, and others. This complements the summary that agents on Windows should run identified, contained, and managed.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build secure and enterprise-ready agents with Agent 365
mentions.shortDescription: A wrapper SDK (not an agent-building or hosting SDK) that makes external agents discoverable, assigns an agent ID, and enables observability, security policies, and the Tools gateway.
mentions.longDescription: The Agent 365 SDK is the mechanism for onboarding agents built outside of Microsoft. It is explicitly not an agent-building SDK and does not host the agent; instead it wraps an existing agent to make it discoverable within Agent 365. Through the SDK you can assign an agent ID, enable full observability, apply full security policies, and take advantage of productivity capabilities via the Tools gateway. Agent 365 is foundationally an end-to-end governance platform supported by trusted enterprise security solutions—Microsoft Entra for identity, Defender for risk assessment and real-time threat detection, Purview for data governance, and Microsoft Intune for shadow AI.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build secure and enterprise-ready agents with Agent 365
mentions.shortDescription: Roughly six (and growing) skills invokable from VS Code, GitHub Copilot, or Claude Code that instrument an agent for Agent 365 in about ten minutes.
mentions.longDescription: Agent 365 ships specific skills that coding agents can invoke to make an agent ready for Agent 365, demonstrated on a LangChain travel agent built on Node.js. The skills can be invoked from VS Code (via slash skills agent 365), GitHub Copilot, or Claude Code [inferred], and there are around six skills with more constantly being added. They include two 'make' skills plus piecemeal skills such as setup (getting an identity for your agent), instrumenting observability so the agent emits telemetry, and optionally adding Work IQ servers so the agent can interact with productivity surfaces. The process takes about ten minutes to run and ultimately makes the agent an employee in the organization with its own user identity.

mentions.sessionTitle: .NET 11 in depth: Runtime, libraries, and SDK for the AI era
mentions.shortDescription: The CLI now heuristically detects when it runs under an agent and adjusts output rendering, such as disabling the terminal logger's token-inefficient live update in an LLM context
mentions.longDescription: The dotnet CLI now uses a heuristic-based approach to detect when it is being run under an agent context. This knowledge lets the CLI change how it renders output to available output streams and understand more about who is driving it and their usage patterns to adjust internal behavior. For example, the terminal logger (the default build display in .NET 10) has a dynamic, constantly-updating portion that LLMs interpret as a token-inefficient stream of constant changes, so the CLI now disables that live update when run in an LLM context.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering the next AI frontier with a unified data platform
mentions.shortDescription: Custom web dashboards built against semantic models using the same Rayfin SDK.
mentions.longDescription: Extending the Rayfin-based applications, Microsoft showed agent-driven BI apps that let users build custom web pages and dashboards tracking data based on semantic models. Using the same Rayfin SDK, users can add custom data apps directly in Fabric, where Copilot in VS Code scaffolds the project, wires up auth, and connects to governed Fabric assets. The agent can reach for a Power BI capability to generate interactive visuals directly against semantic models without rebuilding the foundation maintained by the analytics team.

mentions.sessionTitle: Move AI workflows from test to production on Microsoft Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Saved agents can be evaluated against custom datasets or open-source benchmarks across metrics like relevance, groundedness, coherence, and task completion, using a judge model
mentions.longDescription: Inside the Foundry playground a metrics configurator [inferred, transcript says 'matrix Configurator'] lets users evaluate saved agents against their own custom evaluation datasets or pre-uploaded open-source benchmarks. Metrics include intent/resolution, coherence, fluency, and relevance, and the full evaluation can be run against the entire agent harness—including multiple tool calls and detailed system prompts—rather than just the model. The demo uploads a 50-row code review eval dataset with ground truth for comparison, uses automated field mapping, and selects a GPT-4o Mini [inferred, transcript says 'GPD Photo Mini'] as the judge model.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and deploy an Azure app with your agent team
mentions.shortDescription: Part of the Foundry Toolkit VS Code extension; visualizes agent workflows live, acts as a playground, captures runtime events, and supports normal debugging.
mentions.longDescription: Agent Inspector is a tool that is part of the Foundry Toolkit VS Code extension and serves multiple purposes. It acts as a visualizer showing how multiple agents in a workflow flow together (updated live from runtime object models), a playground for sending payloads, and a normal debugger where you can hover to see variables. It also captures events from runtime so you can inspect every event coming in and out of the agent.

mentions.sessionTitle: Faster AI Responses with Semantic Caching in Azure Managed Redis
mentions.rawName: Agent memory integration with Microsoft Agent Framework
mentions.shortDescription: AMR's short-term and long-term memory capabilities are natively supported within the Microsoft Agent Framework.
mentions.longDescription: The agent memory capability of Azure Managed Redis (AMR) supports short-term memory (full conversations with TTLs) and long-term vector facts that are tagged by categories such as interest, personal, and work. This lets multiple agents rapidly access shared durable and short-term information, improving workflow performance and user experience, as illustrated with a travel companion example. The AMR agent memory capability also fully and natively integrates with the Microsoft Agent Framework. Demo samples are noted to be available on GitHub.

mentions.sessionTitle: Designing Reliable Multi‑Agent Apps with Azure Cosmos DB
mentions.rawName: Agent memory toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB (public preview)
mentions.shortDescription: A background runtime that handles fact extraction, auto-summarization, conflict resolution, and four memory types, backed by Cosmos DB
mentions.longDescription: The agent memory toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB is now in public preview. It provides fact extraction, auto-summarization, and includes package instructions and prompts to do conflict resolution, extract different kinds of memories, and perform user and thread summarization. In the demo it resolved a dietary preference conflict (vegan to omnivore) and extracted user summaries, such as the user planning a trip to Paris, backed by a memories container in Cosmos DB.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: An agentic automation that monitors a PR, resolves merge conflicts, keeps CI green, and addresses review feedback until the PR is ready, while pushing back on unreasonable requests.
mentions.longDescription: Agent Merge is an agentic automation surfaced as a button on a pull request that focuses on getting work over the line. Once clicked, it periodically checks in on the PR to see whether there are merge conflicts, whether CI is green, and whether there is feedback from an agent or a coworker that needs to be resolved, making all of those changes until the PR is green and ready to go. The demo referenced the very first Agent Merge PR, created by Jeremy on March 19th, which added a CLI health check and went through rounds of CCR (Copilot code review) feedback.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: An agent that polls a PR, resolves merge conflicts, monitors and fixes CI, responds to human and Copilot code review feedback (pushing back when warranted), and merges once approved and green
mentions.longDescription: Boyle demonstrates agent merge, one of the options Copilot offers (alongside create PR and create draft PR) when opening a pull request. The agent periodically polls the PR, fixes merge conflicts, monitors CI and pushes changes until it's green, and responds to feedback from both agents like Copilot code review and human reviewers. Once everything is green and approval is granted, it merges the PR. He frames it for low-risk, functional changes where minor review feedback can be trusted to the agent, showing the first-ever agent merge PR from Jeremy, its creator, which adds a health check verifying the GH CLI is installed at app startup.

mentions.sessionTitle: Modernize intelligent apps and agents with .NET that scale as you grow
mentions.shortDescription: A new capability surfacing agent counts, call volume, token usage, and error rates over the last 30 days, with drill-through into Application Insights logs
mentions.longDescription: Azure App Service provides agent observability that surfaces intelligence about the agents running on your app, as long as the agent is added on the app and Application Insights is configured. It shows aggregate data such as the total number of agents (e.g. five agents in the last 30 days), call volume (52 calls), token usage over the last 30 days, and error rate. To dive deeper into an individual agent, you click "Logs" which takes you into Application Insights. You reach this experience the same way as the MCP server view—via "AI", "MCP servers", and then the "Agents" tab.

mentions.sessionTitle: From prototype to production: build and run agents at scale
mentions.rawName: Agent Optimizer for Foundry Agent Service (private preview)
mentions.shortDescription: Turns production traces and evals into ranked candidate agents by tweaking skills, prompts, tool configuration, and models, compared across quality, cost, and latency
mentions.longDescription: Agent Optimizer for Foundry Agent Service is now in private preview. It turns production traces and evals into a set of ranked candidates by tweaking skills, prompts, tool configuration, and even models. These ranked candidates are shown side by side across quality, cost, and latency, and the developer remains in control to choose the exact winning variant to promote, with trace-back, lineage, and rollback available when needed.

mentions.sessionTitle: From observability to ROI for AI agents on any framework
mentions.rawName: Agent Optimizer in private preview (public preview soon)
mentions.shortDescription: Iteratively creates new agent versions, optimizing system prompt, tool/parameter descriptions, skills, and model selection against rubrics; a demo run improved baseline rubric score from 0.577 to 0.7 with 40/40 tasks passing in 25 minutes.
mentions.longDescription: Agent Optimizer is a new feature that iteratively creates and deploys new versions of your agent, recommending the next system prompt, and trying combinations across tasks while assessing them against rubrics. Starting from a hosted agent, a data set of representative tasks (a 40-query data set in the demo), and rubric evaluators, it can iterate on the system prompt/instructions file, skills, and tool and parameter descriptions since those feed into the agent's context. It doubles down on prompts or context that work and tries another strategy for those that do not, running live and iteratively.

mentions.sessionTitle: Responsible AI in Action: From Principles to Real‑World Engineering
mentions.shortDescription: An agent created in the tenant remains private to its owner until explicitly published to a user or group, giving creators accountability over visibility
mentions.longDescription: The transcriptWindow covers only the speaker's introduction and general remarks about responsible AI principles, without detailing this capability. An agent created in the tenant remains private to its owner until explicitly published to a user or group.

mentions.sessionTitle: From observability to ROI for AI agents on any framework
mentions.rawName: Agent ROI in private preview (public preview soon)
mentions.shortDescription: Calculates net agent value by combining an assigned business value per successful invocation with automatically pulled token costs and user-specified tool costs, with drill-down into low-ROI traces.
mentions.longDescription: The Agent ROI feature, in private preview with public preview coming soon, helps you prove the business value of your agents by doing the math on whether they generate sufficient value relative to cost. You enable it in settings, select an evaluator, and assign a business value per successful invocation (for example, $5 saved each time a vendor analyst agent successfully completes its analysis). The feature automatically pulls in the token cost of your agents while you specify the tool cost, then tracks the net value the agent generates over time across invocations.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering the next AI frontier with a unified data platform
mentions.shortDescription: Beyond analytical engines, agents can now generate Power BI reports and provision full medallion architectures from a prompt.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft announced an expansion of agent skills for Fabric, which give agents the expertise to work with Fabric correctly and with best practices. Released about three months ago for working with the analytical engines, the skill set now expands so agents can also create Power BI reports. A demo showed using Fabric's agent skills repo with GitHub Copilot in the CLI to provision an entire medallion architecture and customer data pipeline—including a LakeHouse artifact and notebook—from a single prompt.

mentions.sessionTitle: AI Building Blocks for .NET: Add intelligence to your C# apps
mentions.shortDescription: Enables connecting a Microsoft Agent Framework agent with an NVIDIA NeMo [inferred] agent via agent cards, with A2A configurable as a custom tool in Foundry
mentions.longDescription: Agent-to-agent (A2A) connectivity lets agents communicate across URLs, demonstrated by connecting a Microsoft Agent Framework agent with an NVIDIA NeMo [inferred] agent so they work together. Mapping the A2A connection requires access to an agent card, located at /.well-known/card.json, which describes how an agent works. The sample runs a writer agent at a local URL plus a second agent, with an A2A server consumed by A2A clients. A2A was initially created and opened by Google and is noted as being part of the Linux Foundation.

mentions.sessionTitle: From Test Kitchen to Table: A Demo-driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers
mentions.shortDescription: Agents can be saved as versions (v1, v2, etc.) and compared in real time against the same prompt to detect improvements or regressions
mentions.longDescription: The portal lets developers save different versions of an agent (e.g., v1, v2) after editing its instructions, with a new version created on save. A 'Compare Versions' option opens a playground where two versions can be run against the same prompt to understand which performs better. In the demo, the instructions were customized to make a friendly Zava Retail assistant that asks about the user's DIY project timing and city to advise on weather; comparing v1 and v2 showed the generic v1 response versus the customized v2 that asks the intended follow-up questions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Your PC, Your Rules: AI Agents Meet Windows Personalization
mentions.rawName: Agentic code generation for RGB effects
mentions.shortDescription: Agents use the public LampArray APIs with a C# driver and Python render-frame scripts to generate custom per-lamp animations like koi fish, shooting stars, and campfire effects from a prompt.
mentions.longDescription: Agents use the public LampArray APIs to design and implement per-lamp effects and animations, executed reliably against real OS APIs by the skill's modules. A C# driver discovers all LampArray devices, and Python effect scripts implement a render-frame function mapping time to per-lamp colors. Effects such as koi fish, shooting stars, ocean waves, and falling raindrops are all just math that translates to color.

mentions.sessionTitle: Turn your agents into action: Connect tools, APIs, and documents
mentions.shortDescription: A mode that builds answers step-by-step by reasoning across file content for cases where values must be derived rather than simply found.
mentions.longDescription: Agentic extraction is a new Content Understanding mode coming in July for use cases where an answer needs to be built rather than simply found—constructed step by step by reasoning across content in a file. It targets harder problems such as determining which clause applies across a contract and its chain of amendments, or root-causing an issue, where finding a single specific value isn't sufficient. For the hardest problems where standard Content Understanding doesn't work, you can turn on the agentic mode to get the best possible extractions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Apply orchestration patterns for production AI agents
mentions.rawName: Agentic testing in UiPath Test Cloud
mentions.shortDescription: three capabilities: autonomous test execution with Autopilot (across Playwright, Appium, SAP, Epic, Citrix), autonomous test exploration, and UiPath Delegate for QA administrative work.
mentions.longDescription: UiPath's agentic testing solution in Test Cloud delivers three capabilities with one mission of autonomous software testing. First, autonomous test case execution with UiPath's Autopilot runs manual tests with no pre-built automations, executing across the web with Playwright, mobile with Appium, or any other UI such as SAP, Epic, and Citrix. Second, autonomous test exploration takes a mission and returns full coverage plans including edge cases; third, UiPath Delegate eliminates the administrative busy work that QA and testing teams handle today.

mentions.sessionTitle: Rethinking CI: Actions, AI Agents, and the End of Commit-Fail-Commit
mentions.shortDescription: Markdown-authored workflows that infuse agent logic into Actions will be generally available in public preview the week following the talk.
mentions.longDescription: Agentic workflows, which let you author Actions workflows by infusing agent logic, are going into public preview the week following the talk. The presenters note you can search for GitHub agentic workflows online to find the preview site, which includes a quick start using the CLI and many examples covering use cases such as issue management, continuous documentation, and continuous improvement. The team is also working on multi-repository support to help coordinate different repositories.

mentions.sessionTitle: From zero to teammate in 25 minutes: Build a Teams agent live
mentions.shortDescription: Agents can be given an agentic identity with their own alias and email, allowing them to live across Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, meetings, and group chats with added IT visibility, observability, permissions, and control.
mentions.longDescription: Much like M365 for humans, Agents 365 enables you to take your agent and make it into a teammate by giving it an agentic identity—its own alias and email—so it can live across the tools and apps where you work, including Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Teams, meetings, and group chats. In turn, IT gains more visibility, observability, permissions, and control to understand the impact the agent has. An agent like the project management agent built earlier can serve as a blueprint to create many project-manager personas that carry context throughout the ecosystem, each with its own identity.

mentions.sessionTitle: Claw and agent harness in Microsoft Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Enabling an AGUI endpoint with a few lines of code gives agents a web UI, including built-in chart controls, without extra code
mentions.longDescription: Building on the sample agent harness console, the team did work with AGUI and the Copilot Kit folks to make it easy to build a web UI on top of agents. With just a couple of lines of code—similar to enabling something in ASP.NET in C#, and similarly in Python—you enable AGUI on top of the agent, giving it an AGUI endpoint. AGUI is an open standard for UI that talks to agents, and Copilot Kit provides a library that can talk directly to that AGUI interface. The demo shows the same agent harness behaviors (such as tool calls completing) surfaced in a web UI, including with a different agent given a sales CSV.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio: Agents That Debug, Profile, and Test
mentions.shortDescription: A forthcoming button lets the agent analyze and resolve merge conflicts, escalating only the conflicts that genuinely need human input.
mentions.longDescription: Launching soon, a button will let the AI agent look at and help resolve merge conflicts, which developers report causing fear, anxiety, and frustration. Testing showed the agent resolves conflicts almost the same way a capable human would. When multiple conflicts exist, it escalates only the one (or sometimes none) that genuinely requires human input, taking the heartache out of the process.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship fast, stay secure: from code to runtime
mentions.shortDescription: A single-pane-of-glass posture dashboard that rolls up findings from the CLI, pipeline, and agentless code scanning, scored and prioritized, and correlated with the cloud environment.
mentions.longDescription: The AI code security initiative is a single-pane-of-glass dashboard for security managers that rolls up every finding from every scan, including the CLI, the pipeline, and agentless code scanning. It shows an overall score, the number of recommendations, which repositories have findings, and how they are trending, presenting a curated and prioritized view instead of a hunt-through list of alerts. Most powerfully, Defender correlates these code findings with the cloud environment, so the same vulnerability scores differently depending on whether it runs in an internet-exposed container with sensitive data versus an internal dev tool. Each recommendation traces back to the source repository and line of code, giving security teams and developers the same data through different lenses.

mentions.sessionTitle: Responsible AI in Action: From Principles to Real‑World Engineering
mentions.shortDescription: Models, tools, and agents can be placed behind an API Management gateway to enforce per-user daily and monthly token quotas, securing cost and blocking volumetric attacks
mentions.longDescription: The transcriptWindow only covers the speaker's introduction and reflection on how production agents were once a "black box," without describing the AI Gateway in detail. Models, tools, and agents can be placed behind an API Management gateway to enforce token quotas.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship fast, stay secure: from code to runtime
mentions.shortDescription: The same CLI scanner inspects model artifacts for malicious content, catching a malicious pickle serialization payload in the pipeline before deployment.
mentions.longDescription: The same Defender CLI scanner shown earlier can also scan AI model artifacts, catching malicious content before models are ever deployed. Defender discovers models across multiple registries and flags those containing malicious or vulnerable content, in one case identifying that a specific pickle file contains a malicious serialization payload connected to a live endpoint; the recommended remediation is to disable, unpublish, or archive the affected model version and redeploy a clean one, treating it as an immutable artifact to replace rather than patch. In a separate repo with machine learning training scripts, model artifacts, and a deployment pipeline, the Defender CLI scan runs within the pipeline and catches the vulnerability before the pipeline finishes. This represents end-to-end AI security: discover what you have, scan it in the pipeline, flag what's dangerous in production, and provide a clear path to fix it from code to deployed model.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplify app dev with cloud-native PostgreSQL in Azure HorizonDB
mentions.shortDescription: A SQL-defined pipeline chunks source rows, generates embeddings via the Microsoft Foundry embedding model, and attaches a trigger that incrementally and asynchronously processes new data without blocking inserts.
mentions.longDescription: An AI pipeline is defined in SQL that takes product catalog data from a source table and generates embeddings entirely within the database. The pipeline performs a sequence of steps—first chunking the data for vector search accuracy, then generating an embedding for each chunk—using the pre-provisioned text embedding model. A trigger is attached so that any changes in the product catalog automatically flow through the pipeline, incrementally and asynchronously updating the data and generating new embeddings. The transcript also notes three managed models were auto-provisioned (chat completion, text embedding, and a semantic ranker), plus support for bringing your own enterprise models.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship fast, stay secure: from code to runtime
mentions.rawName: AI-powered fix command in the CLI
mentions.shortDescription: Copilot analyzes a SARIF result file, understands code context, and rewrites the vulnerable code to fix it without leaving the terminal.
mentions.longDescription: After the CLI scan finds vulnerabilities, the developer issues a fix command that operates on a standardized SARIF result file. Copilot analyzes the vulnerability, understands the context of the code, and makes the actual change to fix it without context switching, filing a ticket, or copy-pasting. This completes the developer loop of scan, find, and fix entirely within the terminal, and the changes can then be reviewed side by side in VS Code before being committed.

mentions.sessionTitle: Modern resiliency from build to recovery through Agentic AI
mentions.shortDescription: Will rank individual resources within a recommendation using live signals such as active service health events and prod/non-prod distinctions
mentions.longDescription: Landing soon, AI-powered resource-level prioritization will take Advisor's prioritization a step further by ranking which specific resources within a recommendation to fix first, since applications typically have hundreds of resources. It incorporates live signals from the environment, such as whether a resource is impacted by an active service health event or whether it is a production versus non-production instance, alongside an application's HA goal. This means customers will know not only which issue types to prioritize but also exactly which resources within those types to start with.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship safer code from your IDE with Aikido
mentions.shortDescription: Runs on generated code and executed prompts to support workflows such as vibe coding.
mentions.longDescription: The Aikido MCP is a component of the plugin that helps with workflows such as vibe coding. On every piece of code that gets created or every prompt that is run, the Aikido MCP is also run.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship safer code from your IDE with Aikido
mentions.shortDescription: An IDE extension that scans files for secrets, code security issues, infrastructure-as-code issues, and code quality issues during development.
mentions.longDescription: The Aikido plugin for VS Code is an IDE extension that scans your files for secrets, code security issues, infrastructure-as-code (IEC) issues, and code quality issues while you're developing, embodying a shift-left approach. It is easy to install, requiring an Aikido license and login via a login button or a personal access token. Once files are open, it identifies issues and pinpoints exactly where they occur, allowing you to assess impact with Aikido AI, report false positives, or fix them with Aikido AI.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.shortDescription: Data type changes no longer require rebuilding tables.
mentions.longDescription: ALTER COLUMN in place lets you make data type changes to a table without rebuilding it. Previously, making data type changes meant rebuilding tables, but now you can alter columns in place with no rewrites and no disruption. Joanna describes it as a long-awaited "finally" moment and table stakes for the Fabric Data Warehouse.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.shortDescription: Multiple schema changes can be grouped as a single unit with automatic rollback on failure.
mentions.longDescription: ALTER TABLE inside a transaction brings transactional safety to schema changes in the Fabric Data Warehouse. With explicit transactions, you can group multiple ALTER TABLE operations together as a single unit so everything either succeeds or nothing does. If something goes wrong, all changes are rolled back automatically, eliminating partial updates and post-failure cleanup for safer, more predictable schema evolution.

mentions.sessionTitle: Latest Cobalt VMs and Azure Boost enhancements​
mentions.shortDescription: Powered by 5th-gen AMD EPYC Turin, up to 35% CPU improvement, in 11 regions with broader expansion in 2026.
mentions.longDescription: Azure's AMD-based DA, EA, and FAv7 VMs cover general purpose, memory optimized, and compute optimized workloads, with options for local SSD and new constrained-core sizes for better cost control. They are powered by fifth-generation AMD EPYC Turin processors, delivering up to 35% CPU performance improvement over the prior generation, scaling up to 160 vCPUs and 1.25 TB of memory with boost frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The VMs already live in 11 regions with broader expansion planned in 2026, and show gains including up to 25% for Java, 65% for in-memory caching, 80% for crypto, and 130% on web applications.

mentions.sessionTitle: Develop faster on Windows with AI playbooks and local agents
mentions.shortDescription: A full-stack, open-source suite of setup recipes (kernel development, ComfyUI image generation, Lemonade integration, a clustering playbook for large models) launched a few weeks prior on client and Radeon GPU platforms.
mentions.longDescription: AMD built a full-stack suite of open-source playbooks—setup recipes covering optimized ROCm kernel development, ComfyUI image generation, and integrating Lemonade into your own application for cross-platform/cross-vendor hardware abstraction, plus an upcoming clustering playbook for running very large 200–300 billion parameter models. The playbooks are open-sourced on a public GitHub project where unreleased ones are also visible. They went live a few weeks prior, launching primarily on client platforms and Radeon GPU platforms, with expansion planned to the Halo box (launching in June) and later EPYC server, enterprise, and Instinct use cases.

mentions.sessionTitle: Taking your AI to the edge with .NET MAUI
mentions.shortDescription: Opt-in via `UseMaterial3`, rolling out through .NET 10 service releases with fuller coverage in .NET 11
mentions.longDescription: Work is underway to implement Material 3 on Android in .NET MAUI, with the first controls already added in .NET MAUI 10 through monthly service releases. It is opt-in via a single line, UseMaterial3, in the CS project, which updates the Android application to Material 3 design where supported. Larger layout changes are coming in .NET 11, where the full Material 3 experience is expected, and developers are encouraged to try it today and provide feedback.

mentions.sessionTitle: Real-Time Intelligence: Building event-driven AI apps and agents
mentions.shortDescription: Lets non-data-scientists select an out-of-box model fitted to their data's seasonality and emit anomaly events for the organization to subscribe to.
mentions.longDescription: Anomaly Detector is a public preview capability that makes it easy to leverage streaming data stored in Eventhouse and configure the right anomaly detection model for specific data with just a couple of clicks. It is designed so users don't have to be data scientists, analyzing the provided data to determine which out-of-box models best fit its seasonality and patterns. Detected anomaly events can then be published and emitted for the rest of the organization to subscribe to.

mentions.sessionTitle: Fabric IQ: Bringing enterprise intelligence into the developer workflow
mentions.shortDescription: Recommends the best model to detect anomalies on streaming Eventhouse data and emits anomaly events automatically
mentions.longDescription: The anomaly detector capability is in public preview, making it easy to connect to existing Eventhouse data. It leverages data science to analyze data patterns and recommend the best model to detect anomalies, emitting anomaly detector events automatically when conditions are met. This was described alongside other out-of-box capabilities including building a RAG solution with Eventhouse, the generally available Data agent, and the Operations Agent in Fabric IQ.

mentions.sessionTitle: Data, apps, and agents: the future of app dev with Rayfin
mentions.rawName: App as a new Fabric artifact type
mentions.shortDescription: Apps can be created directly from the Fabric portal via "new item," generating a deployed app artifact with a child SQL database in the workspace.
mentions.longDescription: From within the Fabric portal, a user can go to their workspace and click "new item" to find a new artifact type called "app." After naming it (e.g., an analysis app) and clicking create, you are given a choice of templates such as a blank app or a data app template that scaffolds the ability to query and connect to a semantic model with enterprise-grade visuals. The flow then continues in VS Code, where copying the template prompt and using Copilot's coding agent scaffolds the data app.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure DevOps meets GitHub, the path to AI powered SDLC
mentions.shortDescription: Microsoft-hosted agents in Azure Pipelines with pay-per-minute billing are available for preview sign-up
mentions.longDescription: One of the new releases noted in the blog post is the ability to use Apple Macs with pay-per-minute billing, available for preview sign-up. This delivers a capability customers have been waiting for: Microsoft-hosted agents in Azure Pipelines billed on a pay-per-minute basis.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering the next AI frontier with a unified data platform
mentions.shortDescription: Production-grade line-of-business apps on governed data, built on the Rayfin SDK [inferred], a type-safe, decorator-based optimizer for agentic development.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft introduced Apps in Fabric in preview for the first time, allowing creation of production-grade line-of-business applications running on top of governed data. It provides one managed backend covering functions, storage, security, and authentication, designed to be secure from the ground up and serving as a great environment for vibe-coded applications. It is built on the Rayfin SDK [inferred], a type-safe, decorator-based code optimizer for agentic development, with project setup driven by a single command from the Rayfin CLI.

mentions.sessionTitle: From the Field: Accelerate Your Development for Microsoft Marketplace
mentions.rawName: ARM Test Toolkit (ARM TTK) runs 49 validation tests
mentions.shortDescription: the same tests Microsoft runs on upload, so running them locally first prevents failed upload cycles
mentions.longDescription: The ARM Test Toolkit (ARM TTK) lets you test-drive your ARM template and Create UI definition locally before uploading the ZIP file to the Azure Marketplace. Running its cmdlets executes a set of tests—49 in this version—covering rules such as variables all being referenced and URIs being constructed in a specific way, plus tests for the Create UI definition standards and security. Because Microsoft runs these exact same tests when the ZIP is uploaded, running them locally first saves time and prevents failed upload-and-retry cycles; all 49 results should be successful before uploading.

mentions.sessionTitle: From Test Kitchen to Table: A Demo-driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers
mentions.shortDescription: An in-portal assistant that explains metrics and project state with links to documentation
mentions.longDescription: Ask AI, also referred to as the agent helper, is an in-portal assistant in Foundry for when developers get stuck and need more information. In the demo it is used to ask what a metric like coherence means and what a rating of four out of five implies. It looks at the developer's project and state, then returns explanatory information along with links to the documentation, acting like an expert chef in the test kitchen.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using AI tools to teach old apps new tricks
mentions.rawName: ASP.NET Web Forms and Aspire scenarios in Private Preview
mentions.shortDescription: Converts Web Forms apps to Blazor, adds Aspire orchestration, and deploys to Azure Container Apps
mentions.longDescription: The modernization agent can take an old ASP.NET Web Forms application (e.g., a default.aspx with components that run at server) and upgrade it to .NET 10, converting the entire Web Forms project into Blazor using the Blazor Server hosting model. Started from a Command Center plan or directly from the IDE, it works on a separate branch, containerizes the app, and moves it to a new pipeline rather than the old ASP.NET pipeline. Aspire, described as a code-first layer you add to your application, can then be added on top of the modernized app.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale agentic AI cost‑efficiently on Azure with Arm Cobalt VMs
mentions.rawName: At least 50% better per-core performance over Cobalt 100
mentions.shortDescription: Cobalt 200 is built on 3nm technology on the latest Arm architecture and delivers roughly 50% better per-core VM performance than the prior generation
mentions.longDescription: The Cobalt 200 processor is built on 3nm (three nanometer) technology on the latest Arm architecture. Its per-core VM performance is at least 50% better than the previous generation. Industry benchmarks (such as SPECrate) and Microsoft benchmarks were tested on the VMs and compared against the previous generation on a per-vCPU performance basis.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build smarter AI systems in Foundry as models and costs evolve
mentions.shortDescription: A geospatial weather-modeling system using satellite imagery and atmospheric data that scales beyond traditional models
mentions.longDescription: Aurora 1.5 is the newest purpose-built geospatial weather-modeling system highlighted in the Foundry catalog. It uses satellite imagery and atmospheric data and is positioned as cutting-edge, able to scale out where traditional models can't. It is presented as an example of domain-specific, purpose-built models for areas like geospatial, robotics, biomedical, and material science.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build the thing that builds the thing
mentions.shortDescription: Has the agent recursively call itself with fresh context to run multiple automated review rounds before committing or landing a PR, driven by one line in `agents.md`.
mentions.longDescription: Auto Review automates the tedious manual loop of repeatedly running `/review`, fixing the found issues, and reviewing again, which the speaker once did ten times in a day. Rather than needing hooks or a forked Codex, it relies on agents being good at following instructions: a single line in his `agents.md` tells the agent to run auto review before it commits or lands a PR. It works by having the agent call its own CLI (Codex calling Codex) to get a fresh context, running many reliable rounds of review; an early recursion bug where Codex kept calling Codex was fixed.

mentions.sessionTitle: What we learned shipping VS Code weekly (without breaking everything)
mentions.rawName: Automated issue triage and AI duplicate detection
mentions.shortDescription: Agentic workflows infer owners, classify issues as bugs or feature requests, and semantically dedupe issues hourly via an internal Chrome extension
mentions.longDescription: The team built agentic workflows that automatically triage GitHub issues by classifying them as bugs/regressions or feature requests and inferring owners from data sources such as the codebase commit history and manual ownership declarations. A complementary AI duplicate-detection capability, injected via an internal Chrome extension (not a native GitHub feature), runs roughly every hour against the latest GitHub issues to find duplicates using semantic understanding rather than just keyword or lexical matching. When confident, it can automatically close an issue as a duplicate, saving the team from triaging many issues sharing the same root cause. The owner-assignment logic is debuggable via full agent logs, for instance to diagnose a multi-owner problem.

mentions.sessionTitle: Securing, scaling, and sustaining your data estate in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: Automated provisioning via Terraform Fabric provider and Fabric CLI
mentions.shortDescription: A single pipeline run provisions a full medallion-architecture analytics project as code
mentions.longDescription: A data developer can provision a complete Fabric analytics project with a single parameterized pipeline run covering workspace name, capacity, auth method, and storage. The pipeline runs a Terraform plan that pauses for manual approval, then the Terraform Fabric provider creates 12 resources—workspaces, identity, storage connections, and Git sync—all as code, after which the Fabric CLI patches notebooks, builds the Direct Lake model, and publishes the environment. Copy jobs pull data from ADLS into a Bronze lakehouse, notebooks transform it to Silver, and shortcuts link tables across lakehouses, automating a full medallion architecture with complete lineage.

mentions.sessionTitle: Discover, govern, and scale Azure resources with HashiCorp Terraform
mentions.shortDescription: Search generates resource definitions and import blocks into a `.tf` file (the demo's four resources produced roughly 300 lines), eliminating hand-coding and copy/paste errors while keeping output reviewable in a pull request.
mentions.longDescription: With Terraform Search, code is generated for you instead of being hand-coded, avoiding copy/paste errors or forgotten attributes. The generated resource definitions are stored in a `.tf` file so they can be inspected, peer reviewed in a pull request, and aligned to organizational requirements. This inverts the import question from "I know what I want, help me write the config" to "show me what's there, generate the config from it, and then let me plan the import" — turning three weeks of inventory work into three commands.

mentions.sessionTitle: Post-Training and Deploying Open Source Reasoning Models in Foundry
mentions.rawName: Automatic trace capture and conversion to training datasets
mentions.shortDescription: Every session and interaction is captured with observability into cost and reproducibility, and these production traces can be converted directly into datasets for subsequent reinforcement learning.
mentions.longDescription: Foundry recently launched the ability to dig into how models and agents work together by capturing every single session and interaction with users automatically, providing observability into reproducibility and cost. These specific traces can be inspected to see model invocations and tool calls, and can then be automatically converted into a training dataset for subsequent reinforcement learning to improve agent behavior over time. This supports fine-tuning a small open source model like Qwen 3 14B [inferred], which operates at 1/10th the cost of GPT 5.2, to learn the business domain and optimal tool usage.

mentions.sessionTitle: Post-Training and Deploying Open Source Reasoning Models in Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Every session and interaction is automatically captured, including cost and reproducibility data, viewable at the level of individual session traces.
mentions.longDescription: Foundry recently launched the ability to dig into how models and agents work together by inspecting specific traces. Every single session and interaction with users is automatically captured, providing observability that includes reproducibility (to learn how the agent behaved) and cost, all captured automatically. Users can drill into traces of any specific session to see model invocations and tool calls such as order lookups and policy validation.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio: Agents That Debug, Profile, and Test
mentions.shortDescription: Visual Studio detects project type and auto-includes trusted, team-authored skills (e.g., from the WinForms and Azure teams) into agent context.
mentions.longDescription: Agent skills are markdown files that make agent workflows more powerful, but they are scattered across plugin and marketplace repositories, making them hard to discover for a given scenario. Visual Studio will automatically detect what type of project you are working on and include relevant team-authored skills into the agent context—for example skills written by the WinForms team or Azure team. These skills are open source, accept community contributions, and are trusted, so they are applied automatically to make the agent more capable.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: Scheduled or event-triggered agent jobs (e.g., a 6 AM local "morning brief," or a cloud automation that reproduces bug reports and writes failing test cases on issue creation).
mentions.longDescription: Automations are scheduled or event-triggered agent jobs used to guard a developer's focus amid a fire hose of feedback sources across public, private, and Slack Connect channels. The demo showed a 'morning brief' automation that runs at 6:00 AM every day locally on the presenter's machine, summarizing in-flight PRs that need to get over the line, critical unreviewed PRs blocking other engineers, and new critical issues. Mario noted that Agent Merge is itself a type of agentic automation running locally, and that automations could be extended across the entire software development lifecycle.

mentions.sessionTitle: Claw and agent harness in Microsoft Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: A new third agent type that acts on its own behalf and has a real user account (email alias, ability to send Teams messages and create Word documents), demoed briefly in the prior day's keynote
mentions.longDescription: Autopilot agents are a new, third type of agent in Foundry, joining the existing assistive and autonomous agent categories. Unlike assistive agents (which act as an extension of you) and autonomous agents (which act on their own behalf but can't use work IQ-style user actions), Autopilot agents always act on their own behalf and have a real user account. This gives them their own email address alias and the ability to send Teams messages and create Word documents on their own behalf, so they can perform actions that typically require a user account. They were demoed briefly in the prior day's keynote, and Scout in Foundry is cited as one example of an out-of-the-box Autopilot agent.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Build opening keynote
mentions.shortDescription: Enterprise-grade autonomous agents with identity and compliance; Scout is the first, available on Copilot Frontier.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft introduced Autopilots, described as enterprise-grade autonomous, long-running agents with full enterprise compliance that run in your tenant. Autopilots can have a name, personality, custom connectors, context, and memory, offering a new way to reduce toil. They join the evolving Copilot experience of Chat, Cowork, and Code converging into one Copilot super app. The first autopilot being introduced is Scout.

mentions.sessionTitle: Apply orchestration patterns for production AI agents
mentions.shortDescription: the CLI and skills are live now with GitHub Copilot support; Maestro Flow is in early access, publicly available in the coming weeks.
mentions.longDescription: Cliff Simpkins summarized that everything shown is available now or in early access. The UiPath CLI and skills are both live now with full GitHub Copilot support, and Maestro Flow [inferred] is in early access and will be publicly available in the coming weeks. Developers can install the CLI, add the UiPath skills to GitHub Copilot, and start building on the platform without leaving Visual Studio Code, with everything needed to get started at uipath.com/developers.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build collaborative agents into apps with APIs
mentions.rawName: Available today on Azure with a sub-15-minute quickstart
mentions.shortDescription: The resource is provisioned from the portal like any other Azure resource.
mentions.longDescription: The Omniagent platform is available today on Azure, provisioned from the portal the same way you'd provision any other Azure resource. Once signed up, the quickstart gets you to a running agent in under 15 minutes, and you can bring your existing Azure OpenAI deployment to get started. The speaker also invites Build attendees to visit the booth to build a co-worker live.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build agentic apps in minutes with Rayfin and Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: The demo's "field engineer" template is checked in and open to community contributions; any GitHub URL containing a Rayfin template (including private ones) can be passed to `npm create`
mentions.longDescription: The field engineer template used for the demo is checked into the "awesome Rayfin" [inferred] repo, which accepts community contributions for templates and other items. You can try the demo by following the instructions to install the field engineer template via a simple npm create command that passes the template you want to use. The same pattern works by passing any GitHub URL that contains a Rayfin template, including private template marketplaces inside your own company.

mentions.sessionTitle: Modern resiliency from build to recovery through Agentic AI
mentions.rawName: Azure Advisor AI-powered prioritization experience enters limited preview
mentions.shortDescription: Collapses hundreds of recommendations into a top-five prioritized, exportable action plan ranked by blast radius, criticality, deadlines, and cost; sign-ups offered after the session
mentions.longDescription: Azure Advisor's AI-powered prioritization experience collapses hundreds of recommendations down to a top-five list with an action plan specific to the customer's environment. Microsoft plans to refine the experience further and bring the resiliency flows and advisor flows closer together for seamless end-to-end resiliency management. The experience started limited preview the day of the session, with a few sign-up spots available by meeting the presenters after the session.

mentions.sessionTitle: Safeguard data across you apps and agents development cycle
mentions.rawName: Azure AI Foundry evaluation results synced into Compliance Manager
mentions.shortDescription: Eval results and agent test status are automatically synced into Purview for associated agents.
mentions.longDescription: Within the Compliance Manager solution in Purview, evaluation results from Azure AI Foundry are automatically synced into Purview for the associated agents. The eval test status of the agents is updated accordingly, as shown in the solution.

mentions.sessionTitle: Responsible AI in Action: From Principles to Real‑World Engineering
mentions.rawName: Azure AI Foundry tracing and monitoring
mentions.shortDescription: Foundry exposes per-interaction tracing, application insights integration, scheduled evaluations, and scheduled red teaming, addressing earlier "black box" feedback
mentions.longDescription: The transcriptWindow only includes the speaker's introduction and a recollection of earlier Build conferences and Azure OpenAI Studio, without describing Foundry tracing in detail. Azure AI Foundry provides per-interaction tracing and monitoring for AI applications.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure Storage for AI workloads​
mentions.rawName: Azure Blob backend for NVIDIA NIXL
mentions.shortDescription: A first-class blob backend contributed to NVIDIA's inference transfer library lets any NIXL-speaking framework (vLLM, Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, Ray) read and write KV blocks to Azure Blob with no custom adapter code.
mentions.longDescription: NIXL is NVIDIA's inference transfer library, a unified API for moving model weights and KV blocks across memory tiers with a pluggable backend underneath. Microsoft has contributed a first-class Azure Blob backend into NIXL, so any framework that already speaks NIXL—such as vLLM, Dynamo, TensorRT-LLM, or Ray—can read and write KV blocks to Azure Blob with zero custom adapter code. This puts KVCache on durable Azure storage that travels with the workload rather than the GPU node.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale agentic AI cost‑efficiently on Azure with Arm Cobalt VMs
mentions.shortDescription: Announced by Satya Nadella in the morning keynote, the Cobalt 200 processor is custom-built by Microsoft for server workloads and natively supports Azure Boost
mentions.longDescription: Satya Nadella announced the Cobalt 200 VMs in the morning keynote, building on the Cobalt 100 launched in 2024. Like Cobalt 100, the Cobalt 200 is an in-house, custom-built processor purpose-built by Microsoft for server workloads and optimized for Microsoft's first-party workloads as well as a variety of third-party workloads. Cobalt 200 VMs come innately supported with Azure Boost.

mentions.sessionTitle: Multi-agents in action with 3 AI agents, 3 frameworks, tools & models
mentions.shortDescription: An agent-first technology that provisions in seconds and scales from zero to one in about a second.
mentions.longDescription: Azure Container Apps Express is described as an agent-first technology introduced recently that underpins the sandbox capabilities. It allows you to provision in a couple of seconds and scale from zero to one in around a second, addressing the cold-start problem where agents shouldn't wait a minute for infrastructure when making tool calls or swarming to other agents.

mentions.sessionTitle: Multi-agents in action with 3 AI agents, 3 frameworks, tools & models
mentions.shortDescription: Fast, isolated, and stateful on-demand infrastructure for securely executing agent-generated code, available to try at sandboxes.azure.com.
mentions.longDescription: Azure Container Apps Sandboxes is announced as a private preview of fast, isolated, and stateful infrastructure on demand for securely executing AI-generated/untrusted code separate from your applications. It executes code securely, resumes instantly, supports snapshots for both disk and memory, and can burst to hyperscale, available at sandboxes.azure.com. Internal Microsoft customers already use it, including Microsoft Foundry hosting its hosted agents on ACA sandboxes and GitHub Sandboxes built on the same technology.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale cloud-native workloads with Azure Linux
mentions.rawName: Azure Container Linux is generally available
mentions.shortDescription: Microsoft's hardened, immutable Azure Linux image for AKS reached GA at Build, derived from the Flatcar Container Linux distribution.
mentions.longDescription: Azure Container Linux became generally available the day of the talk, presented as an immutable distribution for AKS that delivers additional support and consistency. It is positioned as part of the 'one OS everywhere' story, letting the same application run across WSL, Azure Linux VMs, and AKS with the same experience. The speakers highlight immutability as a key selling point and promise a dedicated demo for it.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure Storage for AI workloads​
mentions.rawName: Azure Container Storage distributed cache (early access)
mentions.shortDescription: An AKS-native distributed cache where every GPU node acts as both cache and client over local NVMe RAID, delivering roughly 2.5x faster model loading and hitting Blob only once when many pods start together.
mentions.longDescription: To solve the cold-start problem where many pods each pull a large model from Blob at once (e.g., 100 pods pulling a 70B/140GB model equals 14TB causing throttling and NIC saturation), Microsoft built a distributed cache inside the AKS cluster itself with zero changes to the workflow on top—Hugging Face Loader, BlobFuse, and the Run AI Streamer all sit on it unchanged. Every GPU node acts as both cache and client, with local NVMe RAID holding hot data served at NVMe speed via zero-copy sendfile, and missing data coming over the network from a peer. The first pod warms the cache and the next 99 read from inside the cluster, delivering roughly 2.5x faster model loading on AKS while Blob is hit exactly once. It is in early access now; users can scan a QR code to sign up.

mentions.sessionTitle: Foundry IQ: Fuel agents with enterprise knowledge and agentic retrieval
mentions.shortDescription: Powers OCR, document layout, reading-order preservation, table extraction, and image verbalization during ingestion
mentions.longDescription: Foundry IQ has been integrated with Azure Content Understanding to process files (such as PDFs) during ingestion and understand what is inside them before presenting content to agents. It provides high-end components for optical character recognition (OCR) and document layout, including preserving complex reading order and handling difficult tables that span pages or are sparse. This yields high-quality extraction from content that is then used to index and feed the models. The speaker demonstrated configuring a BLOB storage knowledge source with a system identity and selecting the "standard" content extraction option, which uses the full content understanding capability, alongside automatic chunking and vectorization.

mentions.sessionTitle: Inside Azure innovations with Mark Russinovich
mentions.shortDescription: A storage-account-backed pooled KV cache that raised prompt cache hit rate to ~96% across servers regardless of where a request lands
mentions.longDescription: Azure Context Cache, coming out in preview, is backed by a storage account that caches the KV state for inference requests behind all of the servers, so that regardless of which server a request lands on, the cached prompt and KV state can be fetched rather than re-decoded, saving time and money. This solves the problem where moving inference from one GPU or server to another would otherwise force repaying the prefill cost, and where caching only the system prompt is insufficient. A demo showed a cache hit rate of 81% at concurrency level 1, which dropped at concurrency level 10 as requests were sprayed across servers that might not have the system prompt; pooling the cache across servers raised the hit rate substantially.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unify your entire data estate on a single, AI-ready data lake
mentions.rawName: Azure Databricks native storage in OneLake (preview)
mentions.shortDescription: Azure Databricks can now natively store its data in OneLake, joining Microsoft Fabric and Snowflake's Iceberg tables.
mentions.longDescription: Azure Databricks is now in preview with storing its data natively in OneLake, joining Microsoft Fabric (which has always stored data in OneLake) and Snowflake (which can natively store its Iceberg tables there). This is in addition to anything else that can talk to Azure Storage, since OneLake exposes the same ADLS and Blob APIs, so any service that knows how to talk to storage can natively read or write to OneLake.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure DevOps meets GitHub, the path to AI powered SDLC
mentions.shortDescription: Two MCP servers (local and remote) now expose work items, repos, wiki, test plans, and pipelines; the remote server supports service principals, managed identities, and Microsoft Foundry agent creation, with Copilot Studio integration in progress
mentions.longDescription: Azure DevOps now offers two MCP servers—a local and a remote one—both exposing the same tools for work items, repos, wiki, and test plans. The local server gives a top-tier experience when driven from VS Code with GitHub Copilot, while the remote server has consolidated tools and adds support for service principals, managed identities, and creating an agent in Foundry (it is part of that catalog). Copilot Studio integration has been in progress for several months and is hoped to arrive in the coming weeks. Two servers are kept because the remote server is built on Entra [inferred], whose restrictions currently prevent other clients like Claude, Cursor, or Codex from working with it.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure Storage for AI workloads​
mentions.rawName: Azure Files as a data source for Azure AI Search
mentions.shortDescription: Available via a low-code Logic Apps connector and a native Azure Files Indexer, enabling vector or hybrid indexing of file shares and SMB workloads.
mentions.longDescription: For customers with unstructured enterprise data on Azure Files—file shares, SMB workloads, and lift-and-shift estates—Microsoft has made Azure Files a data source for Azure AI Search, with two ways to bring the data to agents. First, the Azure Files Logic Apps connector offers a low-code path to connect a file share and create a vector or hybrid index, and it handles re-indexing as data changes. Second, the native Azure Files Indexer in Azure AI Search gives teams finer control over enrichment and indexing. Either way, the path from a file share to a RAG-ready index is now only a few clicks or a few lines of code.

mentions.sessionTitle: Japan Wrap-up Session
mentions.shortDescription: A managed, PostgreSQL-compatible open-source database supporting large-scale OLTP, alongside Cosmos DB on the backend
mentions.longDescription: As part of innovating the database layer, Microsoft highlighted Azure HorizonDB [inferred] ("Horazon David") as a newer technology released in public preview. It is described as a PostgreSQL-compatible [inferred] open-source database used by many customers that supports even large-scale OLTP processing in a managed fashion. This complements existing backends like Cosmos DB used on the ChatGPT backend.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplify app dev with cloud-native PostgreSQL in Azure HorizonDB
mentions.shortDescription: Announced the prior day by Satya [inferred Nadella], HorizonDB pairs the open-source PostgreSQL engine with a cloud-optimized scalable storage backend for higher resiliency, scale, and performance.
mentions.longDescription: Azure HorizonDB is a new PostgreSQL database whose public preview was announced the prior day by Satya [inferred Nadella]. It takes the open-source PostgreSQL engine and connects it to a cloud-optimized scalable storage backend to achieve higher resiliency, larger scale, and better performance for Postgres workloads. It is designed for the new era of AI agents, shipping with built-in AI models, AI pipelines, and AI functions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Build opening keynote
mentions.shortDescription: 500+ data centers across 80 regions; the Fairwater AI super-factory (Georgia and Wisconsin) runs near-zero-water cooling and the largest Grace Blackwell deployment; Maia 200 (live in Iowa and Arizona) delivers 30% better tokens per dollar; Cobalt 200 VMs enter preview.
mentions.longDescription: Satya Nadella detailed Azure's infrastructure scale, noting it now spans more than 500 data centers across 80 regions—the most expansive hyperscaler footprint—with more capacity added in the last 18 months than in Azure's first decade. He emphasized end-to-end systems optimization from electrons to tokens and community-grounded principles like not raising electricity prices and replenishing water use. He highlighted Fairwater, the first AI super-factory spanning Georgia and Wisconsin, designed from the ground up for AI in close collaboration with NVIDIA, using a two-story architecture to densely pack GPUs. The transcript window does not detail Maia 200 or Cobalt 200 specifics.

mentions.sessionTitle: Latest Cobalt VMs and Azure Boost enhancements​
mentions.shortDescription: A first-party security ASIC acting as a local key vault meeting FIPS 140-3 Level 3, keeping keys inside the HSM boundary.
mentions.longDescription: Azure Integrated HSM (AI HSM) is Microsoft's first-party security ASIC that acts as a secure, hardware-backed local key vault, letting customers offload keys typically stored in Azure Key Vault, Azure Managed HSM, or an external key manager. Customer keys are never exposed in the clear and remain inside the AI HSM boundary while in use, without performance penalties, and the devices carry FIPS 140-3 Level 3 certification. Crypto operations are offloaded to a local PCIe SR-IOV device on the node, reducing exposure to memory-based attacks (such as crash dumps or memory inspection) while lowering latency for cryptographic operations.

mentions.sessionTitle: Inside Azure innovations with Mark Russinovich
mentions.shortDescription: A FIPS 140-3 Level 3 HSM in every server; releasing an AKV key locally raised signing throughput from ~640 to 18,800 operations/second with no loss of security
mentions.longDescription: Building on Microsoft's hardware roots of trust like Caliptra (donated to the Open Compute Project), Azure Integrated HSM—internally called Manacor—is an HSM deployed inside every single server to provide hardware key management so keys never exit the hardware trust boundary throughout their lifecycle. Keys can be released with policy from a managed HSM such as Azure Managed HSM or Azure Key Vault into the Azure Integrated HSM, which is FIPS 140-3 Level 3 certified just like the HSMs behind those services, keeping the key inside that boundary from HSM to server where the hardware is mapped into the VM for operations. A demo signing payloads with an AKV key showed the benefit, comparing signing throughput when using Azure Key Vault directly (about 640 operations/second) versus releasing the key locally (about 18,800 operations/second) with no loss of security.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale cloud-native workloads with Azure Linux
mentions.shortDescription: Demonstrated running live, with WSL preview noted as a fast follow.
mentions.longDescription: Porvi [inferred] demonstrated Azure Linux 4.0 running live through WSL, verifying on stage that the WSL instance was actually running on Azure Linux 4.0. A simple Python application was started in WSL to later be shown running identically on an Azure Linux VM and on AKS, illustrating the 'one OS everywhere' consistency. The demo emphasized running Azure Linux across WSL, VMs, and Kubernetes with declarative deviations that reduce surface area and CVEs.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale cloud-native workloads with Azure Linux
mentions.rawName: Azure Linux 4.0 VM image enters public preview
mentions.shortDescription: The VM image is now available to test, validate, and provide feedback on.
mentions.longDescription: The Azure Linux 4.0 VM image is now in public preview and available for users to use, test, validate, and provide feedback on. It is part of the consistent 'same OS everywhere' experience spanning WSL, VMs, containers, and Azure Container Linux, using the same Python version, kernel, and internal libraries so an application validated on one runs across all. The presenters note they will share later how to reach out with feedback.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and deploy AI at the edge for real-world impact
mentions.rawName: Azure Local capabilities for small form factor devices (public preview)
mentions.shortDescription: Cloud-based provisioning and management functions previously limited to large Azure Local servers are now available in preview for compact industrial hardware
mentions.longDescription: Capabilities that Microsoft Azure has offered for several years, such as provisioning machines from the cloud and managing them from the cloud, were previously limited to Azure Local on big servers. What's new is that those same capabilities are now available in preview for smaller industrial form factors. This small form factor infrastructure was the industrial computer used to run the demo.

mentions.sessionTitle: Faster AI Responses with Semantic Caching in Azure Managed Redis
mentions.rawName: Azure Managed Redis as a first-party offering
mentions.shortDescription: A fully managed in-memory data store built on Redis Enterprise software, described as up to 15 times more performant and offering a more cost-effective TCO than Azure Cache for Redis.
mentions.longDescription: Azure Managed Redis is a fully managed in-memory data store on Azure and a first-party offering based on the Redis Enterprise software. It offers a much more cost-effective TCO than Azure Cache for Redis and is up to 15 times more performant (the speaker corrects an initial misstatement of 15%). Beyond traditional uses like distributed caching, session management, leaderboards, and pub/sub, it can also power RAG scenarios and act as a lightweight vector data store.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using AI tools to teach old apps new tricks
mentions.rawName: Azure Migrate to GitHub Copilot handoff
mentions.shortDescription: A seamless configuration-file handoff lets IT-led on-prem discovery flow into developer code assessment, with reports returned to Azure Migrate storage
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft now supports a seamless handoff between Azure Migrate and the GitHub Copilot Modernization Agent, since enterprise modernizations often start from on-prem infrastructure discovery rather than code assessment alone. Starting from Azure Copilot/Azure Migrate, IT teams assess production applications (seeing details like the web server, e.g., IIS), then choose "At Scale Code Assessment With Automated Report Upload" to generate a configuration file that bootstraps into the modernize CLI. The configuration includes information about Azure Migrate and where the assessment report should be sent back, so developers get reports in GitHub while IT professionals get reports returned to Azure Migrate Storage.

mentions.sessionTitle: PepsiCo’s blueprint for agentic AI
mentions.rawName: Azure SQL Database / Hyperscale GitHub Copilot integration
mentions.shortDescription: Deeper integration with GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code to improve the Azure SQL developer experience
