mentions.longDescription: Azure SQL Database, including Hyperscale, had several announcements that week centered on deep integrations with GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code. These integrations are intended to give developers a better experience working with Azure SQL. Azure SQL Hyperscale is based on SQL Server and is among the relational databases PepsiCo uses.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using autonomous SRE to move from alerts to action
mentions.rawName: Azure SRE Agent for incident management and resource optimization
mentions.shortDescription: An always-on AI teammate that automates operational tasks, accelerates root cause analysis, and is fully customizable to an organization's standards
mentions.longDescription: Azure SRE Agent is an AI-powered agent for incident management and resource optimization in production environments. It offers three core value propositions: automating operational tasks to keep applications running and protect revenue, accelerating root cause analysis to improve reliability and availability, and being fully customizable to an enterprise's unique operational needs and standards. Described as an always-on SRE teammate that learns how your environment works and acts according to how you want it to, it helped Ecolab reduce daily alerts for site reliability engineers from 30-40 a day down to under 10 a day.

mentions.sessionTitle: Inside Azure innovations with Mark Russinovich
mentions.shortDescription: Currently in limited access for OpenAI's use of the Fairwater data center, with a general-purpose ND144V6 offering planned for the near future
mentions.longDescription: By moving management services off the server onto the Azure Boost card, Azure can offer bare metal instances. These have been introduced in limited access specifically for OpenAI's use of the Fairwater data center, where the GPU servers run as bare metal instances, with a general-purpose offering planned for the near future. A demo showed an ND144V6 bare metal instance, SSH-ing in to confirm no virtualization services were running and using LSPCI to view the PCI bus, including a PCI bridge and 8 Ethernet controllers connected to Mellanox RDMA-capable adapters for the GPU back-end network.

mentions.sessionTitle: Secure agent workflows in GitHub Copilot with NVIDIA OpenShell
mentions.shortDescription: Currently alpha (released at GTC in San Jose in March); beta targeted for the next couple of months, with potential donation to CNCF or the Linux Foundation
mentions.longDescription: OpenShell is still in alpha, having only been released at GTC in San Jose about three months earlier in March, and is now being matured across several areas. The team is targeting roughly the next couple of months for a beta version and hopes the community will pick it up and push it forward while NVIDIA drives it. Longer term, under its Apache 2.0 license, the team is considering donating it to the CNCF or the Linux Foundation.

mentions.sessionTitle: From the Field: Accelerate Your Development for Microsoft Marketplace
mentions.rawName: Bicep visual designer in the VS Code Bicep extension
mentions.shortDescription: an experimental feature accessed by right-clicking a Bicep file to get an interactive, exportable graphical overview of declared resources
mentions.longDescription: The VS Code Bicep extension (recommended for code completion and authoring benefits) includes a visualizer accessed by right-clicking any Bicep file and selecting 'Open Bicep Visual Designer', currently an experimental feature. It produces an interactive graphical overview of all the resources the template will create, which can be dragged around and rearranged. It also supports exporting the visualization, a newer capability useful for creating documentation.

mentions.sessionTitle: Create enterprise AI apps at scale with Bolt and Microsoft
mentions.shortDescription: Developers can bundle a local component library, connect existing repos and workflows, and publish an approved design system into Bolt.
mentions.longDescription: The Bolt command line interface gives developers a programmatic way to interact with Bolt. They can bring in approved assets, connect existing repos and workflows, and make the organization's technical standards available to the broader team. This is one of three pieces covered in the demo, alongside design systems and the Bolt interface, supporting a controlled path from idea to application while preserving governance and developer standards.

mentions.sessionTitle: Create enterprise AI apps at scale with Bolt and Microsoft
mentions.shortDescription: Teams can structure a project brief in Microsoft Copilot and tag the Bolt agent directly to send specifications over and trigger a build without losing requirements.
mentions.longDescription: Work starts in Microsoft Copilot, where a team turns a conversation, set of requirements, or early product idea into a clear project brief, including goals, audience, user needs, constraints, success criteria, and brand requirements. After iterating on the plan (for example optimizing for SEO), the team tags the Bolt agent to summarize the conversation into a prompt and asks it to build with those specifications. Copilot connects directly with Bolt, and selecting "Build" sends the prompt over so the project starts building. The demo shows Bolt creating the project with a full hero carousel focusing on images as requested.

mentions.sessionTitle: Embracing frontier R&D with Microsoft Discovery
mentions.shortDescription: A graph-based information retrieval system that indexes scientific papers using entity-relationship graph structures rather than a traditional vector store, productizing GraphRAG technology from Microsoft Research
mentions.longDescription: The bookshelf is a graph-based information retrieval system, one of three new capabilities added for scientific research in Microsoft Discovery. It can run locally in the app, and with an Azure account it is also available as an enterprise service running in the cloud and accessible from the browser. The user experience is described as familiar because Discovery is built on Visual Studio Code and GitHub Copilot [inferred].

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio: Agents That Debug, Profile, and Test
mentions.rawName: Bring any model, including local and on-prem
mentions.shortDescription: Soon any model can be used in Visual Studio whether running locally, on-prem, or in any cloud, with an organizational security layer to mandate or restrict which models are allowed.
mentions.longDescription: Starting very soon, Visual Studio will let developers use any model—whether running locally, on-prem, or in any cloud—beyond the existing built-in list (Opus, Sonnet, GPTs) and bring-your-own-key providers like xAI and Gemini. This is aimed especially at enterprises with strict security requirements that cannot send code to the cloud, allowing models to run on a local machine or private server room. A security/management layer lets organizations lock down and mandate or restrict which models are allowed. It is expected to be available next week in the Insiders build of Visual Studio 2026.

mentions.sessionTitle: Agentic infrastructure needs agentic observability
mentions.shortDescription: Telemetry stays inside the customer's own cloud for control, governance, and sensitive-data handling
mentions.longDescription: BYOC (Bring Your Own Cloud) is the first of groundcover's architectural bets, keeping everything inside the customer's own cloud. The speaker notes this matters for control, governance, and handling sensitive telemetry.

mentions.sessionTitle: Move AI workflows from test to production on Microsoft Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Post-trained or fine-tuned custom models can be registered in Foundry and served through the Fireworks serving stack
mentions.longDescription: When out-of-the-box open-source models aren't satisfactory, the bring-your-own-weights workflow lets users do post-training or fine-tuning. A base model can be tuned with any fine-tuning framework outside of or on Foundry, and the Fireworks AI native platform also supports fine-tuning via its SFT or RFT frameworks. The tuned weights can then be uploaded and served for inference through the same Foundry deployment workflow using the Fireworks tech stack. Earlier in the window, the speaker also notes agents can be published through Foundry and called in code via a project endpoint and API key for use in Python workflows outside the Azure Foundry UI.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build AI-powered collaboration on a visual canvas
mentions.shortDescription: Generation covers BPMN choreography and sequence diagrams, ERDs, network diagrams, AWS/Azure/Google Cloud architecture diagrams, and UML class diagrams.
mentions.longDescription: Lucid's AI diagramming supports a wide range of diagram types beyond flowcharts, including BPMN choreography and sequence diagrams (demonstrated with a loan application process), ERDs for data engineers who can paste high-level instructions or code, and network diagrams that logically group items like PCs and switches into containers. It also supports basic AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud architecture diagrams, plus UML class and sequence diagrams. All of these are placed into assisted-layout containers so shapes can be moved and arrows rearrange automatically.

mentions.sessionTitle: Turn your agents into action: Connect tools, APIs, and documents
mentions.shortDescription: A new tool built on Playwright that lets agents scrape information and fill in forms (demonstrated auto-filling a Microsoft form).
mentions.longDescription: Browser automation is one of the new tools delivered in Foundry and is available today, built on Playwright [inferred]. It enables agents to scrape information and fill in forms. The demo showed it automatically filling in a Microsoft form based on a submitted request.

mentions.sessionTitle: So you want to become an MVP?
mentions.shortDescription: Over 100 MVPs are contributing at this Build event as speakers and lab helpers.
mentions.longDescription: Becoming an MVP can open doors, and over 100 MVPs are participating at Build by speaking, helping with labs, and doing a variety of other activities. MVP benefits also include receiving NDA information before the public, connecting to product groups for roadmaps and insider information, and giving feedback to those product groups. MVPs also join a global community of 4,000-plus members and receive exclusive invites to events such as the annual MVP Summit in Redmond.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio: Agents That Debug, Profile, and Test
mentions.shortDescription: Agents will inspect the error list and other indicators before kicking off a build, avoiding wasted multi-minute builds destined to fail.
mentions.longDescription: When agents run, they frequently need to do a build, but they sometimes kick off a build that takes around two minutes only to fail on errors that were already visible in the error list. One of the first optimizations coming will have the agent inspect the error list and other indicators before starting a build, deciding whether to build now or do more work first. This is one of many performance optimizations coming to the chat window experience.

mentions.sessionTitle: Create enterprise AI apps at scale with Bolt and Microsoft
mentions.shortDescription: Projects can be scanned for issues before publishing directly to a live site.
mentions.longDescription: Before publishing a project directly to a live site, Bolt offers an inbuilt database security scan. In the demo the scan shows no issues, so the team proceeds to publish and view the live site, ready for customers. This caps off a workflow where a server function calling the OpenAI API was created to generate a travel itinerary.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unlock Claude in Microsoft Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Foundry records agent sessions, traces, tool calls, and offers evaluators (groundedness, coherence, relevance, task adherence, code vulnerability) plus custom evaluators, accessible via UI and programmatically.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft Foundry provides built-in observability for hosted agents, showing the agent in the project and all of the sessions that have run for it. Opening a session reveals the steps taken and produced artifacts, such as a weekly forecast chart and an executive summary in markdown, which are available in Foundry and can be accessed programmatically. You can also view the trace of the agent's activity, including all the turns and tool calls the Claude Agent SDK made while running the workflow. In the demo, the presenter used Claude Code to wire up trace recording for the Foundry hosted agent by having it look up the documentation, then viewed and played back the agent's actions and step metadata in Foundry.

mentions.sessionTitle: AI Building Blocks for .NET: Add intelligence to your C# apps
mentions.shortDescription: Vector store, embeddings, chunking, and enrichment building blocks support a Reader→Chunker→Enrich→Embeddings→Vector store pipeline, shown with in-memory and SQLite stores
mentions.longDescription: To move beyond chat and work with data that the model cannot otherwise access, the building blocks support a RAG pipeline framed as a series of steps: reader, chunk, enrich, embeddings/embedder, and vector store. Vector data handles storage and similarity search, data ingestion handles reading/chunking/enriching, and embeddings convert text into vectors representing meaning. Embeddings can run locally—ONNX mini models as small as 50–80 MB are suggested for learning—or in the cloud using models like OpenAI's text-embedding-small, allowing developers to prototype locally and switch to more powerful cloud models.

mentions.sessionTitle: From Test Kitchen to Table: A Demo-driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers
mentions.shortDescription: Connecting an Application Insights resource enables trace inspection plus per-response scoring on quality and safety metrics such as coherence, relevance, task adherence, and intent resolution
mentions.longDescription: To debug an agent, developers can inspect its traces to see what happens behind the scenes in cases of issues, errors, or hallucination. Collecting traces requires connecting an Application Insights resource; the demo creates a new Application Insights and Log Analytics workspace within the resource group via a 'Connect' button and 'Create a New Resource' flow. Once connected, traces of prior conversations are retained and viewable—including user input, output, and the metadata of input and output messages—in the Microsoft Foundry portal.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplify app dev with cloud-native PostgreSQL in Azure HorizonDB
mentions.shortDescription: A single checkbox during cluster creation activates model management plus pgvector and DiskANN vector search extensions, provisioning three managed models (chat completion, text embedding, and a semantic ranker) with the database.
mentions.longDescription: When provisioning HorizonDB, AI models can be bundled directly into the database so it comes with all model connections already provisioned, letting developers skip the infrastructure setup of connecting models. During cluster creation (demonstrated via the Postgres extension and a 'provision Horizon DB' entry in the new server screen), a single checkbox activates model management plus the pgvector and DiskANN vector search extensions for Postgres. This makes the database ready with AI enablement and models provisioned together with it.

mentions.sessionTitle: Fabric IQ: Bringing enterprise intelligence into the developer workflow
mentions.rawName: Business events in the real-time hub
mentions.shortDescription: Ability to publish curated business events from notebooks for anyone in Fabric to subscribe to for analytics or action
mentions.longDescription: Business events are now available directly in the real-time hub, providing the ability to publish curated business events for anyone within Fabric to subscribe to, whether for analytics or action purposes. This was among the real-time intelligence updates released leading up to Build and was shown in the demo.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building WinUI Apps with C# First Patterns and AI Assisted Workflows
mentions.rawName: C# elevated to a first-class way to target WinUI
mentions.shortDescription: The goal is to lift C# from XAML code-behind to a means of writing entire applications with full access to controls and templates currently locked behind XAML.
mentions.longDescription: Citing trends toward AI-assisted, code-first development with tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio Code, and dynamic UI frameworks like SwiftUI, Compose, and React, the team wants to make C# a primary way to target WinUI. The goal is to elevate C# from being a way to do code-behind for XAML to a way to write an entire application, with full access to the existing WinUI framework's controls and templates. Several of those features are currently locked behind needing XAML, and the team wants to bring C# up to parity.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.shortDescription: Configurable window to keep compute warm and avoid cold starts.
mentions.longDescription: Cache cooldown gives you control over how long your compute stays warm between queries. By configuring the cooldown window, you can avoid cold starts and keep frequently-accessed workloads running with low latency, while balancing performance and cost—especially for bursty or intermittent usage patterns. Because scaling remains automatic, the system can scale up or down based on demand without manual intervention, preserving warm-query performance while staying efficient when workloads are idle.

mentions.sessionTitle: PepsiCo’s blueprint for agentic AI
mentions.shortDescription: PepsiCo's six-agent system (orchestrator, data analyst, tactic, tracking, best-practices, and debrief agents) that prepares KAMs for customer meetings
mentions.longDescription: CAM 360 is PepsiCo's agentic system that prepares key account managers (KAMs) for customer meetings, illustrated through the example of a KAM named Priya preparing for a meeting with a large retail customer. Instead of manually combing through many systems, reports, emails, and documents, she uses CAM 360, which provides a team of six agents: an orchestrator that acts as a smart project manager, a data analyst agent that crunches the numbers, a tactic agent that captures account personas and strategies, a tracking agent that manages the account lifecycle, a best-practices agent that ensures PepsiCo's success runbook is followed, and a live conversational debrief agent that fills knowledge gaps by asking the user questions and capturing the answers. Together these agents give every KAM the equivalent of a six-person support team.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: A forthcoming marketplace for first- and third-party canvas extensions, including a Miro integration with agent-driven design boards.
mentions.longDescription: Alongside canvases, GitHub announced a forthcoming marketplace for canvas extensions, spanning both hyper-personalized miniature canvases and official first-party and third-party canvas extensions. The demo highlighted a Miro integration with an entire agent-driven design architecture, including feedback, sticky notes, and the rich features expected of Miro, but now agent-driven so the agent can make modifications and kick off implementation work. More official canvases from partners are described as coming soon, with more details about the Canvas marketplace to be shared.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: Agent-drivable, bidirectional UI surfaces (terminal, browser, triage boards, whiteboards, Kanban) that users or the agent can author dynamically and check into the repo's `.github` folder for team sharing.
mentions.longDescription: Canvases are agent-drivable UI surfaces within the Copilot app that the agent can fully drive on the right-hand side of the app, including a terminal canvas and a web browser. The agent can open the terminal, send commands, read output, open the browser, and perform automated testing in response to natural-language prompts. The demo showed asking the agent to open the terminal canvas, run a web server rendering 'Hello canvas', and then open the browser to render that page. Canvases support a rich bidirectional relationship and enable users to build their own customized views and workflows.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: Dynamically loaded, themeable extensions with bidirectional agent tools that let users build hyper-personalized, shareable agentic UIs (e.g., a triage board, Kanban board, log/trace visualizer), installable from a gist or repo
mentions.longDescription: Boyle introduces canvases as customizable, agent-controlled UIs that move beyond one-size-fits-all workflows. He demonstrates by dictating instructions to open a terminal canvas, stand up a web server rendering a hello canvas page, and open the resulting URL in a web browser. Everything on the right-hand side of a canvas—UI elements, tabs, and the web browser—exposes tools to the agent, enabling capabilities like agentic web debugging, element manipulation, and automated UI testing. He also references opening an existing triage canvas his team uses day-to-day.

mentions.sessionTitle: Securing, scaling, and sustaining your data estate in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: Capacity overage and Real-Time Hub capacity events
mentions.shortDescription: A 24-hour rolling CU limit for spikes and real-time alerts/triggers (e.g. Teams message when interactive delay hits 90%)
mentions.longDescription: Capacity overage acts as a safety valve, letting admins set a 24-hour rolling CU limit so workloads can spike above capacity during crunch time without throttling. Paired with this, the Real-Time Hub exposes capacity overview events where admins can set alerts—for example, filtering on when the interactive delay threshold hits 90% and firing a Teams message. Together these give real-time visibility and the ability to set up triggers and actions before problems surface, complemented by capacity metrics and chargeback apps for root-cause analysis.

mentions.sessionTitle: Securing, scaling, and sustaining your data estate in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: Capacity surge protection with mission-critical workspaces
mentions.shortDescription: Workspace- and capacity-level surge caps, plus marking workspaces mission-critical to exempt them from throttling
mentions.longDescription: Fabric capacity admins can apply workspace-level surge protection to cap ad hoc reporting workspaces (e.g. at 25% of capacity) and enable capacity-level surge protection that rejects background operations above a threshold to preserve room for interactive reports. Critical workspaces, such as sales during year-end close, can be marked mission-critical so they are exempt from the surge cap and get whatever capacity they need. This provides proactive guardrails that keep priority dashboards responsive while limiting noisy-neighbor workloads.

mentions.sessionTitle: Agent supervision is the new senior engineering skill
mentions.shortDescription: Cognition is working with Cerebras on models delivering thousands of tokens per second.
mentions.longDescription: Swix explains that for massively parallel agents you want them to finish as quickly as possible, and that Cognition has been working closely with Cerebras [inferred] on models (referenced as 3, 1.5, and 3C2 coming up) targeting thousands of tokens per second inference. He contrasts this with typical inference speeds of roughly 50 to 100 tokens per second, and references Talus/Talos demos reaching 17,000 tokens per second, predicting near-instant commodity-token inference is mathematically coming.

mentions.sessionTitle: Modern resiliency from build to recovery through Agentic AI
mentions.rawName: Chaos Studio Workspaces public preview on June 11
mentions.shortDescription: An application-centric reimagining with new scenarios and a new agentic service for rehearsing feared outages
mentions.longDescription: Azure Chaos Studio Workspaces supports the "stay resilient" phase by validating that an application's resilience matches expectations, since customers often believe they are resilient until an availability zone goes down, an AI workload silently degrades, or throttling cascades. Announced at Build, Chaos Studio Workspaces launches in public preview [inferred] on June 11 as a complete reimagining of the experience with application-centric workspaces, new scenarios, and a new agentic service. It enables customers to rehearse the outages they actually fear.

mentions.sessionTitle: Run AI SREs without burning token budgets
mentions.rawName: Cheaper models help less than expected
mentions.shortDescription: Models such as DeepSeek V4 are roughly three times cheaper than Opus but less accurate, and often pull more (and wrong) data, eroding the per-token savings.
mentions.longDescription: Yellin explains that switching to cheaper models is a first optimization but helps less than people think. The baseline assumes Opus 4.7 (or 4.6), and Chinese models like DeepSeek V4 are nearly three times cheaper but less accurate on complex problems. Counterintuitively, the overall price often doesn't drop proportionally because cheaper models tend to pull more data and pull the wrong logs first, then retry, ending up using more tokens. For this reason they run almost exclusively Opus family models with customers and reduce cost in other ways.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: A private, per-user searchable record of every session, prompt, and line of code across all Copilot surfaces, queryable by the agent via a direct SQL API plus full-text search; supports features like `Chronicle stand up`.
mentions.longDescription: Chronicle is a per-user, private record of all of your sessions, scoped to your user and only accessible to you, providing continuity across surfaces, machines, and different GitHub Copilot products. It remembers everything you have ever done — every session, every line of code, every prompt — and can crawl through that history to find relevant context, such as how a prior Rust bug was fixed, and load it into the current session. The agent queries Chronicle using a combination of full-text search and structured SQL queries over a data lake of sessions, exposed via a direct SQL API. It also powers features like `Chronicle stand up`, which reviews work done in the last 24 hours.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Copilot Anywhere: From Remote Control CLIs to Cloud Sandboxes
mentions.shortDescription: Indexes all of a user's Copilot sessions across clients to provide queryable, actionable guidance such as tips, stand-up reports, custom instruction improvements, and cost/token usage reduction
mentions.longDescription: Chronicle builds a queryable history from every Copilot session you run, letting you take actionable steps to improve how you work with Copilot—such as creating stand-up updates, getting tips, and improving custom instructions. It can be run in the desktop app, in the CLI, through VS Code, through JetBrains, and on github.com. Chronicle indexes all of your sessions specific to you across every place you create Copilot sessions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: A private personal data lake over all user sessions across Copilot products and devices, queryable by the agent via SQL and full-text search, with a "stand up" report generator
mentions.longDescription: Boyle introduces Chronicle, a personal private data lake spanning all of a user's sessions across all Copilot products and devices. It exposes a search interface to the agent combining structured SQL queries and full-text search, letting the agent find relevant sessions, plan files, assistant messages, turns, user messages, and every line of code ever edited. He demonstrates by asking Chronicle to find a tricky Rust bug from the past week and load that context into the session, watching the agent generate SQL; he notes agents sometimes make SQL mistakes but self-correct well. It can also answer queries like when a file such as app.tsx was last touched.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.rawName: CI/CD for SQL analytics endpoint plus pre/post-deployment scripts (coming soon)
mentions.shortDescription: Git-based version control via DacFX projects, Fabric pipeline integration, and scripted prep/cleanup steps.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft is bringing enterprise-grade CI/CD support to the SQL analytics endpoint, letting teams treat it like production infrastructure with version control, code review, and automated deployments. This includes git-based version control for SQL endpoint schema represented as a DacFX database project, and native integration with Fabric pipelines for deploying schema changes from dev to test to prod with minimal manual steps. Support for pre- and post-deployment scripts is also added to handle prep work (checking prerequisites, validating environments) and cleanup (applying permissions, configuring settings, running validation), turning the full release into one governed artifact. These CI/CD changes are coming soon to all regions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Rethinking CI: Actions, AI Agents, and the End of Commit-Fail-Commit
mentions.rawName: CI Doctor / CI Failure Doctor template
mentions.shortDescription: A prebuilt agentic workflow that auto-triggers when a target workflow fails, analyzes the failure, and files an issue with root-cause analysis and suggested fixes.
mentions.longDescription: The CI Doctor is a special prebuilt agentic workflow that helps users resolve and diagnose Actions issues more quickly, addressing the commit-fail-commit cycle. In the demo it is applied to a standard Actions workflow running a Python script that reads key-value pair files and sums them, helping diagnose and debug a failure. It is presented as an agent-based solution using agentic workflows to let AI diagnose problems when they arise.

mentions.sessionTitle: Stop routing docstrings to 70B models with on-device AI on Snapdragon
mentions.shortDescription: Qualcomm is researching but not yet shipping a routing classifier; Martinez encourages developers to build their own as a competitive advantage, living inside the orchestrator.
mentions.longDescription: The routing classifier inspects signals such as cross-file reference counts and security flags (authorization requests, crypto/injection, or compliance triggers) to decide where a request should run, with adjustable thresholds and the option to make the model recursive, adaptive, and self-learning. It also uses a 'confident fallback': if the entropy of a query gets too high or execution takes too long, it stops and reshuffles the work up to the cloud, then reviews what went wrong over time. The speaker frames building a more powerful classifier as the core IP and competitive advantage developers and companies can create.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unlock Claude in Microsoft Foundry
mentions.rawName: Claude Agent SDK as a supported harness
mentions.shortDescription: The same agent loop, tools, and context management behind Claude Code is programmable in Python and TypeScript and can run inside Foundry.
mentions.longDescription: The Claude Agent SDK is the harness behind Claude Code — the same agent loop, tools, and context management that power the product used by millions of developers daily — and it is programmable in both Python and TypeScript. The loop is to gather context, take action, verify the work, and repeat until the task is done. Out of the box it provides code execution, a file system, web search, a to-do list, and MCP, plus support for your own custom tools. It also includes infrastructure around the loop, including context management, sessions and memory, permissions, and lifecycle hooks.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unlock Claude in Microsoft Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Claude is reachable through GitHub Copilot and Azure AI Foundry, working with existing M365 identity and data without changing developer environments.
mentions.longDescription: Claude is natively integrated with the Microsoft stack: it is available in Azure AI Foundry, works with the identity and data already managed in M365, and is available through GitHub Copilot. As a result, developers don't need to change their environment, and security and platform teams don't take on a new vendor surface to review. On Azure it also sits inside existing governance — data handling, access controls, content filtering, audit, and compliance — so capability isn't traded for control.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unlock Claude in Microsoft Foundry
mentions.rawName: Claude model family available in Microsoft Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Haiku are deployable in Foundry with shared safety, prompting strategies, API patterns, and identical environment across the three models.
mentions.longDescription: The Claude model family is available in Microsoft Foundry, including Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet [inferred] (transcribed as 'Claude Summit'), and Claude Haiku, positioned among the best models for coding and agentic workflows. Because they are a family, you get the same safety, prompting strategies, environment, and API calls across all three models, allowing you to switch between them depending on the use case. Claude Opus is described as the most intelligent model for genuinely hard problems such as complex reasoning, deep coding across large or unfamiliar code bases, and long-horizon agentic tasks, with the ability to stay coherent over extended runs. Sonnet is described as a strong default.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build smarter AI systems in Foundry as models and costs evolve
mentions.shortDescription: Anthropic's Claude (including Opus 4.8 [inferred], launched the prior week) is now running natively on Azure on GB300 hardware
mentions.longDescription: Anthropic's Claude is now running natively on Azure, on GB300 hardware [inferred] (described as Microsoft's highest-end available hardware). The newest model, Opus 4.8, was launched the prior week and is available in the Foundry model catalog. This brings the Anthropic lifecycle and development tools directly to customers from Azure.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build the thing that builds the thing
mentions.rawName: Clause Reaper, an automated issue/PR triage system
mentions.shortDescription: Spins up a Codex session via GitHub Action on every issue or pull request, guided by a `vision.md` file, to comment on or close items; credited with closing roughly 15,000 issues.
mentions.longDescription: Clause Reaper [inferred] is an automated triage system that starts a Codex session in the cloud via a GitHub Action whenever someone opens an issue or pull request. A standard prompt points the agent at a `vision.md` file describing what the project does and does not want, and based on those rules the agent either comments on or closes the item. The speaker says this approach let him close around 15,000 issues, operating under the assumption of effectively infinite tokens.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using autonomous SRE to move from alerts to action
mentions.shortDescription: Developers can create, configure, and interact with the SRE Agent entirely from developer tools like the terminal and Copilot CLI, using prebuilt recipes from the Microsoft SRE Agent repo rather than the Azure Portal
mentions.longDescription: Instead of going to the Azure Portal, developers can create, configure, and interact with the SRE Agent completely from their developer tools such as the Terminal and Copilot CLI. To create a new agent, you can use one of the prebuilt recipes hosted in the Microsoft SRE Agent repo, which come with a set of connectors, tools, and skills available out of the box so you don't have to build from scratch. The recipe shown creates an agent that connects to GitHub and Dynatrace and is customized to understand the architecture of hosted applications like App Service and PostgreSQL.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: Scheduled "morning brief" inbox digests and an issue-created automation that attempts to reproduce bug reports, writes failing test cases, labels issues, and comments
mentions.longDescription: Boyle describes automations that guard human attention, starting with morning briefs—a local, private automation that runs every day at 6:00 AM across surfaces like Slack, Teams, and Outlook to produce a focused inbox digest of top new customer issues, his PRs needing attention, and teammates' PRs. He contrasts this with a cloud automation called issue repro that continues running even when his laptop is closed. Triggered on issue created in a private repo, it attempts to reproduce incoming bug reports and, when successful, proceeds further (writing failing test cases). The segment also continues the rubber duck cross-model-family critique discussion, noting a Cloud-authored plan is automatically critiqued by a GPT-5.5 [inferred] rubber duck agent.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and deploy AI at the edge for real-world impact
mentions.shortDescription: Using an ownership voucher in the Azure portal, a device can have its software stack (e.g., Azure Linux) installed straight from the cloud with no keyboard or monitor attached
mentions.longDescription: In the Azure portal, a machine can be provisioned by inputting the ownership voucher for a Lenovo SE100 device, which the portal then picks up. The user can choose which software stack to install onto the computer straight from the cloud portal without needing to plug in a keyboard or monitor; in this case Azure Linux was chosen and provisioned entirely from the cloud. This produces a provisioned machine resource representation in Azure Resource Manager that looks and works much like a cloud virtual machine, including management functions such as granting access to a colleague via Microsoft Entra ID.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Copilot Anywhere: From Remote Control CLIs to Cloud Sandboxes
mentions.rawName: Cloud Sandboxing for GitHub Copilot in public preview
mentions.shortDescription: Every Copilot session using a cloud sandbox runs in its own isolated cloud environment, with the host machine becoming optional and work persisting even if the local laptop disconnects or shuts down
mentions.longDescription: Cloud sandboxing for GitHub Copilot, now in public preview, gives every Copilot session that uses it its own isolated environment in the cloud, sandboxed down to the tools, file system, and network you choose to grant it. Because the session lives in the cloud, the host machine no longer needs to be running—you can connect even if your laptop disconnects from the internet or shuts down. It also lets users run many heavy agents in parallel by allocating cloud resources instead of overloading local resources.

mentions.sessionTitle: Latest Cobalt VMs and Azure Boost enhancements​
mentions.shortDescription: Launching in West US 3, East US 2, Central US, and Sweden Central, with more regions to follow.
mentions.longDescription: Cobalt 200 is launching in West US 3, East US 2, Central US, and Sweden Central, with region expansion to continue from there. The product availability region link referenced on the slide is the source of truth for the latest regional footprint. Arm-based VMs are built into Azure the same way x86 VMs are, using the same control plane, tools, and workflows (portal, CLI, marketplace, scale sets, monitor, backup, AKS).

mentions.sessionTitle: Latest Cobalt VMs and Azure Boost enhancements​
mentions.shortDescription: Azure's next Microsoft-designed Arm CPU, delivering up to 50% higher performance over Cobalt 100 and positioned as Azure's leading performance offering.
mentions.longDescription: Cobalt 200 is Azure's next Microsoft-designed Arm CPU and the most exciting item on the Cobalt roadmap, following the strong customer reception of Cobalt 100. It is positioned as Azure's leading performance offering, with a new VM family taking shape around it. Cobalt is described as Azure's all-silicon CPU purpose-built for the cloud, reshaping the price-performance conversation; Cobalt 100 delivered up to 2x the .NET performance of the prior generation and up to 20% lower cost than comparable Azure VMs.

mentions.sessionTitle: Under the hood of Microsoft AI models
mentions.shortDescription: Efficient agentic coding model with ~5 billion active parameters, scoring 71.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.2 on SWE-bench Pro, shipping as default in GitHub Copilot inside VS Code
mentions.longDescription: Code 1 Flash is Microsoft AI's efficient, dedicated coding model built from the ground up for agentic coding tasks at speed, with just 5 billion active parameters. It scores 71.6 on SWE-bench Verified and 51.2 on SWE-bench Pro, one of the hardest real-world coding benchmarks, and is optimized to be cost-effective for high-throughput workloads. It is already shipping as the default in GitHub Copilot inside VS Code, where the speaker encourages developers to try it.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship fast, stay secure: from code to runtime
mentions.shortDescription: Defender traces a running container back through runtime, ship, build, and code phases, filtering on risk factors like internet exposure and sensitive data paths.
mentions.longDescription: Attack path mapping moves beyond a list of findings to answer which vulnerabilities actually put the organization at risk by mapping them to the live cloud environment and asking whether an attacker can reach them and what they could gain. Defender lets users filter on risk factors such as internet exposure and a path to sensitive data, prioritizing the riskiest applications running in real time. The speaker notes that internet exposure, a path to something valuable, and a known vulnerability are each low priority alone but together represent the biggest risk. One example attack path is examined in the Azure portal, showing internet exposure and high-severity vulnerabilities.

mentions.sessionTitle: Low-latency AI for developer workflows
mentions.shortDescription: A lighter, faster variant of Codex that delivers responses in seconds, positioned as a daily driver for interactive coding.
mentions.longDescription: Codex Spark is described as a lighter, faster version of Codex running on Cerebras Inference. The speed Cerebras provides has made it Jason Liu's daily driver, with tasks running incredibly fast. The speakers note the speed is already there and the intelligence is catching up, and they intend to demo automations users can build themselves in the app.

mentions.sessionTitle: Agent supervision is the new senior engineering skill
mentions.rawName: Cognition shipped an agent command centre
mentions.shortDescription: Announced "yesterday," it features local-to-cloud handoff and follows the same multi-agent "conductor" form factor as Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, and GitHub Copilot.
mentions.longDescription: Swix notes that Cognition, a company he advises, shipped an agent command centre the day before, converging on the same multi-agent 'conductor' form factor as Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, and GitHub Copilot. It includes interesting features such as local-to-cloud handoff. He frames this as the industry shifting focus away from managing individual agents toward more organized multi-agent orchestration.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using AI tools to teach old apps new tricks
mentions.shortDescription: A self-hostable portal giving a portfolio-level dashboard of modernization status, timelines, and comparable assessment reports
mentions.longDescription: The Command Center is a self-hostable portal that ships with the modernize CLI and provides a dashboard to see the status of your modernization across the organization. It surfaces phases such as how many applications have been assessed and planned, a project timeline showing start, deadline, and where the agents are today, and lets you share assessment reports company-wide. It also lets you compare between two assessment reports to make informed decisions about which migration looks best.

mentions.sessionTitle: What we learned shipping VS Code weekly (without breaking everything)
mentions.rawName: Component browser for agent-driven UI validation
mentions.shortDescription: Extracts VS Code components so agents can render, screenshot, and compare changes with-and-without a diff directly in a PR without a full product build
mentions.longDescription: The component browser is a feature (rolled out around April) that slices up VS Code components so the agent can work on them effectively without running a full product build. Because components were rewritten to run and accept injected data outside the product, an agent can render a change, take screenshots with and without the change, and post the comparison directly in the PR. In the demonstrated example, adding a back button was accomplished with a single prompt and all validation was done in the PR. The tool is useful both for building new features and for catching regressions introduced as a side effect of other changes.

mentions.sessionTitle: Security for AI and Agent Augmented Coding on Windows
mentions.shortDescription: The same policy maps to different isolation boundaries (process, micro-VM, full VM, cloud) depending on workload risk, avoiding lock-in to one rigid container.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft Execution Containers are built around a composable sandbox model in which the same policy and SDK can map to different isolation boundaries depending on the workload, so developers are not locked into one rigid container. Windows applies the right isolation primitive for the task while preserving one coherent abstraction, letting developers declare intent with policies and have Windows enforce the appropriate boundary. A coding agent, an interactive agent, and a cloud-managed agent do not all need the same boundary, but they share one coherent trust story—giving flexibility in implementation without fragmentation in governance.

mentions.sessionTitle: Latest Cobalt VMs and Azure Boost enhancements​
mentions.shortDescription: Coming to Intel TDX, providing near-zero downtime for maintenance on confidential VMs.
mentions.longDescription: Confidential VM live migration is coming soon to Intel TDX with v6 confidential VMs, providing near-zero downtime for maintenance and upgrades. It eliminates outages and operational disruptions for mission-critical workloads while improving reliability and performance by transparently moving workloads away from failures and rebalancing capacity without customer intervention. A demonstration showed a confidential VM (CVM) migrating from a source to a destination server, with attestation and key exchange occurring and only a short blackout time before the workload resumed.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.shortDescription: Default 30-day retention is now adjustable from 1 to 120 days for time travel, point-in-time restore, and table clones.
mentions.longDescription: The Fabric Data Warehouse's out-of-the-box retention policy is 30 days, which doesn't suit all workloads since some customers want higher and others lower retention. Retention enables time travel, point-in-time restores, and table clones for the specified history period. Microsoft is announcing the ability to modify the default configurable retention setting anywhere from one to 120 days, letting teams balance operational needs with storage cost optimization.

mentions.sessionTitle: Faster AI Responses with Semantic Caching in Azure Managed Redis
mentions.shortDescription: Cosine similarity thresholds (demonstrated at 50%, 75%, and 90%) let developers tune how strict a semantic cache hit must be.
mentions.longDescription: The demo shows how a cosine vector similarity search generates similarity scores against stored prompts, with a configurable threshold set in the application or client to determine what triggers a semantic cache hit. At a 50% threshold the top four prompts qualify as cache hits; raising it to 75% excludes variation four; and at a strict 90% threshold every variation misses. An exact key-value prompt cache hit always matches 100% of the time, giving developers flexibility over how strict each scenario should be.

mentions.sessionTitle: Data, apps, and agents: the future of app dev with Rayfin
mentions.shortDescription: Declarative connectors let apps read from and write back to databases, warehouses, and semantic models in OneLake, with agent instructions that pull schemas into typed classes.
mentions.longDescription: Rather than only spinning up a new backend and database, Rayfin introduces connectors that let apps connect to existing data in Fabric OneLake, including databases, warehouses, and semantic models, and—depending on the data source—write back to it. You declare the data source in your configuration, and agent instructions help pull in the relevant tables and generate classes so you get type safety. It selectively pulls only the schema you need (for example, a single table from a semantic model with hundreds of tables) rather than all the data. Related backend logic can be defined as functions in TypeScript that deploy as Fabric functions with rayfin up.

mentions.sessionTitle: Turn your agents into action: Connect tools, APIs, and documents
mentions.shortDescription: Added as an engine for extraction and classification, alongside broader file-type coverage and integrations for Logic Apps, Agent Framework, LangChain, and Markitdown.
mentions.longDescription: Content Understanding is being improved with broader coverage and quality integrations, including new file types supported. The GPT-5 family of models [inferred] is added as an engine for running extraction and classification, improving quality. Easier integration is provided with support for Logic Apps, Agent Framework, LangChain [inferred], and Markitdown—a set of open-source tools that let you use this extraction as part of your agent runtime.

mentions.sessionTitle: Run AI SREs without burning token budgets
mentions.shortDescription: Supplying or auto-learning environment context, memories, and skills spares the agent from rediscovering the customer's observability setup on every alert.
mentions.longDescription: Yellin describes that in a simple architecture with no memory or cross-investigation learning, the agent must rediscover the customer environment, observability data, and how to query their tools on every alert, including what data lives in which time series databases. By either giving the agent context directly or having it auto-learn context, generate memories, or auto-build skills, the cost can be reduced by roughly 20 to 30%. The savings come from the agent not having to relearn everything in each investigation.

mentions.sessionTitle: Post-Training and Deploying Open Source Reasoning Models in Foundry
mentions.rawName: Converting production traces into training datasets
mentions.shortDescription: Traces from models and agents in production can be automatically converted into datasets for subsequent reinforcement learning runs.
mentions.longDescription: Traces from models and agents running in production can be automatically converted into datasets used for subsequent reinforcement learning to improve behavior over time. Users can select sessions executed against any model version to generate a training dataset, then choose which traces are useful and invoke subsequent reinforcement fine-tuning runs. This supports post-training, a broad umbrella term covering custom data, agent traces, distilled data from larger models, or synthetically generated data.

mentions.sessionTitle: Taking your AI to the edge with .NET MAUI
mentions.rawName: Copilot-authored merged PRs rose from 7% to 62% in under a year
mentions.shortDescription: The team embedded AI end-to-end across reproduction, testing, fixing, MAUI-aware code review, and documentation, with data published per-PR
mentions.longDescription: The .NET MAUI team embedded AI end-to-end across their open-source engineering pipeline, including a MAUI-aware Copilot code reviewer with domain expertise, Copilot custom agents for verification and learning from merged PRs, and agentic workflows that determine documentation/blog needs and even open issues and draft PRs. With humans still in the loop, this approach took Copilot-authored merged PRs from 7% to 62% in under a year, peaking in April. The per-PR data across the .NET MAUI repositories and supporting Android/iOS tools is published openly on agenticengineers.net.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure DevOps meets GitHub, the path to AI powered SDLC
mentions.rawName: Copilot Auto-fix for GitHub Advanced Security (Azure DevOps)
mentions.shortDescription: Generates fixes for CodeQL alerts and opens a pull request automatically, with plans to expand to all alert types, third-party tools, and security campaigns
mentions.longDescription: Copilot Auto-fix for GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS) is being brought to Azure DevOps, allowing GHAS users to automatically fix issues that pop up. In the demo, CodeQL scans run on a repo and surface issues such as SQL injection, showing severity, a description, and a recommendation, with Copilot able to generate fixes. Like the related code-review feature, usage is billed to the user's Azure subscription as part of the preview, and the speaker suggests starting slowly with a few repos to understand the cost.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: Stateful micro VMs provisioned in seconds that suspend after 10 minutes of inactivity and resume with full state, enabling work to continue after the laptop is closed
mentions.longDescription: Boyle demonstrates `copilot --cloud` in the Copilot CLI, which stands up what is called a GitHub sandbox—micro VMs provisioned in a matter of seconds that are completely stateful. They suspend after 10 minutes of inactivity by the agent, and resuming the session from the local CLI spins the micro VM back up with all state intact. He shows the full lifecycle by putting it on autopilot to add an emoji to his README, then notes the changes don't appear locally, illustrating how he can offload long-running implementation work to a sandbox, close his laptop, and return to a finished prototype.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: Stateful, isolated fast micro-VMs with tightly scoped credentials, letting users delegate tasks to run in the cloud overnight without keeping a laptop connected.
mentions.longDescription: Copilot `--cloud` lets users delegate tasks to run in the cloud so they can close their laptop and go home without keeping it connected to the internet. It is built on top of GitHub sandboxes, fast micro-VMs that spin up in a matter of seconds. The sandboxes are stateful and isolated, with tightly scoped credentials, so users can safely test out PRs separate from their laptop environment or kick off a task to run all night, ready to return to in the morning. The demo also showed switching into an autopilot 'Yolo' mode to run tasks in the cloud.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure DevOps meets GitHub, the path to AI powered SDLC
mentions.rawName: Copilot code review for Azure Repos
mentions.shortDescription: Brings GitHub Copilot code reviews to Azure Git repos without requiring a Copilot license or GitHub account, billed to the user's Azure subscription via a dynamic background pipeline
mentions.longDescription: Announced in a blog post, this brings the power of GitHub Copilot code reviews to Azure Repos. It does not require a Copilot license or even a GitHub account—it works on the back end, provided the code is in Azure Git repos (it does not work with TFVC, with no plans to support it). Usage is billed to the user's Azure subscription, and the feature can be enabled per repo from the repo settings.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and deploy an Azure app with your agent team
mentions.rawName: Copilot-generated evaluations via Foundry MCP server
mentions.shortDescription: Copilot generated a 10-row test dataset and evaluators and submitted the evaluation directly to the Foundry service.
mentions.longDescription: By prompting Copilot with "add evaluations to my agent," Copilot used its access to the source code to understand the agent's inputs and outputs and generated everything needed, including a test dataset of 10 rows simulating different customer feedback and suggested evaluators. After confirming, Copilot ran it behind the scenes using the Foundry MCP server to submit the evaluation directly to the Foundry service. The agent results can then be viewed directly inside VS Code.

mentions.sessionTitle: Securing, scaling, and sustaining your data estate in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: Admins can ask natural-language questions (e.g. which domain has the most unlabeled items) instead of running reports or exporting to Excel
mentions.longDescription: In the OneLake catalog's governance report, admins can open Copilot and ask natural-language questions such as which domain has the most unlabeled items, and Copilot answers directly (e.g. the sales domain). This removes the need to run a report or export to Excel and build a pivot table. The governance report itself surfaces three key areas—data estate, security and compliance, and trust and reuse—giving admins a 360-degree view of the tenant.

mentions.sessionTitle: Imagine Cup World Championship
mentions.rawName: Copy Flag named 2026 Imagine Cup World Champion
mentions.shortDescription: Patrick Brown's AI defense platform for creators won the top prize.
mentions.longDescription: CopyFlag was announced as the 2026 Imagine Cup World Champion, selected over two other finalist startups. Founded by Patrick Brown, CopyFlag is an AI-powered platform that helps independent creators turn the invisible problem of AI-modified copyright infringement into a visible, actionable one. The win was announced by Hans Yang alongside Dona Sarkar.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build the thing that builds the thing
mentions.shortDescription: Splits a large codebase into ~50 sections for separate agent review, useful for cleaning up legacy code.
mentions.longDescription: Core Patch [inferred] addresses the fact that there is no `/review` for a project with a million lines of code because it is too much for an agent's context. The principle is simple: take a big project apart into roughly 50 subsections by feature or other division and have the agent review each separately. The speaker says you can download and run it on your project to find many interesting things, and that it is especially good at cleaning up legacy code bases, though it is not as perfect as it could be without scaling to thousands of Codex sessions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and ship faster with a developer-optimized Windows experience
mentions.shortDescription: Linux-style core utilities (e.g. grep) now run natively in Windows Terminal, letting Unix/Mac/Linux scripts from sources like Stack Overflow or GitHub work without translation to PowerShell
mentions.longDescription: Linux-style core utilities (such as grep) are being made available to run natively in Windows Terminal. This lets developers mix systems—for example, piping PowerShell output into grep—and run scripts written for Unix, Mac, or Linux without translating them to PowerShell. Code copied from sources like Stack Overflow or GitHub will work if it uses these utilities, since they are also available on Windows.

mentions.sessionTitle: Taking your AI to the edge with .NET MAUI
mentions.rawName: CoreCLR becomes the default runtime in .NET 11
mentions.shortDescription: Replaces Mono on iOS, Android, and Mac Catalyst, unifying with the broader .NET runtime and enabling tools like dotnet-trace and dotnet-counters
mentions.longDescription: In .NET 11, CoreCLR becomes the default runtime for .NET MAUI on iOS, Android, and Mac Catalyst, replacing the Mono runtime that was still used on those platforms. This unifies MAUI on a single runtime shared with ASP.NET, Azure services, and other .NET workloads, automatically bringing the broader .NET performance upgrades. It also enables diagnostics and profiling tools such as dotnet-trace and dotnet-counters, with more tools under consideration, and developers can opt out with a one-liner if needed before GA in November.

mentions.sessionTitle: Designing Reliable Multi‑Agent Apps with Azure Cosmos DB
mentions.shortDescription: An installable repo of skills usable by agent-skills-compatible coding agents (GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Gemini CLI) to enforce partitioning, indexing, and RU best practices, droppable into CI/PR reviews
mentions.longDescription: The Cosmos DB agent kit is generally available now. It is not a service or an account you provision, but a repo of skills that any agent-skills-compatible coding agent—such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and others—can pull in to give the agent Cosmos DB instincts around partitioning, indexing, RU economics, and modeling for actual access patterns. It produces an impact-ranked report of recommendations, supports interactive pushback, and can be dropped into CI and PR reviews so every change gets a Cosmos DB expert opinion before it merges.

mentions.sessionTitle: PepsiCo’s blueprint for agentic AI
mentions.shortDescription: Among several Cosmos DB announcements that week, highlighted as popular with the community
mentions.longDescription: Among several Cosmos DB announcements made that week, semantic re-ranking was highlighted as one that is very popular and well-liked by the Cosmos DB community. It is part of Microsoft's broader push to give every Azure database integrated vector support for rich searching, tightly integrated with tools like Foundry. Cosmos DB is described as a NoSQL database with transactional intent that PepsiCo has used in one of its solutions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build the thing that builds the thing
mentions.rawName: Crab Box, a cloud test-sandbox wrapper
mentions.shortDescription: rsyncs changes to beefy cloud VMs to run heavy or parallel tests, with fallback across ~20 providers; later extended with cross-platform OS testing, VNC, and screenshot/click/type computer-vision automation.
mentions.longDescription: Crab Box was created after a third-party test-box service ("Blacksmith" [inferred]) became too unreliable, going down for hours a day while the team depended on it; it wraps such sandboxes with alternative providers. It spins up a beefy cloud VM, rsyncs the user's changes into an already-checked-out repo, and runs intensive or parallelized tests there instead of melting local machines. It gained automatic fallback (main provider, then AWS, then Azure [inferred]) growing to roughly 20 providers via pull requests, and was later extended with cross-platform OS testing, VNC, and screenshot/click/type computer-vision automation.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build the thing that builds the thing
mentions.shortDescription: Runs Codex inside Crab Box so maintainers can view, talk to, and take over a shared agent session.
mentions.longDescription: Crab Fleet [inferred] grew from the realization that since Crab Box already runs tests in a cloud box, Codex itself could run in there too, which it can. This produces "multiplayer Codex": when the speaker wants a second opinion he can send a link to a maintainer who can view the session, talk to it, and take over the session. He describes it as multiplayer clanking, built to remove the awkward intermediary of passing agent output back and forth through chat.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build collaborative agents into apps with APIs
mentions.shortDescription: When enabled per session, the agent extracts facts and carries context across web, phone, and text so users do not re-explain.
mentions.longDescription: Memory can be turned on at the channel layer: when you start a session for a user, you tell the Omniagent API to remember, and from that point the agent extracts facts, summarizes conversations, and carries that context forward automatically. Memory follows the user across every channel, so a conversation can start in a web app, continue on the phone, and be picked up over text the next morning. The result is the same agent with the same context and no re-explaining.

mentions.sessionTitle: Orchestrate omnichannel AI agents with Foundry and Twilio
mentions.shortDescription: A live demonstration showing an agent remembering a seat change made on a voice call when the same customer later texts via SMS, resolved through profile resolution on the phone number
mentions.longDescription: In a live demo using an airline use case, the presenter calls the agent and Twilio handles speech in and out while TAC bridges into the Foundry agent framework for reasoning. On the voice call, the agent identifies the caller's flight 543 to Seattle and changes their seat from 23B (an aisle seat) to 23A (a window seat). The presenter then switches to SMS and texts to add a bag to the reservation, and the agent responds remembering the prior voice conversation—correctly noting the customer is on flight 543 in seat 23A, the seat just changed two seconds earlier. This demonstrates shared customer memory across channels, resolved via profile resolution on the phone number.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scott and Mark learn to Vibe Check
mentions.rawName: Cursed CSS query engine by Cassidy Williams [00:21:26]
mentions.shortDescription: A browser-tab tool that loads a real SQLite database via WebAssembly but performs all querying, ordering, and limiting in pure CSS using selectors, checkboxes, and Flexbox; open-sourced on her GitHub
mentions.longDescription: A browser-based query engine, created by Cassidy Williams, that runs fully within a single browser tab and a single API, performing database-style querying in CSS rather than conventional code. It was praised on stage as going 'two or three notches to the right past vibes' and won the 'Best vibes' award. Cassidy confirmed it is open source on her GitHub.

mentions.sessionTitle: AI solutions built to power industrial innovation and sovereign control
mentions.shortDescription: Developers can connect custom MCPs or use catalog MCPs to link local data sources alongside chosen models and RAG
mentions.longDescription: As part of the Foundry Local tools capability, developers can connect a custom MCP to their local data sources, combining the right model chosen via RAG capabilities with custom MCPs and other local tools. This combination runs on an Arc-enabled Kubernetes environment across the different form factors of Azure Local, from single-node to multi-node. The platform also allows discovering and deploying curated catalog models or bringing your own model (for example a container with models from Hugging Face such as YOLO 10 [inferred] or other predictive or generative AI), merged with your own OCI registry and served via vLLM or ONNX Runtime.

mentions.sessionTitle: From Test Kitchen to Table: A Demo-driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers
mentions.shortDescription: Developers can build LLM-as-a-judge evaluators (e.g., a friendliness evaluator) or deterministic code-based evaluators (e.g., conciseness)
mentions.longDescription: Foundry provides a catalog of many built-in evaluators across four categories: quality (e.g., coherence, fluency, response quality, formats), safety (e.g., violence, hate), business, and agentic evaluators (e.g., intent resolution, task adherence, response completion). Beyond the built-ins, developers can create a custom evaluator for an agent; the demo begins adding a friendliness evaluator that rates the agent's friendliness based on criteria the developer provides. This supports tasting and ranking responses against acceptance criteria, following the test kitchen analogy.

mentions.sessionTitle: Beyond REST: .NET Apps That Talk to Hardware
mentions.rawName: Custom hardware test harness for agentic workflows
mentions.shortDescription: A scripted orchestration layer (not unit tests, mocking, or manual QA) that connects to real hardware, deploys apps, and prints line-by-line output so a coding agent can see what worked and what failed
mentions.longDescription: The speaker built a custom test harness after finding that coding agents like Copilot would confidently generate incorrect hardware implementations (e.g. for Bluetooth and NFC) that failed on real devices. It is not a unit test framework, mocking layer, or CI system, but a scripted orchestration layer that physically connects to real hardware, composes the allowed inputs for a test, and drives the system under test by deploying and running. Crucially it prints output line by line so the coding agent can see exactly which steps were taken and what worked or failed, since the hardware itself may have failed. It runs on the dev box, can deploy apps to a phone and cross-communicate with them, and supports USB connection and ADB on Android.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering the next AI frontier with a unified data platform
mentions.shortDescription: Reduces Spark pool startup from 3–5 minutes to 3–5 seconds via pre-warming.
mentions.longDescription: Custom live pools reduce the long Spark pool startup times customers used to experience when loading libraries and network security settings, from 3 to 5 minutes down to anywhere between 3 to 5 seconds. Users can schedule pools to be pre-warmed with all their configurations at a set time each morning, avoiding long startup waits when attaching compute to notebooks. The demo also referenced the up-to-date runtime including Spark 4.0 and Delta 4.0.

mentions.sessionTitle: Discovering Power App Data with M365 Copilot using MCP
mentions.rawName: Custom MCP tools with targeted Dataverse fields
mentions.shortDescription: Developers can build custom tools that pass specific selected fields (rather than whole tables) to produce focused data insights at a prompt.
mentions.longDescription: Beyond the basic CRUD experience, developers can create custom tools for the MCP to deliver richer data insights at a prompt for their users. The presenter demonstrates custom tools such as 'show equipment work order status' that produce tailored UI like cards and charts—dashboard-style experiences similar to what one would build in Power Platform—showing equipment, inspections, and statuses at a glance. These custom tools let users view, edit, and modify live application data without leaving their context.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using AI tools to teach old apps new tricks
mentions.shortDescription: Lets teams encode their own migration patterns, internal libraries, and Azure best practices once and reuse them across the portfolio
mentions.longDescription: Custom skills, also generally available, let you customize and repeat tasks by encoding your team's specific migration patterns once and reusing them across your portfolio. The principle is write once, reuse at scale, so developers keep their business-specific logic and goals while still hitting enterprise-scale speed. It is part of GitHub Copilot modernization, available across editors, the CLI, the command center, and GitHub itself.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.shortDescription: Adjustable allocation of the default 50/50 split between select and non-select workloads.
mentions.longDescription: The Fabric Data Warehouse has had intelligent workload management built in from the start, automatically routing queries so select reporting workloads and non-select ingestion/transformation workloads don't interfere with one another, with resources split evenly by default. Because some environments are heavier on reporting while others focus on ingestion and ETL, custom SQL pools give you direct control over that 50/50 split. For example, you could increase the select workload group to 80% and leave 20% for ingestion to better match how your workloads actually behave.

mentions.sessionTitle: Real-Time Intelligence: Building event-driven AI apps and agents
mentions.shortDescription: Developers can build their own connector, upload the package, and have Fabric host it to bring custom sources into an Eventstream.
mentions.longDescription: The Custom Stream Connector, currently in private preview, lets developers build their own connector, upload the package, and have Fabric host that connector to bring data from their own sources into an Eventstream. It addresses the need for developers who don't want to be limited to the connectors provided out of the box and have their own data sources. It complements the broader Eventstream capabilities such as SQL semantics, multiple destinations, and developer productivity features.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unify your entire data estate on a single, AI-ready data lake
mentions.shortDescription: Data encryption with customer-managed keys is generally available, alongside immutable diagnostic logs and stronger network security (workspace private links, outbound access protection, workspace firewall, resource instance rules).
mentions.longDescription: Generally available today is data encryption with customer-managed keys when your data is at rest in OneLake. This is accompanied by diagnostic logs with immutable storage to see and debug everything happening within the data lake, plus stronger network security including workspace-level private links, outbound access protection, workspace firewall, and new resource instance rules that specify which Azure services are allowed to connect to your data.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: The SDK enables configuration and evaluation runs (inline questions or CSV datasets against expected answers) that the portal alone cannot provide
mentions.longDescription: The Data Agent SDK lets you select, configure, and run data agents beyond what the portal allows—the portal only supports creating the agent, adding instructions, and publishing, leaving wrong answers as a black box. The SDK's main advantage is the ability to run evaluation against an Azure OpenAI endpoint: you provide a base URL and a test token created earlier from an app registration, set up a client with the API version, and then query the data agent with questions and expected answers. This enables systematic evaluation of agent responses that the portal alone cannot provide.

mentions.sessionTitle: Data, apps, and agents: the future of app dev with Rayfin
mentions.rawName: Data app template with Power BI
mentions.shortDescription: A template co-built with the Power BI team for building applications directly on the semantic layer, comprising a data package, a React/Vega-Lite visual package, and agent skills.
mentions.longDescription: The team partnered with the Power BI team to build a data app template, since one of the most common things enterprises build as data apps is dashboards. The template allows building applications directly on the semantic layer, so the effort invested in semantic models and the analytics stack can be reused for applications. It has three core components: a data package that normalizes the Fabric endpoint connection, query retries, and caching; a visual package using React and Vega-Lite components for flexible, AI-first visuals with enterprise-grade defaults; and agent skills that teach the coding agent how to use the packages effectively.

mentions.sessionTitle: Safeguard data across you apps and agents development cycle
mentions.shortDescription: Discover, Protect, and Investigate pillars extend DSPM, DLP, and IRM to agents running on developer machines and endpoints, introduced at Build for managed agents with Claude Code and GitHub Copilot.
mentions.longDescription: Introducing Data Security for Local Agents, which extends Purview's protection to agents running locally—such as coding assistants in IDEs, automation on laptops, and tools on endpoints the organization does not fully control—that can access files, credentials, and source code that never touch the cloud. The same three pillars used for DSPM for AI in cloud apply here: Discover, Protect, and Investigate, mapping to the lifecycle of managing risk around local agents. Discover uses DSPM to inventory every agent in the environment, Protect brings data loss prevention to the local agent layer so the same DLP policies used for cloud agents extend to local ones with no separate configuration, and Investigate provides the ability to look into activity when something looks off.

mentions.sessionTitle: Deploy. Observe. Learn. Reinforcement learning for production agents
mentions.shortDescription: Introduced at Build for residency guarantees in the US
mentions.longDescription: Introduced at Build [inferred] ("Adbuild" appears to be a mishearing of "at Build"), the data zone SKU is a training type that provides data residency guarantees in the US. It is offered alongside the developer preview and standard tier options when configuring a fine-tuning run.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Dataverse plugin: unleashing coding agents on the enterprise
mentions.shortDescription: A single capability embedded in existing coding tools that turns business intent into governed Dataverse operations across schemas, data, queries, security, and admin tasks.
mentions.longDescription: The Dataverse Skills plugin is a single capability embedded in the coding tools a team already uses that turns plain-English business intent into governed Dataverse operations spanning schemas, data, queries, security, and admin operations, all without leaving the workflow. The session demonstrates three different roles doing three different jobs with this single approach, starting with Maya [inferred], a builder who installs the plugin, connects via her Microsoft sign-in, and from one prompt has the agent discover her environment, configure the MCP server, and verify the connection. No config files, docs, setup, or guides are required.

mentions.sessionTitle: Discovering Power App Data with M365 Copilot using MCP
mentions.shortDescription: Each set of tools can be downloaded as a declarative agent zip file and uploaded into Microsoft 365 (e.g., Teams) for end users.
mentions.longDescription: After adding tools and pasting in the Fluent UI, the developer saves and publishes the MCP, then uses the download option to package the tools as a declarative agent zip file. This download must be repeated each time a new tool is created. The resulting zip lands in the Downloads folder and is uploaded into Microsoft 365—for example via Teams by choosing manage apps and uploading the app—though doing so requires appropriate M365 or Global Admin permissions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Faster AI Responses with Semantic Caching in Azure Managed Redis
mentions.shortDescription: Zone redundant by default with a four nines SLA, and a five nines SLA available via geo-replication.
