mentions.longDescription: Azure Managed Redis is zone redundant by default and provides a four nines availability SLA out of the box. Users can also configure a five nines setup using geo-replication, which delivers a five nines availability SLA.

mentions.sessionTitle: Securing, scaling, and sustaining your data estate in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: Default sensitivity label policies and tags at the domain level
mentions.shortDescription: Newly created items are automatically protected, with delegation so domain owners fine-tune settings for their context
mentions.longDescription: From the recommended actions in the OneLake catalog, admins can activate a default sensitivity label policy at the domain level so that every new item created in the domain is automatically protected with no user action required. Because settings are delegated, domain owners can fine-tune the labels for their own context (e.g. the sales domain). Admins can also create tags for organization-wide and domain-specific use, letting users apply them to items and workspaces to improve discoverability and trust.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship fast, stay secure: from code to runtime
mentions.rawName: Defender CLI powered by code name "MDASH"
mentions.shortDescription: A multi-model agentic scanning harness that orchestrates over a hundred specialized AI agents across an ensemble of frontier and distilled models, running a five-stage pipeline (prepare attack surface, scan candidate paths, validate by agent debate, de-duplicate, prove the vulnerability with triggering inputs).
mentions.longDescription: The Defender CLI, code-named MDASH, is a terminal-based security scanner that runs directly in the developer's environment rather than waiting on a pipeline. Instead of a single model doing pattern matching, it orchestrates over a hundred specialized AI agents across an ensemble of frontier and distilled models, running them through a five-stage pipeline: preparing the attack surface, scanning candidate code paths, validating findings by having agents debate whether a bug is reachable and exploitable, de-duplicating, and proving the vulnerability by constructing triggering inputs. In the demo it scans a repository called Benchmark Python and catches real vulnerabilities that traditional static analysis scanners miss by reasoning about what the code actually does. As the speaker puts it, the model is one input while the system around it is the product.

mentions.sessionTitle: Real-Time Intelligence: Building event-driven AI apps and agents
mentions.shortDescription: Works with mirror databases and, soon, general lakehouse Delta Tables.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft is introducing the public preview of a Delta Change Feed connector for Eventstreams, since a lot of data now lives in Delta Tables in Fabric as part of a mirror database rather than only in relational databases. It works with mirror databases today and will soon work with general lakehouse Delta Tables. It was presented alongside related capabilities such as DeltaFlow, Spark Structured Streaming, Fabric Business Events, and Eventstream Observability.

mentions.sessionTitle: Real-Time Intelligence: Building event-driven AI apps and agents
mentions.shortDescription: Simplifies processing Debezium CDC events, adapting to source schema changes, and managing hundreds or thousands of source tables into Eventhouse.
mentions.longDescription: DeltaFlow is a public preview feature that quickly converts CDC events into an analytics-ready form and sends them to an Eventhouse. In the demo, SQL CDC from Azure SQL is used as an Eventstream source, with DeltaFlow handling schema registry storage and creating separate tables in Eventhouse for each source table. It abstracts away details like CDC resume handling, performing the initial snapshot replication so SQL database changes become available in the Eventhouse within seconds.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and deploy an Azure app with your agent team
mentions.shortDescription: A wizard pushes the locally running agent to the Foundry service as a fully managed, observable hosted agent, with log streaming that Copilot can read to fix errors.
mentions.longDescription: A command, "deploy hosted agent," pushes the locally running agent into the Foundry service to run as a host agent that is fully managed and observable, guided by a short wizard. Once deployed, a playground talks with the service live, and a log streaming feature returns all the call stacks happening on the server side. That log can be reviewed directly with VS Code Copilot, which extracts the messages from the service so Copilot can fix any errors, exceptions, or issues right there.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build agentic apps in minutes with Rayfin and Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: Rayfin apps are Fabric workspace items that inherit the workspace's capacity, CU billing model, and permission/sharing model
mentions.longDescription: In response to a question about deploying to a capacity, the speaker explains that a Rayfin app is an item inside Fabric, just like other Fabric workspace items called "app." You can create the item in any workspace, and whatever capacity that workspace is attached to is the capacity the application uses, following the same CU billing model. Under-the-hood services include the Fabric SQL database and the hosting/reference service, but you are only charged for some of the child services.

mentions.sessionTitle: Create enterprise AI apps at scale with Bolt and Microsoft
mentions.rawName: Design systems as a shared foundation
mentions.shortDescription: Bolt can ingest code, design artifacts, and documentation to generate a navigable Storybook instance so new projects start from approved components rather than a blank canvas.
mentions.longDescription: Using the Bolt CLI, a developer can bundle and create a design system from a local component library, sending code, design artifacts, and documentation to a Bolt Agent. Bolt makes sense of the code and design components so the team can build new applications, prototypes, or internal apps on top of that existing material. The core value is reducing the non-deterministic qualities of agents and giving back control over what code is produced and used. The demo prompts via Copilot to create a design system and publish it within Bolt, then views it at bolt.new under Settings.

mentions.sessionTitle: Deploy. Observe. Learn. Reinforcement learning for production agents
mentions.shortDescription: Hosting with no hosting fee to make experimentation cheaper
mentions.longDescription: Developer tier hosting is a newly introduced option with no hosting fee, making experimentation easy and cheap. It serves as a bridge to get fine-tuned models to production, after which substantial cost savings appear as usage ramps up. It complements developer tier training (spot capacity at 50% off), where the median supervised fine-tuning job costs about a dollar.

mentions.sessionTitle: Deploy. Observe. Learn. Reinforcement learning for production agents
mentions.shortDescription: A spot/low-priority SKU offering training at 50% off standard-tier cost, with the median supervised fine-tuning job costing about a dollar
mentions.longDescription: Developer tier (developer preview) is a training SKU selectable as a training type when starting a supervised fine-tuning run, allowing training at half the cost of a standard-tier job. It runs on a low-priority VM, so jobs may take longer, but it is well-suited for developers worried about fine-tuning being expensive. The training type options also govern data residency and cost.

mentions.sessionTitle: AI Building Blocks for .NET: Add intelligence to your C# apps
mentions.shortDescription: A visual tool to inspect agents and workflows in real time, including traces and tool calls
mentions.longDescription: DevUI is described as a super-cool tool for web applications that lets you see in real time how agents are working through a visual interface. You can test your workflows and agents in it, and view traces, tool calls, and more within a single, nice UI application. It is presented in the context of running a workflow (which is itself internally an agent) using StreamingAsync.

mentions.sessionTitle: Data Science & Machine Learning with Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: Diabetes-projection demo using a public Microsoft dataset [00:05:00]
mentions.shortDescription: A healthcare scenario ingests data from Azure Blob storage, splits it 70/30 for training and validation, and compares a linear regression against a decision tree regressor, with the decision tree scoring better
mentions.longDescription: The presenter lists and retrieves machine learning experiments in a Fabric workspace, focusing on one named 'experiment-diabetes', and retrieves its runs (each with a run ID, finished status, and artifact URL). A quick visualization compares models, showing better scores with the decision tree regressor than with linear regression. The presenter explains that you can run multiple experiment iterations, inspect per-run metrics like training score and mean square error, then select a preferred run and save it as a model in the Fabric workspace (named 'build table 2602' [inferred]).

mentions.sessionTitle: Inside Azure innovations with Mark Russinovich
mentions.rawName: Direct virtualization for Azure Container Instances
mentions.shortDescription: Places Hyper-V-isolated containers directly on servers as peers to the management VM, removing virtualization overhead; full fleet migration expected to take one to two years
mentions.longDescription: Direct virtualization removes the virtualization overhead in Azure Container Instances by placing Hyper-V-isolated containers directly on servers as peers to the management VM, rather than nested inside a virtual machine. The management VM acts as the parent partition or layer-one virtualization host, while layer-two virtualization hosts (child VMs) host individual containers or pods, providing strong hostile multi-tenant isolation without process isolation. ACI is widely adopted across Microsoft services such as GitHub Actions, Python in Excel, and Horizon DB. Migrating the entire fleet to direct virtualization is expected to take a year or two and deliver significant performance and efficiency benefits.

mentions.sessionTitle: Embracing frontier R&D with Microsoft Discovery
mentions.shortDescription: A cognitive layer that fully automates the discovery loop (hypothesis, experimentation, reasoning), spawning and assigning tasks to agents and abandoning or continuing research paths based on model confidence scores
mentions.longDescription: The Discovery Engine is one of three new capabilities added for scientific research, and it fully automates the scientific discovery loop of hypothesis, experimentation, and reasoning. It can run locally in the Discovery app, and with an Azure account it is also supported as an enterprise service running in the cloud, accessible via the browser. It works alongside the bookshelf and the scientific research-tailored user experience.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.shortDescription: Compact filters from smaller tables are pushed down to large fact-table scans to eliminate non-matching rows early.
mentions.longDescription: Distributed bitmap filters speed up queries by addressing wasted work in JOINs between large fact tables and smaller dimension tables, where many fact-table rows never match anything useful. The feature takes the smaller table, builds a compact filter from it, and pushes that filter down to where the large table is being scanned, eliminating non-matching rows early. This reduces data movement, IO, and resource requests for faster query execution, especially for selective JOINs and GROUP BY aggregations. The feature is coming soon and is expected to drive significant performance gains on common warehouse workloads.

mentions.sessionTitle: Designing Reliable Multi‑Agent Apps with Azure Cosmos DB
mentions.shortDescription: Atomic execution of writes across partitions and containers, so multi-container operations succeed or fail together
mentions.longDescription: Distributed transactions in Cosmos DB are now in public preview, providing atomic execution of multiple requests. Whereas previously a transaction was limited to a single partition key, you can now get atomic transactions across partitions or even across containers. In the booking use case this means updating the trips container status, storing memory, and emitting a booking event to the events container can all either succeed or fail together, giving consistency at the container level and simplifying application error handling.

mentions.sessionTitle: Taking your AI to the edge with .NET MAUI
mentions.shortDescription: Interactive target-framework/device prompts and terminal hot reload, designed to be agent-friendly CLI tooling
mentions.longDescription: New CLI tooling lets developers simply run `dotnet run` instead of longer build/run commands with target framework flags, with interactive prompts to select the target framework and device (such as switching between Android or iOS emulators). `dotnet watch` adds terminal-based hot reload, starting the app on an emulator or simulator and automatically picking up code changes in the running debug session. These CLI tools are designed to be agent-friendly, being easy for Copilot to invoke and parse, while also serving terminal fans.

mentions.sessionTitle: .NET 11 in depth: Runtime, libraries, and SDK for the AI era
mentions.rawName: `dotnet run` gains first-class device deployment for .NET MAUI
mentions.shortDescription: The MAUI team contributed enhancements so `run` can pick a target framework, select a valid device, build the installation payload, and launch it on a simulator, via an extensible protocol usable by frameworks like Uno or Avalonia
mentions.longDescription: Starting in .NET 11, the .NET MAUI team contributed enhancements to `dotnet run` to make device flows a first-class citizen, expanding the .NET MAUI targets so that `run` handles device deployment. The flow lets `dotnet run` pick the target framework to deploy to, select a valid device for that framework, upload the device payload, and launch it on a simulator. `run` also now understands how to query the devices available, and this entire protocol is extensible, working not just for MAUI but extendable to UI frameworks like Uno or Avalonia.

mentions.sessionTitle: .NET 11 in depth: Runtime, libraries, and SDK for the AI era
mentions.shortDescription: A native AOT tool for consistent, admin-free, user-level acquisition and management of .NET tool chains across platforms, with previews coming soon
mentions.longDescription: `dotnet up` is a Native AOT tool aimed at giving users who work across multiple platforms, or teams whose members work on multiple platforms, a consistent way to acquire and manage their .NET toolchains. It supports nightlies, uses global.json if present, and performs user-level installs of the tooling so no admin is required. Previews of the tool are coming soon, and a dedicated deep-dive recording was made available for Build.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplifying .NET Installs with dotnetup
mentions.rawName: dotnetup, a new cross-platform .NET install manager
mentions.shortDescription: A native AOT tool that behaves identically on every platform and installs .NET into the user directory without admin elevation.
mentions.longDescription: dotnetup is a new product the .NET SDK team has been building to simplify getting .NET onto a machine and managing versions over time. Chet Husk frames the problem that users today fall into one of two buckets: Visual Studio on Windows, where the toolchain is managed and updated for you, or 'everyone else' who lacks that experience — which is the gap dotnetup aims to solve. The session previews the initial preview versions of dotnetup along with its roadmap.

mentions.sessionTitle: Secure agent workflows in GitHub Copilot with NVIDIA OpenShell
mentions.shortDescription: Users can select the underlying isolation primitive (Firecracker, hardened containers, trusted computing, or gVisor/Kubernetes sandboxing) while OpenShell enforces the runtime on top
mentions.longDescription: OpenShell introduces a concept called drivers that lets users pick the underlying sandboxing perimeter when launching it. Options include Firecracker, hardened containers, trusted computing, or SIG primitive sandboxing from Kubernetes [inferred: gVisor]. OpenShell relies on whatever isolation technology is chosen under the hood and enforces its runtime on top of it.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building Agents You Can Trust on Windows
mentions.shortDescription: MXC scales from small processes to VMs, Firecracker-style micro VMs, and cloud PCs, spanning Windows, WSL, and Linux.
mentions.longDescription: Dynamic composition means that when an agent runs there is no fixed container; the MXC library creates the container on the fly by combining the definition of the application or action, the user's consent and permissions, and the policy defined by IT into a container configuration. It then looks at the available operating system primitives to craft the appropriate container. MXC is a full cross-platform library spanning Windows, WSL, and Linux that can scale from tiny small processes to VMs, micro VMs, Firecracker-style micro VMs, all the way up to cloud-based PCs. This allows a security boundary that is designed and proportionate to the task to be accomplished.

mentions.sessionTitle: Expand local AI reach with Windows ML
mentions.shortDescription: Apps can dynamically acquire vendor execution providers (e.g. QNN) via Windows Update rather than bundling roughly 80 MB of providers, reducing app size.
mentions.longDescription: Windows ML allows apps to dynamically acquire hardware vendor execution providers (SDKs built by vendors like AMD, Intel, NVIDIA, and Qualcomm that accelerate models on NPUs, GPUs, and CPUs) rather than bundling them. This means an app doesn't need to carry roughly 80 MB of providers, reducing app size and simplifying distribution. In the demo, the app creates an ORT environment, uses the Find All Providers API to discover compatible execution providers, locates the QNN EP, calls EnsureReadyAsync to make it ready, and registers it to the environment.

mentions.sessionTitle: Multi-agents in action with 3 AI agents, 3 frameworks, tools & models
mentions.shortDescription: A platform-level egress gateway outside the sandbox can allow/deny destinations and inject secrets (such as an API key header) into outbound calls, so agent code never holds the secret.
mentions.longDescription: The sandbox includes an egress policy feature, with one type called transform, where a platform-level egress gateway that lives outside the sandbox has the final say on outbound calls. The code running in the sandbox has no access to secrets; instead, a secret (such as an Azure AI/OpenAI API key) is defined for the sandbox and the egress policy is configured to inject that key as a header on any outgoing calls to a particular endpoint. This means the agent-generated code never holds the API key, yet calls to external services still succeed because the gateway intercepts and modifies the request.

mentions.sessionTitle: Develop a conversational search experience without rebuilding your app
mentions.rawName: Elastic Agent Builder is now generally available
mentions.shortDescription: previously in technical preview, it can now be used for production workloads.
mentions.longDescription: Elastic Agent Builder, which powers agentic search using AI agents, was announced as generally available after being in technical preview for a while, meaning it can now be used for production workloads. The presenter introduces a demo using an e-commerce camping gear website for a company called Wayfinder, whose product descriptions and titles were created with generative AI and whose search is powered by Elastic. The demo showcases chat-based, hybrid, and lexical search capabilities.

mentions.sessionTitle: Develop a conversational search experience without rebuilding your app
mentions.rawName: Elastic is natively available on the Azure Marketplace
mentions.shortDescription: deployable through the Microsoft Marketplace without separate procurement or additional vendor relationships.
mentions.longDescription: Elastic is natively available on the Azure Marketplace, deployed, managed, and built through the Microsoft Marketplace, allowing customers to go from zero to a production-grade AI search deployment without leaving the Azure ecosystem, without a separate procurement motion, and without managing additional vendor relationships. When paired with models from the Microsoft Foundry model catalog, such as Azure OpenAI or other catalog models, Elastic provides grounded, relevant, and trustworthy AI answers powered by your own data rather than just the model's training data.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build agentic apps in minutes with Rayfin and Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: Beyond the browser, apps render inside the Fabric portal for internal/line-of-business scenarios
mentions.longDescription: Beyond running in the browser, a Rayfin application also offers an embedded view that can be rendered inside the Fabric portal, which is useful for internal/line-of-business applications. The embedded view exposes the properties and controls needed to manage the application, while the local development life cycle remains in VS Code. Because it runs in Fabric, it can talk to production data and uses Fabric single sign-on without manual database or auth setup.

mentions.sessionTitle: Design systems for every user, including people and LLMs
mentions.rawName: Embedded-text extraction outperforms OCR by roughly 200x
mentions.shortDescription: Extracting four pages with iText [inferred] leveraging embedded text took 0.075 seconds versus about 18 seconds for the Docling OCR pipeline *(00:07:41)*.
mentions.longDescription: Comparing extraction methods on a four-page PDF, the OCR-based Docling pipeline took about 18 seconds to process the pixels, while a basic Java implementation using iText to extract the embedded text and metadata took only 0.075 seconds — roughly 200 times faster. Both produced the same tables and content in the resulting Markdown, but the iText approach also correctly omitted the author's unintended watermark and preserved semantic structure like sublists. The takeaway was to design for understanding, not just rendering, especially with PDF documents.

mentions.sessionTitle: Discovering Power App Data with M365 Copilot using MCP
mentions.rawName: Enabling the MCP yields four standard CRUD tools
mentions.shortDescription: Turning on the Copilot MCP setting automatically provides create, read/review, edit/update, and query tools against the app's Dataverse data.
mentions.longDescription: In the preview Maker portal (previewmake.preview.powerapps.com [inferred]), developers go into their app settings, turn on Copilot control, and then enable the Copilot MCP via a yes/no setting. When turned on, the app's MCP automatically provides four basic CRUD tools—edit, create, review, and query—against the app's data. These standard tools appear in the MCP alongside any custom tools, and the same MCP is surfaced in Microsoft 365.

mentions.sessionTitle: Move from data to intelligence with Oracle MCP and Microsoft IQ
mentions.rawName: End-to-end identity propagation via Entra ID and OAuth 2
mentions.shortDescription: A user's Azure Entra ID identity is propagated into the Oracle database itself through an OBO token flow, so the database applies its own security rules to the agent's queries as if the user connected directly.
mentions.longDescription: After an agent is registered as an MCP client, an OAuth 2 workflow handles authentication: the user logs in, their Azure Entra ID credentials are verified, and they grant the agent permission to act on their behalf via an OBO (on-behalf-of) token, after which the agent obtains an access token without repeated logins. The user's Entra ID identity is then propagated into the Oracle database itself, so the database sees the user as themselves rather than the agent. This allows Oracle's own security rules to be applied to the agent's queries as if the user connected directly, provided the user's group membership grants access to the relevant resources.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build realtime multimodal agents with LiveKit and Azure
mentions.rawName: End-to-end voice agent built on Azure plus LiveKit
mentions.shortDescription: Azure can serve all three pipeline stages: Azure STT, OpenAI through Azure for the LLM, and Azure TTS.
mentions.longDescription: LiveKit is model agnostic and lets developers pick which STT, LLM, and TTS models to use in the voice pipeline, mixing and matching with one line of code to swap a model. Azure fits into all three stages: Azure STT for speech-to-text, OpenAI through Azure for the LLM, and Azure TTS for text-to-speech. The agent's SDK at the orchestration layer is where custom code, tools, MCP servers, and business logic connect media to the model.

mentions.sessionTitle: The AI-native Data Engineer
mentions.rawName: Enhanced Copilot Chat in Fabric notebooks
mentions.shortDescription: An upgraded conversational experience that helps users work directly in the Fabric portal.
mentions.longDescription: The newly enhanced Copilot Chat in Fabric notebooks helps users work directly in the Fabric web portal. It is presented as one of the conversational AI experiences suited for exploration, debugging, and ad hoc analysis, keeping the engineer close to the data while guiding the AI step by step.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.shortDescription: Procedural constructs including loops, multipath execution, and if/then/else branches.
mentions.longDescription: Scalar UDFs in Fabric Data Warehouse are evolving to support richer, more complex business logic by bringing procedural constructs into SQL workflows. These include loops, multipath execution, and complex if/then/else branches. They are built for analytical scenarios and optimized for scale, letting you write cleaner, reusable logic without compromising performance.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure DevOps meets GitHub, the path to AI powered SDLC
mentions.shortDescription: A public-preview, full-fidelity migration tool that moves Azure Repos to GitHub—including history, pull requests, and commits—with roughly 30 minutes of downtime and automatic reconnection of pipelines and boards
mentions.longDescription: The Enterprise Live Migrator is a public-preview tool for moving repos from Azure Repos to GitHub with full fidelity, bringing over the entire history, pull requests, and commits in a seamless cutover. Unlike the GitHub Enterprise Importer, which has caused four-to-five-day downtimes for very large repos, ELM does the migration with roughly 30 minutes of downtime. It also automatically connects up your pipelines and boards after the repo moves, removing those extra steps.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using autonomous SRE to move from alerts to action
mentions.shortDescription: Built-in reader/standard/administrator roles, per-agent user-assigned managed identity, "on behalf of" elevation, review versus autonomous run modes, command validation hooks, and KQL-queryable audit trails in Application Insights
mentions.longDescription: The Azure SRE Agent builds trust and control into every layer across permissions, governance, security, and monitoring. There are three built-in user roles—reader, standard user, and administrator—each scoped to the persona's needs, and every agent gets its own user-assigned managed identity (so no secrets or API keys to manage) with an "on behalf of" (OBO) flow to temporarily elevate without standing access. Governance is controlled through run modes: review mode proposes actions and waits for administrator approval, while autonomous mode executes directly for trusted recurring tasks. It also supports command validation hooks that inspect and validate every command or tool call before execution, with every action logged to Application Insights as a full audit trail queryable with KQL.

mentions.sessionTitle: Security for AI and Agent Augmented Coding on Windows
mentions.shortDescription: Distinct, provisioned agent identities (via Entra and Intune) for session-isolated agents, plus low-cost agent-identification tags for delegated process-isolation scenarios.
mentions.longDescription: To distinguish human from agent actions, Microsoft described two methods for identifying agents: a delegated path best suited to process-based isolation, where work done on a user's behalf still gets a low-cost agent identification tag that lets downstream systems like Entra apply agentic risk controls, and a unique agent identity for session-based isolation. Going beyond process-level to session-based isolation enables distinct agent identities with deep integration into the Entra Agent ID system, providing comprehensive authentication and authorization support for agentic actions. The example uses a modified version of the open-source OpenClaw agent, where session isolation fits better than process isolation, with the agent loop running under a separate agent user account visible in Windows Task Manager.

mentions.sessionTitle: Apply orchestration patterns for production AI agents
mentions.rawName: Evaluations for end-to-end processes in Flow
mentions.shortDescription: test-case-style evaluations applied to whole process orchestrations, not just individual agents.
mentions.longDescription: UiPath announced bringing evaluations to end-to-end processes in Flow. These can be thought of as test cases for entire process orchestrations, extending the concept of evaluations previously used with individual agents. The goal is to combine an enjoyable developer experience with the power of an enterprise platform.

mentions.sessionTitle: Real-Time Intelligence: Building event-driven AI apps and agents
mentions.shortDescription: Every Eventhouse endpoint exposes a remote MCP URL so agents can query live data, define rules in natural language, and use reusable skills via tools like GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code.
mentions.longDescription: With Real-Time Intelligence, Eventhouse MCP lets agents directly ask questions over live data and get instant insights, and MCP is also enabled for other items like Activator where rules and alerts can be defined in natural language. Fabric Skills give agents reusable capabilities and domain knowledge for interacting with Real-Time Intelligence items, connecting to tools like GitHub CLI and Claude Code. In the demo, Fabric Skills are installed and listed within GitHub Copilot CLI, including Eventhouse, Eventstream Authoring, and Consumption Skills, enabling agents to reason, act, and detect in real time.

mentions.sessionTitle: Foundry IQ: Fuel agents with enterprise knowledge and agentic retrieval
mentions.rawName: Every knowledge base is exposed as an MCP server out of the box
mentions.shortDescription: Created knowledge bases are immediately consumable via an MCP endpoint (`/MCP`) or API with no extra setup
mentions.longDescription: The speaker demonstrated that after creating a knowledge base in a Foundry IQ instance (here named "Demo 3"), it can be consumed via APIs or, out-of-the-box, as an MCP server with no extra setup required to stand up or run it. He connected the knowledge base to a GitHub Copilot session as an agent by adding a new MCP server, using an MCP proxy pointing to the Foundry IQ instance backed by Azure Search (search.windows.net), referencing knowledge bases and appending "/MCP" to the API entry point. Like all the APIs, the MCP endpoint is versioned with the API version shipped that day.

mentions.sessionTitle: Develop a conversational search experience without rebuilding your app
mentions.rawName: Every tool built in Agent Builder is exposed as an MCP tool and accessible via API
mentions.shortDescription: agents and tools can be called from any application with an API key.
mentions.longDescription: The presenter notes that any tool created in Elastic Agent Builder is officially an MCP tool, so with an API key it can be accessed from any other application you're building. This is demonstrated in the context of creating a 'Get Customer Profile' tool that wraps a workflow taking a User ID input, which is then assigned to a new 'Trip Planner Agent' configured with custom instructions to search the product catalog and generate trip plans.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build smarter AI systems in Foundry as models and costs evolve
mentions.shortDescription: Adding Nemotron [inferred] reasoning models, Cosmos for physical AI, and Earth-2 weather models
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft is expanding its partnership with NVIDIA, bringing additional models including Nemotron reasoning models [inferred], Cosmos for physical AI, and the new NVIDIA Earth-2 [inferred] AI weather models. These models enable developers and enterprises to build systems that sense, act, and respond to real-world conditions, extending beyond software workloads into physical AI. Together, the companies are enabling a unified platform spanning into physical AI.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale agentic AI cost‑efficiently on Azure with Arm Cobalt VMs
mentions.shortDescription: Beyond the D, DP, and ECDS series carried over from Cobalt 100, new memory-optimized VMs offer about 16 GB of memory per core, plus dense local-storage-optimized LCDS VMs aimed at agentic AI and cloud-native workloads
mentions.longDescription: Beyond the D, DP, and ECDS series carried over from Cobalt 100, Cobalt 200 extends the lineup with a memory-optimized version in which every core gets about 16 gigabytes of memory. It also adds dense local-storage-optimized LCDS VMs aimed at agentic AI and cloud-native workloads. Together these VM offerings are intended to fit any enterprise or cloud-native workload.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Build opening keynote
mentions.rawName: Expanded Windows ML and two new local models
mentions.shortDescription: Aion Instruct (an efficient reasoning SLM) and Aion Plan (a local agentic planning loop) run inbox on Windows across the full GPU install base, enabling onboard agents without cloud round trips.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft is expanding the scope of Windows ML and Windows AI so developers can build local onboard AI that runs across the full install base of GPUs without round-tripping to the cloud. Two new models will run inbox on Windows: Aion Instruct, an efficient reasoning SLM, and Aion Plan, a planning model that provides a full local agentic loop. With tool access, developers can build fully onboard agentic applications. The expansion builds on existing local AI uses like Outlook Summarize, PowerPoint alt text, and third-party apps such as Adobe After Effects and Premiere using Windows ML across NPUs and GPUs.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build smarter AI systems in Foundry as models and costs evolve
mentions.rawName: Explicit prompt caching / Azure context cache
mentions.shortDescription: A customer-owned cache for guaranteed performance and better privacy, in private preview today
mentions.longDescription: Explicit prompt caching is a new service in Foundry that evolves caching from a low-level optimization into a core system capability, delivering consistent and guaranteed performance and savings. Unlike implicit caching owned by the inference provider, the Azure context cache is owned by the customer—it is your data, with visibility into deployments and savings, providing better privacy controls and better operational availability across long-running tasks. It is available in private preview today.

mentions.sessionTitle: The AI-native Data Engineer
mentions.shortDescription: Lets Copilot read a Spark notebook, discover skills in built-in folders (E2E medallion architecture, eventhouse authoring), propose a phased plan, and execute selected cells.
mentions.longDescription: The Fabric-aware notebook agent mode, available through the new Fabric Data Engineering VS Code extension, lets Copilot read a Spark notebook reading from an event stream and propose an ingestion plan. Copilot interprets the notebook, scans built-in folders, and discovers available skills such as E2E medallion architecture and eventhouse authoring best practices. It then suggests a phased plan starting with a Phase 1 Bronze Layer that parses the JSON value column, adds tracking/metadata columns (ingestion timestamp and batch ID), writes to a Delta bronze table in append-only mode with checkpointing, and validates row counts.

mentions.sessionTitle: Data Science & Machine Learning with Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: Once published, a Fabric Data Agent is accessible as an MCP server endpoint and can be integrated with Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Studio, and Microsoft Foundry
mentions.longDescription: Once a Fabric data agent is created, it can be accessed as an MCP server endpoint. It can also be deployed on Microsoft 365 Copilot [inferred] and integrated with Microsoft Foundry as well as Copilot Studio. The Fabric data agent lets users execute natural-language queries against data in OneLake, converting them into corresponding SQL statements based on provided instructions and returning the information.

mentions.sessionTitle: Data Science & Machine Learning with Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: Fabric Data Agent for natural-language insights [00:14:49]
mentions.shortDescription: Any user can point a generative-AI-backed agent at OneLake data, add custom instructions, and receive insights; it is currently read-only
mentions.longDescription: The Fabric Data Agent lets anyone—not just data scientists or ML engineers—get insights from data, using generative AI behind the scenes. As long as the data is in OneLake, users can add it to the data agent, supply custom instructions, and receive insights. A current main limitation is that it is read-only: it can return insights from the data but cannot write back. Once ready, the agent can be consumed in Fabric, on the Foundry side, integrated with Copilot Studio, exposed as an MCP server, and deployed into Microsoft 365 Copilot [inferred].

mentions.sessionTitle: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: Fabric data agent publishing to Foundry and Microsoft 365 Copilot
mentions.shortDescription: Agents publish via workspace ID and data agent (artifact) ID, then connect as a tool in Foundry or appear directly in M365 Copilot
mentions.longDescription: A Fabric data agent queries the lakehouse (or now an ontology created from a semantic model with one click) using SQL-like queries and returns results. When you publish the data agent, you can use it in Foundry by supplying two things—the workspace ID and the data agent (artifact) ID—or you can surface it directly in Microsoft 365 Copilot, where it appears as a usable agent. In Copilot it starts a new session via the data agent MCP, retrieves the data, and can even visualize results, with the data agent coding against the matplotlib library to provide dataframes and information.

mentions.sessionTitle: Responsible AI in Action: From Principles to Real‑World Engineering
mentions.rawName: Fabric data agents publishable to Microsoft 365 Copilot
mentions.shortDescription: A data agent built on a Fabric ontology/lakehouse can be exposed to Copilot with a single click and queried in natural language alongside other agents
mentions.longDescription: The transcriptWindow only contains the speaker's introduction and framing of a Responsible AI demo, and does not describe this feature in detail. A data agent built on a Fabric ontology/lakehouse can be exposed to Microsoft 365 Copilot and queried in natural language.

mentions.sessionTitle: The AI-native Data Engineer
mentions.rawName: Fabric Data Engineering extension for VS Code with MCP support
mentions.shortDescription: Now enhanced with the Fabric notebook MCP server and tools that make the GitHub Copilot agent aware of Fabric context, including lakehouse targets.
mentions.longDescription: The Fabric Data Engineering extension in VS Code is now enhanced with MCP and tools that make the custom GitHub Copilot agent aware of Fabric context. It targets professional developers and data engineers who are most productive in an IDE with GitHub Copilot and source control. In the demo it is used with a Fabric-aware notebook agent mode to read an event stream from a Spark notebook leveraging Kafka, bridging Spark and real-time intelligence (RTI) in Fabric.

mentions.sessionTitle: Securing, scaling, and sustaining your data estate in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: OneLake catalog is natively integrated into Foundry knowledge so agent developers can discover trusted data, with Fabric governance and role-level security carrying over
mentions.longDescription: Fabric in Foundry lets AI developers bring together unstructured data (e.g. SharePoint documents, PDFs, Excel files) alongside structured data in a Fabric lakehouse using OneLake shortcuts that virtualize files into place with no copy or data movement, unifying multi-cloud sources like Amazon S3 and Azure Blob Storage. In Microsoft AI Foundry, developers use knowledge to index this context for grounding, and the OneLake catalog is natively integrated into Foundry knowledge. This lets developers search across available data, see what has been endorsed, and use signals like sensitivity labels to identify trusted, ready-to-use data, carrying Fabric governance and security over to agent building.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: Fabric IQ ontologies on top of semantic models
mentions.shortDescription: Introduced around Ignite, ontologies add nodes, properties, and named relationships so agents understand data context beyond raw one-to-many SQL table relations
mentions.longDescription: At Ignite, Microsoft introduced Fabric IQ, which adds ontologies alongside semantic models. Unlike raw SQL tables that only express one-to-many relations, ontologies provide nodes, properties, and named relationships so an agent or AI system can understand the actual meaning of the relationship between entities rather than just seeing 'one-to-N' cardinality. This mirrors how chat bots were built ten years ago using graphs and ontologies as a knowledge base, and aligns with Microsoft's medallion (bronze-to-silver-to-gold) data ingestion practice in Fabric.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering the next AI frontier with a unified data platform
mentions.shortDescription: New connections across Foundry, Copilot Studio, and Agent 365 [inferred], still in preview ahead of GA later this year.
mentions.longDescription: Building on the Fabric ontology announced a few months ago, Microsoft announced new integrations across Foundry, Copilot Studio, and Agent 365, expanding support for ontologies. Ontologies extend semantics beyond reporting analytics to explain to AI how the business works, including business processes, real-time feeds, policies, and actions, so the AI can participate in business processes. The capability is still in preview and becoming more capable as it moves toward GA coming later this year.

mentions.sessionTitle: Japan Wrap-up Session
mentions.rawName: Fairwater AI data center and Project Leyfin [inferred]
mentions.shortDescription: A dedicated AI data center built on sustainability principles, and a Fabric-powered service (public preview) for taking AI apps to production including backend. [00:41:00]
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft began construction of an AI-dedicated data center called Fairwater, built on sustainability principles such as not raising local electricity bills and circulating water to reduce consumption toward zero, and running Microsoft's in-house Maia and Cobalt chips. Separately, Project Leyfin [inferred] is a Fabric-powered service that helps take AI apps and mockups to production level—including the difficult backend work of authentication, operations, and governance—and was announced as a public preview.

mentions.sessionTitle: Deploy. Observe. Learn. Reinforcement learning for production agents
mentions.shortDescription: A skill, available in GitHub Copilot for Azure or as a standalone download, that lets users describe fine-tuning goals in natural language and runs an autopilot flow that picks models, graders, and hyperparameters
mentions.longDescription: A newly added fine-tuning skill lets users employ their favorite coding agent and natural language to describe what they want to do, and the skill figures it out for them. In the demo, the presenter gave it the address of a hosted agent and described the goal (e.g., create a grader that checks the agent calls the right tools, gives partial credit, and reports how well the model performs), without having to learn the API or SDK or click around the UI. The demo used Claude and Copilot CLI [inferred] and was run ahead of time.

mentions.sessionTitle: Move AI workflows from test to production on Microsoft Foundry
mentions.rawName: Fireworks AI as a first-party Azure/Foundry provider
mentions.shortDescription: Open-source models are accessible day-zero on Foundry with optimized, workload-aware inference served through the Fireworks stack
mentions.longDescription: Fireworks AI is presented as a high-performance open-source inference provider with a first-party Azure integration, offering day-zero support for major open-source models (from Kimi to GLM 5.1) on Microsoft Foundry. Built by a founding team from PyTorch at Meta and Vertex at GCP, it serves around 30 trillion tokens per day and 180,000 requests per second. The Fireworks serving stack uses workload-aware optimization—adaptive caching, quantization, its own inference engine (Fire retention [inferred, likely FireAttention]), and hardware selection—to tune for ultra-low latency or high throughput. Users can access it via Azure and also bring their own models or fine-tuned weights to Foundry for serving.

mentions.sessionTitle: Shipping custom models at scale from fine-tuning to inference
mentions.rawName: Fireworks AI is available on Microsoft Azure
mentions.shortDescription: Ferguson notes the managed inference and training service, highlighted in Build announcements, can now be used on Azure.
mentions.longDescription: Rob Ferguson, VP of Technology at Fireworks AI, introduces Fireworks as a managed service providing both AI inference performance and AI training. He notes the announcements made at Build and highlights that the service can now be used on Microsoft Azure.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build smarter AI systems in Foundry as models and costs evolve
mentions.shortDescription: GA partnership providing zero-day access to optimized frontier models with native Azure integration
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft announced the general availability of its partnership with Fireworks for deploying customized and open-source models in Foundry. It brings customers zero-day access to optimized frontier models, best-in-class inferencing performance, and native integration into Azure for an enterprise foundation. The key differentiation versus using Fireworks directly is that on Foundry it deeply integrates across the enterprise stack, using the same auth, API endpoints, and SDK.

mentions.sessionTitle: AI Building Blocks for .NET: Add intelligence to your C# apps
mentions.shortDescription: A maintained SDK integrates Model Context Protocol with Microsoft.Extensions.AI, demonstrated connecting to the Microsoft Learn MCP server for live documentation retrieval
mentions.longDescription: A first-class, maintained C# SDK integrates the Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Microsoft.Extensions.AI to connect external (and local/internal) tools to applications. MCP is described as a standard wire protocol originally created by Anthropic, and the SDK can connect to virtually any public MCP server. The demo connects a console chat client to the Microsoft Learn MCP server (located at learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp) to retrieve the latest published documentation, asking for the latest version of Microsoft Agent Framework and its URL.

mentions.sessionTitle: Inside Azure innovations with Mark Russinovich
mentions.shortDescription: Achieved with Intel using a migration TD enforcing policy across servers; not yet in production
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft worked with Intel to achieve confidential live migration, addressing a long-standing gap in confidential computing offerings. It uses a migration TD (MIG TD), a confidential partition measured as part of the VM's measurement, where the sending side enforces a policy that the VM will only migrate to another server with a MIG TD approved for that VM, extending the confidential trust boundary across two servers via confidential computing hardware. The demo, shown publicly for the first time ever, migrated a confidential VM with a few gigabytes of RAM between two servers using Hyper-V Manager, with TD info attestations printed during the transfer and the RDP connection dropping as the CVM moved. The capability was achieved in the last few weeks and is not yet in production.

mentions.sessionTitle: Inside Azure innovations with Mark Russinovich
mentions.rawName: First public demo of container live migration
mentions.shortDescription: Containers moved between server pools with no gap in output
mentions.longDescription: This was the first public demo of container live migration in Azure, moving containers from one pool of servers to another with minimal downtime, mirroring the live migration capability long available to virtual machines. In the demo, a container on server dev 6 emitted a tick every second up to tick 695, at which point migration kicked in and it stopped running on that server. The container reappeared on dev 1 already at tick 7055, and inspecting the output file with cat confirmed tick 695 was present, proving no gap in output occurred during the migration. The feature is still under development, shown via command line.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship safer code from your IDE with Aikido
mentions.shortDescription: AI-generated fixes that can be pushed directly into a file or rejected, with red lines marking problematic code and green lines marking the suggested replacement.
mentions.longDescription: Fix with Aikido AI provides AI-generated fixes for detected issues. When you click the fix button on the right-hand side, a new tab pops up offering a fix if one is available, which can be pushed straight into the file or rejected if you don't like the solution. In the diff view, red lines mark the bad lines and green lines mark the suggested good replacement.

mentions.sessionTitle: Discovering Power App Data with M365 Copilot using MCP
mentions.rawName: Fluent UI generation via Claude/GitHub Copilot skill
mentions.shortDescription: Microsoft provides a Power Platform skill for Claude and GitHub Copilot that turns a tool's JSON structure into a Fluent UI HTML file, with local preview against sample data.
mentions.longDescription: When a custom tool is tested, the Maker portal generates a JSON structure of the selected fields and table data. Microsoft provides a Power Platform skill for Claude and GitHub Copilot (used via the Power Platform plug-in in VS Code) that turns this JSON into a Fluent UI HTML file. The developer simply types 'generate MCP APP UI' in Claude, supplies a description and the JSON, and it produces the HTML; alternatively developers fluent in Fluent UI can hand-code their own. In the demo a robust timeline UI took about two to three minutes to generate.

mentions.sessionTitle: Stop routing docstrings to 70B models with on-device AI on Snapdragon
mentions.shortDescription: The underlying entropy, quantization, and routing research has not been published yet but is promised.
mentions.longDescription: The speaker explains how the routing approach extends beyond LLMs to generative AI with multiple tracks (e.g., audio, video, and sentiment analysis), where each track has its own entropy limits and classifier, and an orchestrator aggregates inputs and handles routing logic, execution monitoring, and output aggregation. He describes this as a work in progress and notes the underlying research paper has not yet been written or published, but promises to do so, telling the audience they are getting a preview of the paper.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unlock Claude in Microsoft Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Custom-code agents (built with the Claude Agent SDK, GitHub Copilot SDK, LangChain, or LangGraph) can be moved from a local machine into an automatically secured cloud sandbox in Foundry Agent Service.
mentions.longDescription: Foundry hosted agents are agents you build with custom code in any framework you want — including the GitHub Copilot SDK, LangChain, LangGraph, or the Claude Agent SDK — and run within Microsoft Foundry inside a hosted container sandbox. You start by building and testing the agent on your local machine, then move the application up into the cloud sandbox hosted in Foundry Agent Service. The sandbox is automatically secured and set up with the authentication needed to access Foundry resources, such as calling Claude models in Microsoft Foundry. It also facilitates the authentication needed to securely connect to tools and MCPs that host your enterprise data.

mentions.sessionTitle: Orchestrate special agents with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Hermes Agent on Nemotron 3 Super completes a real email-to-pull-request task and retains a learned skill across separate sessions and services
mentions.longDescription: This demo shows a Foundry hosted agent deployment running Hermes Agent powered by Nemotron 3 Super, with Nemotron Super and Nano models running on Foundry managed compute endpoints. The agent is granted access to external data—GitHub, Teams, and email—through Entra ID [inferred]. In the scenario, the presenter delegates a real feature-request task from a colleague's email about adding chat completions endpoint support to an internal benchmarking repo (LLM Perf Bench); because the hosted agent is connected to Outlook and GitHub through Foundry, it finds the relevant email, makes the code changes, and opens a pull request autonomously without the email being pasted into context.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: Foundry IQ as a permission-aware knowledge layer
mentions.shortDescription: A single identity/knowledge layer where queries are checked against permissions, labels, and policies before returning data
mentions.longDescription: Foundry IQ is described as a single identical (identity) knowledge layer that is part of Microsoft IQ alongside Work IQ and Fabric IQ. When a user queries knowledge through Foundry IQ, the request is checked against permissions, labels, and policies to determine whether that person is allowed to access the data. It governs access via context, permissions, and policies on top of the knowledge base.

mentions.sessionTitle: Japan Wrap-up Session
mentions.shortDescription: Serverless AI search in public preview, scaling to zero, with a developer tier
mentions.longDescription: Foundry IQ serverless was announced in public preview as a serverless AI search service. Whereas the previous AI search system required sizing capacity in advance, the serverless model can scale to zero, making it more user-friendly. It is currently available in a developer tier for trial use.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure Storage for AI workloads​
mentions.rawName: Foundry IQ with Blob as a first-class knowledge source
mentions.shortDescription: Microsoft's unified knowledge layer for agents can ground against an Azure Blob container directly, carrying storage security, lineage, and governance with no glue code.
mentions.longDescription: Foundry IQ is Microsoft's unified knowledge layer for agents, giving a single governed knowledge layer that any agent in Microsoft Foundry can ground against instead of every agent reinventing its own retrieval stack. Azure Blob Storage is a first-class knowledge source for Foundry IQ: just point it at a blob container and enterprise data becomes agent-accessible knowledge with the security, lineage, and governance of Azure Storage already in place and no glue code required. Foundry IQ also supports Azure AI Search indexes with Azure Blob or Azure Files data, closing the loop between the data plane in Azure Storage and the agent plane in Microsoft Foundry.

mentions.sessionTitle: AI solutions built to power industrial innovation and sovereign control
mentions.rawName: Foundry Local on Azure Local in public preview
mentions.shortDescription: Foundry Local now runs on Azure Local infrastructure for both connected and disconnected, single-node and multi-node scenarios across Azure Local form factors
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft announced in public preview Foundry Local running on Azure Local infrastructure, supporting both connected and disconnected scenarios across single-node and multi-node deployments and the different form factors of Azure Local. Models are cached locally and inference runs without any cloud dependency, while operations teams retain full control. Security and governance use the same identity layer as the cloud estate, with identity handled through Microsoft Entra ID and JWT validation, and inference endpoints secured with TLS and API key or token-based authentication. Azure Local is positioned as an AI-ready platform bringing Foundry capabilities to the enterprise edge with pre-validated hardware and Kubernetes-native operation.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build Apps w/ Local AI for Unmetered Intelligence on every Windows PC
mentions.shortDescription: Running common open-source models locally across CPU, GPU, and NPU, with new catalog additions including a Qwen 3.5 vision-language model and new speech models.
mentions.longDescription: Foundry Local, the local counterpart to Microsoft Foundry on Azure, enables developers to run common open-source models locally on CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, and is now generally available. It was demonstrated powering an inventory management application for a coffee shop, uploading an image of dropped-off product and identifying items in the back end. This used the Qwen 3.5 vision-language model [inferred], which is brand new to the Foundry Local catalog and classifies and describes everything in an image. The recommended way to get started is the GitHub repo, which has many samples.

mentions.sessionTitle: Post-Training and Deploying Open Source Reasoning Models in Foundry
mentions.rawName: Foundry now supports customizing agents with any open source framework and model
mentions.shortDescription: Beyond creating and deploying agents, Foundry enables fine-tuning open source models to reach a production-ready quality bar.
mentions.longDescription: Foundry now not only enables creating and deploying agents but also customizing those agents using any open source framework on any open source model to achieve the quality level needed to ship to production. The approach emphasizes defining evaluations upfront—described as test-driven development for the age of agents—so you can specify policies, expected tool-calling behavior, and a quality bar that remains consistent as you swap between frontier models like GPT 5.2 and smaller open source models. The demo shows a customer service retail agent operating against custom data, policy, and business domain using GPT 5.2 [inferred] alongside an open source model.

mentions.sessionTitle: Post-Training and Deploying Open Source Reasoning Models in Foundry
mentions.rawName: Foundry now supports customizing agents with any open source framework or model
mentions.shortDescription: Beyond creating and deploying agents, Foundry enables fine-tuning open source models to reach production-quality bars.
mentions.longDescription: Foundry now enables not only creating and deploying agents but also customizing them using any open source framework and any open source model to reach production-quality bars. The speaker frames evals as test-driven development for agents, defining quality bars upfront so teams can swap between frontier models (like GPT 5.2) and small open source models while verifying quality. The demo uses a customer service retail agent with four custom tools, comparing GPT 5.2 against an open source model (Qwen 3 14B [inferred]).

mentions.sessionTitle: Japan Wrap-up Session
mentions.shortDescription: New multi-turn Evaluation and continuous evaluation (public preview); Rubric Evaluator, Agent Optimizer, and ROI for Agents (private preview)
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft introduced new Foundry evaluation and observability capabilities, validated by NTT DATA during private preview. The new Evaluation capability extends existing functions to support multi-turn evaluations across full conversational exchanges, dataset creation from existing trace data, and continuous evaluation with sampling, released as public preview. In private preview, the Rubric Evaluator automatically generates custom evaluators from agent definitions, and an Agent Optimizer (plus ROI for Agents) builds on the rubric evaluator.

mentions.sessionTitle: From Test Kitchen to Table: A Demo-driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers
mentions.rawName: Foundry portal as a low-code agent test kitchen
mentions.shortDescription: The portal lets developers experiment with models, tools, and instructions for a single agent in a browser-based playground before writing any code
mentions.longDescription: The Microsoft Foundry portal is presented as a low-code 'test kitchen' where developers can experiment with models, tools, and instructions for a single agent in a browser-based playground before writing a single line of code. It offers built-in support for observability—including traces, evaluations, and monitoring—to accelerate inner/outer loop iteration and to deploy comparable versions in real time. Developers can then move seamlessly to code-first environments to build multi-agent solutions or more complex frameworks and workflows. The portal is structured to mimic the three main phases of the AI development journey, providing the relevant features and tools at each step.

mentions.sessionTitle: Safeguard data across you apps and agents development cycle
mentions.rawName: Foundry–Purview integration toggle with non-PII insights
mentions.shortDescription: Enabling the toggle in the Foundry control plane lets admins set up inline DLP and surfaces Foundry-specific, non-PII data security posture insights for a subscription.
mentions.longDescription: Within the Foundry control plane, a Purview integration toggle has been introduced; once enabled, Purview admins in the Purview portal can start setting up inline DLP policies for prompts. Enabling the toggle also surfaces Foundry-specific, high-level insights from Purview for that particular subscription, covering all the AI apps and agents built within it. This information is all non-PII, so Foundry admins—who may not be security admins—get a bird's eye view of the data security posture without seeing PII-related information, helping connect the loop between security and Foundry admins.

mentions.sessionTitle: Multi-agents in action with 3 AI agents, 3 frameworks, tools & models
mentions.rawName: Foundry registration and management for heterogeneous agents
mentions.shortDescription: Agents built on different frameworks can be registered, observed, and continuously evaluated in Microsoft Foundry as long as they share an agent-to-agent contract.
mentions.longDescription: In AI Foundry you can register agents built on different frameworks and technologies, as long as they talk agent-to-agent (A2A) or share some contract between them. Once registered, you can manage them, run continuous evaluations, and observe insights. This works alongside OpenTelemetry instrumentation that streams telemetry via an OTel collector into Application Insights, visible in both the Azure portal and Foundry.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and deploy an Azure app with your agent team
mentions.rawName: Foundry skill in the Foundry Toolkit VS Code extension
mentions.shortDescription: Supplies Copilot with up-to-date knowledge of the new Microsoft Agent Framework and Microsoft Foundry service so it can scaffold agents correctly.
mentions.longDescription: When prompted in VS Code Copilot to build a production-ready Foundry host agent using the Microsoft Agent Framework, Copilot pulled up the Foundry skill that ships with the Foundry Toolkit VS Code extension to get the latest knowledge about the service and framework. Because the Microsoft Agent Framework (an open-source framework for orchestrating multi-agent systems) and the Microsoft Foundry service are both very new, Copilot needs this skill to learn about the new technologies and understand how to build the agent. This enabled iterating with Copilot in plan mode to design a four-agent system (classifier, enrichment, triage, aggregate).

mentions.sessionTitle: From prototype to production: build and run agents at scale
mentions.shortDescription: A single managed, MCP-compatible endpoint for all agent tools with governance, guardrails, and a tool-search feature to optimize context usage
mentions.longDescription: Tool boxes in Foundry are becoming generally available soon. They provide one single managed endpoint for all the tools that make agents powerful, with the right governance and policy in place. Skills are now a first-class integration with tool boxes as well.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and deploy an Azure app with your agent team
mentions.rawName: Foundry toolbox with unified endpoint and authentication
mentions.shortDescription: Packages multiple tools (Azure AI Search over a product catalog and a Fabric IQ connector to customer/order data) behind a single endpoint, attached only to the enrichment agent.
mentions.longDescription: Foundry Tools and Toolbox lets you package various tools into a single entity that your program can interact with, solving how an agent running in the Microsoft Foundry service connects back to Fabric data. In this case the toolbox contains an Azure AI Search index over a product catalog and a Fabric IQ connector that links to customer and orders data, all accessible via a unified endpoint and unified authentication so you connect once. The toolbox is attached only to the enrichment agent, so that single agent can access internal data while the other agents cannot.

mentions.sessionTitle: From prototype to production: build and run agents at scale
mentions.rawName: Foundry Toolkit for VS Code (generally available)
mentions.shortDescription: A purpose-built developer experience for building Foundry agents without leaving the editor
mentions.longDescription: Foundry Toolkit for VS Code is now generally available. It provides a purpose-built developer experience for building Foundry agents without the developer ever having to leave the editor.

mentions.sessionTitle: From observability to ROI for AI agents on any framework
mentions.rawName: Foundry Toolkit with MCP server and skill
mentions.shortDescription: A VS Code extension providing code-first observability that bundles the Foundry MCP server and an opinionated Foundry skill to analyze evals and recommend client- or server-side fixes.
mentions.longDescription: The Foundry MCP server and the Foundry skill are packaged together under the Foundry Toolkit, an extension in VS Code, enabling code-first observability from the developer environment. The skill is an opinionated flow provided by Foundry creators that knows which part of the observability loop you are in and can recommend improvements, connecting both client-side and server-side layers. In the demo, Copilot chat inside VS Code was prompted to retrieve an eval result and explain why a low score (0.4) appeared and surface opportunities for improvement. Support for other coding agents and editors is planned in the future.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build collaborative agents into apps with APIs
mentions.shortDescription: The browser SDK connects over HTTPS and WebRTC through Azure Front Door, with core pods on Azure Kubernetes Service and rendering on dedicated Azure VM clusters, all on managed services.
mentions.longDescription: The Omniagent API is Azure Native: the browser-side SDK opens an HTTPS and WebRTC connection through Azure's Front Door and load balancing solutions, with private endpoint support in the network stack. Omniagent core pods run auto-scaled in Azure Kubernetes Service, the orchestration layer can talk to your own Azure OpenAI deployment or theirs, and the real-time multimodal rendering pipeline runs on dedicated Azure VM clusters streaming synchronized video back over WebRTC. Every component in the stack runs on an Azure managed service.

mentions.sessionTitle: Embracing frontier R&D with Microsoft Discovery
mentions.shortDescription: The enterprise platform, introduced in private preview at last year's Build, has moved to general availability
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft Discovery is an enterprise platform for what the speaker calls "frontier R&D," using agentic AI to let teams of AI agents execute the scientific discovery loop end to end while humans provide intent, direction, guardrails, and judgment. Introduced in private preview at last year's Build, it has now moved to general availability. The team shared Build demos including developing novel PFAS-free immersion coolants [inferred] and breaking down plastics using proteins for recycling.

mentions.sessionTitle: Fabric IQ: Bringing enterprise intelligence into the developer workflow
mentions.rawName: Geospatial map visualization generally available in Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: Map item for real-time and analytical geospatial needs
mentions.longDescription: Geospatial visualization in the map item directly within Fabric is generally available, ready for all geospatial needs across both real-time and analytical scenarios. It can be used alongside all of the other pieces across Fabric. This was the final item in a whirlwind tour of real-time intelligence capabilities.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio: Agents That Debug, Profile, and Test
mentions.shortDescription: Full worktree and git submodule support is shipping next week in Visual Studio.
mentions.longDescription: Worktree support is coming next week in Visual Studio, along with full support for git submodules. These were mentioned as nice additions shipping in the same timeframe.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Agentic Workflows: Automation That Actually Reads the Room
mentions.rawName: GitHub Agentic Workflows enters public preview
mentions.shortDescription: The capability ships in public preview the week after the session, with a companion website and ecosystem of existing workflow templates.
mentions.longDescription: GitHub Agentic Workflows is being released in public preview the week after the session, letting developers automate CI/CD, triage test failures, create issues, generate daily repo reports, and open pull requests. There is a companion website that is part of the offering, along with a deep ecosystem of existing agentic workflow types. The session also includes a GitHub Skills exercise attendees can run with their own GitHub handle to learn the capability firsthand.

mentions.sessionTitle: Rethinking CI: Actions, AI Agents, and the End of Commit-Fail-Commit
mentions.shortDescription: A GitHub CLI extension (`gh aw compile`) compiles Markdown agentic workflow files into a `.lock.yml` Actions YAML file.
mentions.longDescription: The GitHub AW (agentic workflows) extension is installed inside the GitHub CLI and is used to compile Markdown agentic workflow files placed in a repository. Running the `gh aw compile` command turns the Markdown file into an Actions YAML file, emitting warnings such as suggesting the workflow be restricted to the main branch. The output is saved as a `.lock.yml` file to differentiate it from non-agentic workflows, and you recompile and commit it whenever the Markdown file changes.

mentions.sessionTitle: Agent supervision is the new senior engineering skill
mentions.rawName: GitHub commit growth cited at 14,000x year-on-year
mentions.shortDescription: Attributed to a podcast conversation with the GitHub CEO; Claude Code attribution on GitHub is described as rising from ~4-5% in February toward a projected 50% by year end.
mentions.longDescription: Referencing a podcast he released with the GitHub CEO the day before, Swix cites a figure of roughly 14,000x year-on-year commit growth on GitHub. He also notes that Claude Code [inferred] attribution on GitHub rose to 4-5% as of February, is probably around 10% currently, and is on trend to reach 50% by end of year, with similar dynamics expected from Codex, Copilot, and other coding agents.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: A new surface focused on helping developers finish work (triage, CI, review, merge) rather than spawning ever more parallel sessions; available for download at github.com/app
mentions.longDescription: Mario Rodriguez introduces the GitHub app as one of GitHub's surfaces and describes it as foundational to the new agent-native engineering system. He frames its purpose around "lowering the floor and raising the ceiling"—making software development accessible to people GitHub could never reach before while enabling creation and community-building. The surface is positioned within a broader vision combining surfaces and data across the SDLC, with Evan Boyle set to demo it.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Build opening keynote
mentions.rawName: GitHub Copilot app and Rayfin SDK
mentions.shortDescription: A new app managing parallel agent sessions via git worktrees, with Rayfin providing an enterprise backend-as-a-service (partnered with Replit, hosted on Microsoft Fabric).
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft introduced a new GitHub Copilot app that combines the speed and flexibility of a CLI with the capability of an IDE and the ability to scale to an effectively infinite number of agent sessions, addressing the cognitive overload of managing many CLI sessions. Alongside it, Microsoft announced Rayfin [inferred], an agent-first SDK that connects agents to a backend-as-a-service, handling identities, storage, and database schemas. In partnership with Replit, developers can build apps in Replit while the app and data deploy into an enterprise-managed Fabric tenant via the Rayfin SDK. The Rayfin SDK is available now for use with other tools as a backend service.

mentions.sessionTitle: Japan Wrap-up Session
mentions.shortDescription: Expanded scenarios including mainframe migration, validated with partners Hitachi and NTT Data
mentions.longDescription: GitHub Copilot app modernization was presented as a feature extension (not a GA) aimed at changing how modernization progresses by helping development, infrastructure, and IT teams work on the same foundation. Demonstrated via a VS Code extension on a Java application, it runs an assessment in roughly 20 minutes that reports how to migrate to the cloud and what needs to change. The biggest change in the announcement is expanding supported scenarios to include mainframe migration, with the work validated alongside Japanese partners such as Hitachi and NTT Data.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: A newly launched surface positioned not as a session manager but as a tool to finish work, handling triage, CI, review feedback, merging, and deployment.
mentions.longDescription: The newly launched GitHub Copilot app is positioned not as just another session manager but as a tool built to help engineers finish work and deliver value to users. Rather than focusing on implementation or creating lots of parallel work, it handles the meta work around delivery: issue triage, getting through CI and keeping it green, responding to review feedback, merging, and getting changes deployed to customers. Evan Boyle, co-creator and engineering lead for the Cobalt CLI, Cobalt SDK, and the Copilot app, introduced it on stage.

mentions.sessionTitle: Japan Wrap-up Session
mentions.rawName: GitHub Copilot desktop app and Copilot SDK GA
mentions.shortDescription: Enterprise agentic development with a Canvas extension, daily automation running in the cloud, and SDK support for six languages (Java and another newly added). [00:29:00]
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft launched the Copilot SDK at GA, enabling enterprise agentic development where AI agent teams and humans collaborate toward a single outcome. In the Copilot desktop app, tasks can be assigned, looped, code-reviewed in a split pane, and automatically merged by agents. The SDK currently supports six languages, with Java and a final language newly added, and includes cross-platform and sandbox functions so agents can run on local machines, in the cloud, or in network-disconnected environments.

mentions.sessionTitle: Apply orchestration patterns for production AI agents
mentions.rawName: GitHub Copilot integration via NPM-installed UiPath skills and CLI
mentions.shortDescription: installing the skills gives Copilot full context on the platform's APIs, CLI commands, and deployment patterns so developers can build and deploy without leaving Visual Studio Code.
mentions.longDescription: Copilot can now unlock the capabilities of the UiPath platform. Developers install the UiPath skills and CLI using NPM, which gives Copilot full context about the platform's APIs, CLI commands, and deployment patterns. From that point, developers can build, deploy, and manage their agentic automations on UiPath using their preferred coding agent.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship fast, stay secure: from code to runtime
mentions.rawName: GitHub issue creation assigned to Copilot
mentions.shortDescription: From the attack path view, a GitHub issue is created, assigned to Copilot, and identifies that fixing one package resolves three additional CVEs.
mentions.longDescription: Through the GitHub Advanced Security integration with Defender for Cloud, a security team can create a GitHub issue directly from the attack path view to immediately route a vulnerability to the right developer and repository. The created issue is automatically assigned to Copilot, which identifies that fixing one package will also resolve three additional CVEs and pinpoints the exact place in the code that needs changing. In this case the fix is simply updating a package from version 0.21 to 1.13, though the issue could be buried in base images or more transitive packages. This lets security teams meet developers exactly where they work and avoid vulnerabilities getting lost in a backlog.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplifying .NET Installs with dotnetup
mentions.shortDescription: Running `dotnetup sdk install` reads a repo's global.json (including roll-forward policies like `latestFeature` and `latestPatch`) and installs the matching SDK automatically.
mentions.longDescription: Running `dotnetup sdk install` inside a repo reads that repo's global.json and installs the matching .NET SDK automatically.
