mentions.shortDescription: Starting next week in Visual Studio Insiders, Visual Studio moves onto the same Copilot CLI SDK shared with VS Code and the CLI, so features arrive at the same time across tools while still using Visual Studio's warm MSBuild and Roslyn for builds.
mentions.longDescription: Starting next week in Visual Studio Insiders, Visual Studio will move onto the GitHub Copilot CLI SDK, replacing its own implementation that talked to the Copilot API and back-end service directly. Because VS Code, the CLI, and Visual Studio will all share the exact same SDK base, features will arrive at the same time across the tools, even though each implements them differently. In Visual Studio's case, when the agent kicks off a build it still uses Visual Studio's already-warm MSBuild and Roslyn, making builds faster than running them on the command line.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unify your entire data estate on a single, AI-ready data lake
mentions.rawName: Mirroring support for Workspace Private Link (preview)
mentions.shortDescription: Routes mirrored database traffic through Microsoft's private network for Azure Cosmos DB, Azure SQL Managed Instance, and SQL Server 2025.
mentions.longDescription: Mirroring support for Workspace Private Link is coming to public preview today, addressing one of the top customer asks for mirrored databases. It brings private link network security to mirrored databases, routing all traffic through the Microsoft private network rather than the public internet. At launch it includes support for Azure Cosmos DB, Azure SQL Managed Instance (SQL MI), and SQL Server 2025, with more data sources coming.

mentions.sessionTitle: Local models, developer control, and the future of AI runtimes
mentions.shortDescription: A native Apple-device inference path (supporting NVFP4) offering faster performance than the previous engine when pulling MLX models from Ollama's registry.
mentions.longDescription: In response to a question about whether Ollama still uses llama.cpp under the hood and plans for its own engine, the speaker noted Ollama has its own MLX inference engine. For users on an Apple device, it is highly recommended because it offers faster performance. To use it, you just need to pull one of the MLX models from Ollama's model registry.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Agentic Workflows: Automation That Actually Reads the Room
mentions.shortDescription: Workflows can run on Copilot, Claude [inferred], Codex, or Gemini to diagnose test failures, open pull requests, and recommend stack updates.
mentions.longDescription: The agentic workflows are backed by agents and models, supporting Copilot, Claude [inferred], Codex [inferred] ("clawed codecs"), or Gemini—any of the models. These can dynamically diagnose test failures, open pull requests to make changes, update your stack, and give recommendations. There is already a deep ecosystem available for different types of agentic workflows.

mentions.sessionTitle: Move AI workflows from test to production on Microsoft Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Two models can be run side-by-side on identical input to weigh latency, quality, and token count before saving the winner as an agent
mentions.longDescription: The Foundry playground lets users chat with a deployed model to see how it performs for a specific use case, such as a code review agent catching SQL injections or hard-coded secrets. Through the compare models UI, two models can be run side-by-side on the same input so output is generated simultaneously across both—demonstrated by comparing a minimax model against a Kimi 2.6 model. Users can weigh latency, response quality, and the number of tokens generated, then pick the preferred model and click 'Save as agent' to persist it.

mentions.sessionTitle: From Test Kitchen to Table: A Demo-driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers
mentions.shortDescription: A catalog of 11,000+ models can be ranked on quality, safety, throughput, and cost, with a trade-off chart for choosing the best model for the job
mentions.longDescription: From the 'Discover' tab, developers can access a model catalog of 11,000+ models. The Microsoft Foundry leaderboard is a feature that runs benchmarks across catalog models and presents charts ranking them on criteria such as quality, safety, throughput, and benchmark costs. The demo used this to assess how the default GPT-4.1 model stacks up against others, motivating selection of a cheaper model for simpler tasks rather than an expensive feature-rich model for everything.

mentions.sessionTitle: From Test Kitchen to Table: A Demo-driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers
mentions.shortDescription: An intelligent router that automatically selects the appropriate backend model based on prompt complexity, routing simple queries to cheaper models and complex tasks to higher-performance ones
mentions.longDescription: Model Router is described as a distinct Azure Foundry model that acts as an intelligent router, so developers don't have to worry about which underlying model to use. It looks and feels like any other model: you send a prompt and it figures out the right backend model to route it to. In the demo it is deployed from the 'Discover' > 'Models' area, where deploying it opens the model playground and can be saved as a new agent (an 'auto routing agent').

mentions.sessionTitle: Build smarter AI systems in Foundry as models and costs evolve
mentions.shortDescription: The Foundry model router now supports 28 models (GPT-5.4, GPT-5.5 family, Claude Opus) with automatic failover, and as of today supports policy governance over which models it may select
mentions.longDescription: The Foundry model router automatically analyzes incoming prompts and routes each request to the best model, supporting 28 different models including GPT-5.4, the GPT-5.5 family, and Claude Opus models. It offers automatic failover to improve customer experience and agentic support. Starting today, it adds policy governance so customers can constrain which models the router is allowed to select; future investment will allow customizing and fine-tuning the router itself and bringing in fine-tuned models.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure DevOps meets GitHub, the path to AI powered SDLC
mentions.rawName: Model selection for the Copilot cloud agent
mentions.shortDescription: Rolling out the ability to pick the model used by the work-item-assigned coding agent, with the choice persisted ("sticky") per repository
mentions.longDescription: Building on the work-item integration with the Copilot cloud agent, users can now pick the model used by the agent. This is being rolled out as the speaker presents, letting teams choose which model works best since certain models perform better in certain repos depending on the agent, the instructions, and cost considerations. The selection is sticky, so once chosen it persists for subsequent runs.

mentions.sessionTitle: Understand and fix Agent Framework apps with observability and evals
mentions.rawName: Model swap raising effectiveness from ~50% to ~90%
mentions.shortDescription: Changing only the model from GPT-4.1 to GPT-5.4 [inferred] raised the same agent's eval pass rate to roughly 90% with no other code changes.
mentions.longDescription: Using the dataset and evals as a continuous testing loop, the speaker demonstrates model selection as a classic example of iteration. The exact same application and agent, with nothing changed except running against GPT-5.4 instead of GPT-4.1 [inferred], jumps to 90% effective. No application changes were made beyond swapping the model, and the eval-driven testing loop makes it possible to score the change and tell when things are working or broken.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using AI tools to teach old apps new tricks
mentions.rawName: Modernization Agent in the CLI is generally available
mentions.shortDescription: Orchestrates simultaneous assessments and migration plans across an entire app portfolio, with end-to-end automated Java and .NET framework upgrades
mentions.longDescription: The modernization agent, now generally available, is how you scale assessments and upgrades across your entire portfolio, operated from the CLI. It orchestrates multiple assessments and migration plans running simultaneously, then hands those plans off to developers who can execute and validate in their IDE. Java and .NET framework upgrades are now automated end-to-end straight from the agent CLI. It is part of GitHub Copilot modernization, built directly into GitHub Copilot.

mentions.sessionTitle: What we learned shipping VS Code weekly (without breaking everything)
mentions.rawName: Move from monthly to weekly stable releases (February)
mentions.shortDescription: Adopted to keep pace with the rapidly turning AI space and to land smaller, lower-risk batches rather than large monthly drops
mentions.longDescription: The VS Code team moved from monthly to weekly stable releases in February, driven by the rapidly turning AI space where features shipped to the daily Insiders build would be matched by competitors within two weeks while stable only updated once a month. Adopting AI increased their output (roughly 3X more issues and many more open pull requests since January), creating competitive pressure to release more frequently. Smaller weekly batches also reduce risk compared to landing large monthly drops, letting the team validate changes and avoid on-call incidents from big batches. The shift reflects a broader point that adopting AI requires teams to also change how they work and evolve their engineering systems.

mentions.sessionTitle: Agentic infrastructure needs agentic observability
mentions.rawName: "Move the LLM up; push the analysis down"
mentions.shortDescription: The model handles intent and investigation strategy while the backend does deterministic analytical work close to the data
mentions.longDescription: This is a new observability model where the LLM is moved up and the analysis is pushed down, meaning the model is not the execution engine. The LLM's job is to understand intent, decide investigation strategy, generate deterministic operations, and interpret results, while the backend does the actual analytical work close to the data, accurately and cheaply. The goal is to have the model orchestrate investigation over a deterministic analytical system with complete telemetry rather than brute forcing analysis itself.

mentions.sessionTitle: Inside Azure innovations with Mark Russinovich
mentions.shortDescription: A new Ethernet-based networking protocol co-developed with OpenAI that packet-sprays across independent "planes" to survive congestion and link failures during massive training jobs
mentions.longDescription: MRC (Multi-Path Reliable Connection) is a new Ethernet-based networking protocol developed with OpenAI and a growing consortium of partners, replacing RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet) in the Fairwater data centers that switched from InfiniBand to Ethernet. It is designed to be resilient during massive synchronous training jobs connecting up to 100,000 GPUs, where congestion or a single failure could otherwise force a costly restart from a checkpoint. MRC sprays packets across independent network domains called planes, so when a link is dropped the spraying rebalances across the remaining available planes. A demo showed two servers sending 4 GB payloads over 4 switches, achieving roughly 95 GB/s by spraying across 8 planes at about 12 GB per plane.

mentions.sessionTitle: .NET 11 in depth: Runtime, libraries, and SDK for the AI era
mentions.shortDescription: Threads, not just processes, will be supported by the time .NET 11 launches, reducing IPC and JIT-loading overheads; task authors can learn about adoption at the linked resource
mentions.longDescription: In .NET 11, MSBuild is embracing threads, not just processes. Today's MSBuild uses a multi-process architecture that is great for isolation and safety but has high overheads in inter-process communication costs and things like CoreCLR JIT loading. This multi-threaded mode has been in development for a while and is not ready to use today, but it will be ready by the time .NET 11 launches. Task authors can follow the linked resource to learn about the changes needed to adopt this ecosystem.

mentions.sessionTitle: Low-latency AI for developer workflows
mentions.shortDescription: A main agent can interpret a developer's daily goals and dispatch fast Spark sub-agents to read sources like Slack, Google Drive, and Google Meets.
mentions.longDescription: Codex Spark allows defining multi-agents, where a main agent is responsible for understanding the developer's daily goals. That main agent can kick off fast Spark sub-agents to read sources like Slack, Google Drive, and Google Meets, helping the developer understand what's happening within the company and their responsibilities.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: Slash commands (`/review`, `/security review`) orchestrate parallel sub-sessions using multiple models (Gemini, GPT, Claude Sonnet 4.6), built with GitHub Advanced Security.
mentions.longDescription: The Copilot app acts as an orchestrator that can compose review workflows together using slash commands: `/review` for code review and `/security review` for security. These can run as parallel sub-sessions using multiple models — Gemini, GPT, and Claude Sonnet 4.6 — which, because they have different training distributions and don't always agree, yield the best possible results. In the demo, the presenter asked the agent to use the create session tool to run one session doing a multi-model code review with Gemini, GPT-5 [inferred, heard as 'GPT 55'], and Sonnet 4.6, and a second session running a multi-model security review, then to rubber duck the combined output critically and optionally post comments to the pull request.

mentions.sessionTitle: AI solutions built to power industrial innovation and sovereign control
mentions.shortDescription: Building on the February single-node ONNX catalog, customers can now run the Foundry Local model catalog and inferencing across multi-node deployments
mentions.longDescription: Building on the February announcement of the Foundry Local model catalog on single-node deployment (suited for customers with ONNX inferencing needs where a single node is sufficient), Microsoft announced that customers who need to scale can now run the Foundry Local model catalog and inferencing capabilities across multi-node deployments. This runs on an Arc-enabled Kubernetes environment across the different form factors of Azure Local, from single-node to multi-node deployment.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build collaborative agents into apps with APIs
mentions.shortDescription: Swapping LLM providers is a configuration change rather than a rewrite, using the same agent configuration.
mentions.longDescription: Omniagent provides multi-provider support, letting you bring whichever LLM you've already deployed. Swapping providers is a key change rather than a rewrite, using the same agent configuration either way. The speaker cites Siemens as a key deployment where field service technicians interact with manufacturing systems through voice and video, with the same architecture running customer service, sales onboarding, and corporate training.

mentions.sessionTitle: Orchestrate special agents with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Knowledge from multiple task-specialized teacher models is distilled into Nemotron 3 Ultra to consolidate capabilities
mentions.longDescription: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation is a training technique highlighted as a breakthrough in Nemotron 3 Ultra, building on prior progress from supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. It uses multiple large teacher models, each trained on specific tasks, and distills their knowledge down into Nemotron 3 Ultra. NVIDIA spent significant time ensuring the Ultra model learns well across all the teachers and gains those combined capabilities and skills.

mentions.sessionTitle: Move AI workflows from test to production on Microsoft Foundry
mentions.rawName: Multi-tenant serverless and dedicated deployment tiers
mentions.shortDescription: Data Zone Standard offers a shared serverless endpoint for testing, while Global/Data Zone Provisioned Throughput provides single-tenant deployments sized via a PTU calculator
mentions.longDescription: Foundry offers different deployment types for Fireworks models. Data Zone Standard is a multi-tenant serverless endpoint shared across multiple users, where token-per-minute rate limits can be set per account, suited for testing and running evals rather than massive production workloads. Once benchmarks and evaluations look good, users can move to a more dedicated single-tenant deployment via Global Provisioned Throughput or Data Zone Provisioned Throughput. These provisioned options include a PTU calculator that estimates how many provisioned throughput units are needed based on input/output token counts and requests per minute.

mentions.sessionTitle: From observability to ROI for AI agents on any framework
mentions.shortDescription: Extends evaluation from single-turn to entire sessions, accounting for factors like session duration, not just final success.
mentions.longDescription: Multi-turn evaluation is a new public preview capability within Foundry that extends evaluation beyond single turns to span an entire session. This is powerful because an agent might succeed at the end of a session, but if a session that should take 5 minutes instead takes 20 minutes, that is not a successful session. Multi-turn evaluation accounts for such session-level factors rather than only final success.

mentions.sessionTitle: .NET 11 in depth: Runtime, libraries, and SDK for the AI era
mentions.rawName: Native AOT journey for the .NET CLI
mentions.shortDescription: Bundled tools (user-secrets, dev-certs, user-jwts) are native AOT as of Preview 6, with `dotnet user-secrets` averaging ~54ms (only ~14ms application code); the entire CLI is on track for AOT
mentions.longDescription: The team is starting a journey to make the dotnet CLI a Native AOT application. As of two weeks before the talk, several standalone but bundled tools in the CLI—User Secrets, dev certs, and JSON Web token services—are Native AOT, available starting in Preview 6. The net result is improved performance, and over time more commands (such as solution management, template-related, and tool management commands) will move into the native space.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build persistent and scalable AI agent memory with TiDB
mentions.shortDescription: TiDB connects directly to an Azure OpenAI deployment for embedding generation
mentions.longDescription: TiDB offers a native Azure OpenAI integration so users can easily connect their Azure deployment for embedding generation. This is presented alongside getting-started resources, including spinning up a free TiDB starter cluster at TiDB.com that is ready within 30 seconds with no credit card.

mentions.sessionTitle: Post-Training and Deploying Open Source Reasoning Models in Foundry
mentions.rawName: Native integration with Ray dashboards and a rollout browser
mentions.shortDescription: Fine-tuning jobs integrate with Ray clusters managed in Foundry through an AAD-authenticated endpoint, allowing monitoring of CPU/GPU nodes, jobs, and RFT rollouts.
mentions.longDescription: When a fine-tuning job is kicked off, Foundry provides native integration with Ray dashboards along with a rollout browser. With a Ray cluster managed in Foundry, users can bring custom code, run GRPO, and bring their own model, managing the entire Ray cluster through an AAD-authenticated endpoint that exposes CPU nodes, GPU nodes, and lets you monitor the job and rollouts. The RFT trajectories view shows each sample going through tool calls, where specific tool calls are rewarded or penalized so you can watch reinforcement fine-tuning in action.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scalable Applications Without Polyglot tax: Azure SQL Hyperscale
mentions.rawName: Native JSON type and path-specific JSON indexes
mentions.shortDescription: SQL stores JSON as a pre-parsed binary (ANSI JSON type, no longer NVARCHAR(MAX)), cutting JSON storage by 30–50% and allowing indexing of a specific JSON path rather than the whole document.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft SQL recently introduced a native JSON type and JSON indexes, replacing the earlier NVARCHAR(MAX) approach. The native JSON type is ANSI-compliant and stored as a pre-parsed binary, which makes JSON storage 30 to 50% smaller. Unlike other relational databases that index the entire JSON document, Microsoft SQL lets you index a particular path of the JSON (e.g. only the device attribute), and the JSON index will pick that path. JSON also retains schema flexibility for documents with varying attributes.

mentions.sessionTitle: Post-Training and Deploying Open Source Reasoning Models in Foundry
mentions.rawName: Native Ray dashboard integration and a rollout browser
mentions.shortDescription: Foundry offers an AAD-authenticated endpoint to manage an entire Ray cluster (CPU and GPU nodes), monitor jobs, and inspect RFT trajectories and rollouts.
mentions.longDescription: When kicking off a job, Foundry provides native integration with Ray dashboards and a rollout browser. Through an AAD-authenticated endpoint, users can manage an entire Ray cluster—including CPU nodes, GPU nodes, and everything in between—bring custom code and models, run GRPO, and monitor jobs and rollouts. The trajectories view in RFT lets users watch reinforcement fine-tuning in action, inspecting every sample's tool calls and how each call is rewarded toward the reward target.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scalable Applications Without Polyglot tax: Azure SQL Hyperscale
mentions.rawName: Native vector type with DiskANN and HNSW indexes
mentions.shortDescription: Vectors moved from varbinary to a native type, with vector indexes built on Microsoft Research's DiskANN, including recently introduced updatable DiskANN indexes.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft SQL recently started supporting vectors, initially on top of varbinary before switching to a native vector type. The vector type was released first without an index, and later vector indexes were added using DiskANN, which came out of Microsoft Research and is described as pretty fast, along with HNSW. This positions SQL to handle vector workloads without needing a separate specialized vector database.

mentions.sessionTitle: Orchestrate special agents with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Foundry
mentions.rawName: Nemotron 3 Ultra, NVIDIA's largest and most capable open model
mentions.shortDescription: Announced Sunday with 550 billion total / 55 billion active parameters, targeting frontier reasoning and orchestration; general availability stated for Tuesday
mentions.longDescription: Nemotron 3 Ultra is NVIDIA's largest and most capable open model to date, announced Sunday with broader detail shared in the session and general availability stated for Tuesday. It targets frontier reasoning and orchestration capabilities with 550 billion total parameters and 55 billion active parameters. It is positioned at the top of three Nemotron sizes (nano, super, ultra) and is expected to run on roughly two B200-class data center GPUs. NVIDIA emphasizes fast task completion, quick prefill and turn handling for agentic tasks, lower costs, strong performance across ecosystem agentic harnesses, and a fully open release including datasets and research.

mentions.sessionTitle: Accelerating developer productivity with Windows 365
mentions.rawName: New 32-core SKU with up to 128 GB RAM
mentions.shortDescription: Expands the diversity of Cloud PC compute options for memory-intensive local AI workloads.
mentions.longDescription: Windows 365 offers a diversity of Cloud PC SKUs, including a new 32-core SKU supporting up to 128 GB RAM [inferred] (stated in the transcript as "128-gigabit RAM"). This expanded compute is aimed at running AI models directly on the developer-controlled Cloud PC environment, where available RAM and CPU can be used flexibly without incurring additional token-based costs. In the demo, the presenter uses VS Code and Microsoft Foundry's model catalog to filter and run a small Qwen model locally on CPU, noting that the number of models that can run is limited only by available free RAM.

mentions.sessionTitle: Real-Time Intelligence: Building event-driven AI apps and agents
mentions.shortDescription: Includes a new MQTT version, an Oracle DB Change Data connector, HTTP/REST endpoint ingestion, and a MirrorDB Change Feed connector, with roughly 40 connectors total.
mentions.longDescription: Eventstream's connector catalog spans dozens of connectors and keeps growing, with several newly launched options highlighted. These include a new MQTT version, an Oracle DB Change Data Connector, an HTTP connector for pulling data automatically from REST endpoints, and a MirrorDB Change Feed Connector for getting change data feeds from databases, Delta Tables, and mirror databases. Additional connectors are on deck and will be available soon.

mentions.sessionTitle: Latest Cobalt VMs and Azure Boost enhancements​
mentions.shortDescription: A high-memory MP series (16 GB/vCPU, up to 1.3 TB) and a dense local-storage LP series (up to 23 TB NVMe local storage) join the refreshed DP, DPL, and EP families.
mentions.longDescription: Cobalt 200 introduces entirely new VM types built in response to customer requests, alongside refreshed existing families. The new high-memory MP series sets a ratio of 16 GB of memory per vCPU, scaling up to 84 vCPUs and 1.3 TB of memory in a single VM, targeting large in-memory databases, caches, big analytics, relational databases, and ERP. A new dense local-storage LP series offers 8 GB memory per vCPU, up to 128 vCPUs, 1 TB of memory, and up to 23 TB of NVMe local storage for data preprocessing, storage caching, databases, big data analytics, and search/index engines.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building WinUI Apps with C# First Patterns and AI Assisted Workflows
mentions.rawName: New DataGrid and Charting controls coming to core WinUI
mentions.shortDescription: These data-oriented controls are due relatively soon and will ship in the core WinUI bits.
mentions.longDescription: The team is adding a lot of new controls, including DataGrid and Charting, which are up and coming and should be out relatively shortly. These will ship in the core WinUI bits and will enable a lot more data-oriented scenarios.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering the next AI frontier with a unified data platform
mentions.shortDescription: Public preview for Dremio and Azure Database for MySQL, with Azure Monitor and AWS Glue coming soon to bring observability data alongside business data.
mentions.longDescription: OneLake adds public preview support for Dremio and Azure Database for MySQL, with Azure Monitor and AWS Glue coming soon. These new sources allow the whole observability data estate to be brought into OneLake to join with the business data estate, continuing the effort to add more data sources with zero ETL.

mentions.sessionTitle: Foundry IQ: Fuel agents with enterprise knowledge and agentic retrieval
mentions.shortDescription: A newly trained ranker continues the team's multi-year ranking work, contributing to improved relevance
mentions.longDescription: The speaker explained that improvements over prior iterations came from a mix of factors, including a newly trained semantic mode and semantic ranker. The team has been training rankers for a while and continues to push the boundary on ranking quality. Additional gains came from updating the retrieval workflow to fit current models, improving answer synthesis, and model-specific prompt tuning for tasks like MCP parameter binding. The science team behind this publishes detailed write-ups for those interested in information retrieval and evaluation methodology.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unify your entire data estate on a single, AI-ready data lake
mentions.shortDescription: DreamView [inferred], Azure Monitor in public preview, with AWS support coming soon; recently added SharePoint and OneDrive shortcut/mirroring.
mentions.longDescription: Many new data sources for shortcut and mirroring are entering public preview, including support for DreamView [inferred], Azure Monitor, and soon AWS [inferred] support. This builds on recently added shortcut and mirroring for SharePoint and OneDrive, and existing generally available sources like the SQL family (SQL Server 2025, on-premises SQL Server), Snowflake, Oracle Database, and SAP Datasphere. Shortcuts connect data wherever it lives with no data movement, while mirroring brings the entire data catalog into OneLake using change data capture.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.shortDescription: Fuzzy string matching (Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler), new concatenation operations, UNISTR, DATE_BUCKET, and the ANY_VALUE aggregate.
mentions.longDescription: T-SQL in the Fabric Warehouse continues to evolve with recent updates that expand its expressiveness and analytical power. These include fuzzy string-matching capabilities based on Levenshtein and Jaro-Winkler algorithms, new string concatenation operations, and additional functions like UNISTR and DATE_BUCKET. New aggregates such as ANY_VALUE are also added.

mentions.sessionTitle: From zero to teammate in 25 minutes: Build a Teams agent live
mentions.shortDescription: A command-line tool built from the ground up for both humans and coding agents, handling app registration, bot creation, secrets, and gluing the pieces together via `teams app create`.
mentions.longDescription: The Teams CLI has been built from the ground up for both humans and agents. For humans it is interactable—you can type something like `teams app` and use arrow keys to select actions such as create app, get app details, update app, download the package, manage secrets, and manage permissions. Behind the scenes the create command performs multiple steps including creating an Entra application, creating a bot, creating secrets, and gluing all of those pieces together to produce an installation link.

mentions.sessionTitle: Latest Cobalt VMs and Azure Boost enhancements​
mentions.shortDescription: Generally available with the first VMs (Intel-based V7), delivering up to 400 Gbps networking bandwidth and 1 million remote-storage IOPS.
mentions.longDescription: Niko Pamboukas introduces the latest generation of Azure Boost, Azure's server offload technology, which has recently become generally available with the first VMs using it—the Intel-based V7 VMs. Azure Boost is a Microsoft-designed system that offloads virtualization tasks traditionally handled by the hypervisor and host OS onto specialized hardware and software, improving performance, host isolation, servicing, networking, and storage access. Relative to Build 2025, the next generation delivers dramatic increases in storage throughput and IOPS, plus a deep-dive feature, Guest RDMA, for direct memory-to-memory transfers between VMs.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.shortDescription: Per-compute billing with a one-minute minimum then per-second granularity.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft is evolving its billing model to more closely match how real data warehouse workloads behave by moving to a node-based billing model where you're billed on the actual compute used to run queries. Billing starts with a one-minute minimum and then moves to per-second granularity, so the larger and more stable your workloads, the more that initial minute is monetized. Combined with compute efficiency improvements, this results in more predictable and efficient usage for long-running analytical queries, and serves as a foundation for further engine efficiencies over time.

mentions.sessionTitle: Your PC, Your Rules: AI Agents Meet Windows Personalization
mentions.shortDescription: A watcher monitors Windows toast events and flashes the keyboard red on incoming messages, resuming with no state loss to support focus mode.
mentions.longDescription: A notification watcher that monitors Windows toast events and flashes the keyboard red whenever a message arrives, so a user in deep focus mode without sound won't miss notifications. It resumes with no state loss, allowing the user to see an incoming message, respond, and return to focusing without missing a beat. The user enables it by simply telling the agent to flash the keyboard red whenever a message is received.

mentions.sessionTitle: Design systems for every user, including people and LLMs
mentions.shortDescription: The OCR pipeline pulled a watermark into the Markdown output, which the author never intended to expose and which could be abused to jailbreak an LLM *(00:08:20)*.
mentions.longDescription: When running Docling to convert a PDF to Markdown via OCR, the output captured a watermark that the author never intended to be extracted. Because OCR processes the rendered pixels, such unintended content ends up in the Markdown file and could be used or abused to jailbreak an LLM if used as training data. By contrast, extracting embedded text and metadata avoids pulling in this unintended content, which is better for security.

mentions.sessionTitle: Design systems for every user, including people and LLMs
mentions.shortDescription: OCR failed to recognize sublists, while the embedded-metadata approach reconstructed them correctly, and such errors compound over time into wrong output.
mentions.longDescription: The OCR pipeline (Docling) failed to recognize that certain items were sublists because the semantic meaning was lost when processing rendered pixels, whereas using the embedded document metadata reconstructed the sublist correctly. These OCR mistakes are hard to trace and can compound over time, producing very wrong output formats. The recommendation is to enable embedding of metadata when producing PDFs and ensure tags correctly convey the author's intent, which yields smart data extraction, easy search, and accessibility for free.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build the thing that builds the thing
mentions.shortDescription: Routes read-only, non-mutating calls through a GitHub App (raising the rate limit from 5,000 to 15,000 requests/hour) via Cloudflare, reserving the personal token for mutating actions.
mentions.longDescription: Octopus is a GitHub token proxy the speaker built after repeatedly running out of API tokens while agents searched for related issues. An individual gets 5,000 API requests per hour, but a GitHub App gets 15,000, so Octopus intercepts `gh` calls and routes non-mutating, read-only actions on public repositories through a Cloudflare worker that uses the GitHub App's token instead of his personal one. Only mutating actions or calls that don't match fall back to his personal token, effectively raising his rate limit.

mentions.sessionTitle: Local models, developer control, and the future of AI runtimes
mentions.shortDescription: An optional service introduced this year that runs frontier-grade open models on data-center hardware with zero data retention and no training on user data, for users lacking local compute.
mentions.longDescription: Ollama Cloud was added starting this year to augment local inference, allowing users to run frontier models on data-center-grade hardware when they lack sufficient local compute. Data is never trained on and the service has zero data retention. It enables use cases such as parallel agents to accomplish difficult work not possible with smaller models, with models offering the maximum context window from the providers themselves. It is a completely optional service usable with Ollama.

mentions.sessionTitle: Local models, developer control, and the future of AI runtimes
mentions.shortDescription: A command that injects open models directly into existing tools such as Claude Code [inferred], VS Code, and GitHub Copilot, with one-line setup for agent harnesses.
mentions.longDescription: Ollama Launch is a recently introduced command that integrates open models directly with a developer's favorite tools. By using the command, open models can be injected directly into harnesses such as Claude Code [inferred], VS Code, and GitHub Copilot. It builds on Ollama's core proposition of being the easiest way for developers to access and run open models in one command.

mentions.sessionTitle: Develop faster on Windows with AI playbooks and local agents
mentions.shortDescription: A demo showing Lemonade pulling together collections of models and intelligently routing queries to image generation, speech, or text models based on query context.
mentions.longDescription: A live playbook demonstrates Omni-modal routing in Lemonade, where the choice of model depends on the use case—routing application inference one way, or routing an image-generation request to a specialized image generation model. Lemonade itself is described as an embeddable DLL that provides the "tracks and switches" to build applications, while the UI shown is an open-source sandbox demo built by the community. The community continually adds features (Mac support was added a couple months prior, NVIDIA support the previous week), governed through a bi-weekly maintainers meeting.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build collaborative agents into apps with APIs
mentions.rawName: Omniagent API runs at one cent per render minute
mentions.shortDescription: When bringing your own LLM, pricing is roughly 20 times cheaper than alternatives, making a five-minute call cost five cents and an eight-hour agent under $5 per day.
mentions.longDescription: The Omniagent API runs at only one cent per render minute when you bring your own LLM, which is roughly 20 times cheaper than the alternatives. At that rate, a five-minute customer call costs five cents and a full-time agent running eight hours a day costs less than $5. According to the speaker, this cost shift makes real-time multimodal video agents a production tool rather than a proof of concept.

mentions.sessionTitle: Claw and agent harness in Microsoft Foundry
mentions.rawName: One-click publish to Teams and M365 Copilot
mentions.shortDescription: From the Foundry portal, deployed agents can be scoped to the creator or submitted to the Microsoft Admin Center for organization-wide approval, yielding both Teams and Copilot UIs out of the box
mentions.longDescription: Foundry offers a one-click publish to Teams and M365 Copilot so deployed agents can appear in the surfaces people use every day rather than as a standalone UI. From the portal, a publish drop-down lets the creator fill out a few key details—name and the actions the agent can perform, which is what end users see—and then make the agent instantly available scoped just to themselves or share it with the entire organization. The speaker demonstrates clicking the "Publish to Teams and M365 Copilot" button on a simple prompt agent and walks through the resulting dialog.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build agentic apps in minutes with Rayfin and Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: Deploying provisions a managed database, static content hosting, and a Fabric single sign-on auth service without custom configuration
mentions.longDescription: Running the deploy command (shown as "rayfin up" [inferred]) presents the available options and provisions the backend automatically. At the back end it deploys a database, static content hosting, and an auth service, where auth is Fabric single sign-on. These services are baked in without the developer having to do any custom configuration or setup.

mentions.sessionTitle: Securing, scaling, and sustaining your data estate in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: OneLake catalog integrated into 100+ surfaces, public APIs, and MCP
mentions.shortDescription: Governance and security travel into Excel, Teams, Copilot Studio, and tools like Visual Studio Code via MCP
mentions.longDescription: The OneLake catalog is integrated into more than 100 places across Microsoft Fabric and Office, including Microsoft Teams, Excel, and Microsoft Copilot Studio, so users find and analyze data from the tools they already use while governance—access permissions, DLP rules, and OneLake security—travels with the data. The same catalog is also accessible through public APIs and MCP; for example, in Visual Studio Code an LLM-powered app can ask in natural language what sales-related lakehouses Zava has and get results from the same trusted catalog with the same governance and security. Whether a person searches in Excel or an AI agent queries through an API, the same governed truth is discoverable and usable everywhere.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unify your entire data estate on a single, AI-ready data lake
mentions.rawName: OneLake catalog natively integrated into Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Trusted enterprise data, including sensitivity labels and endorsements, is discoverable and usable directly in Foundry knowledge and agents.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft is bringing the OneLake catalog natively integrated into Foundry, letting users discover all of their trusted enterprise data in one place and immediately use it inside knowledge, agents, and any AI workloads. It contains the full capabilities of the OneLake catalog for discoverability, including sensitivity labels and endorsements, creating a consistent view of data across the entire estate of analytics and AI by making it available across both Fabric and Foundry. This data is made available without copying through a common data foundation, and can unify structured and unstructured data from sources like SharePoint and Amazon S3.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unify your entire data estate on a single, AI-ready data lake
mentions.rawName: OneLake File Explorer and OneLake MCP (GA)
mentions.shortDescription: Both are now generally available.
mentions.longDescription: In a recap of recent storage improvements, Josh Caplan announces that the OneLake File Explorer is now generally available along with the OneLake MCP. The OneLake File Explorer application lets users see everything in a workspace across all item types as folders and files in a single consistent view within Windows File Explorer.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unify your entire data estate on a single, AI-ready data lake
mentions.rawName: OneLake Table API metadata write support
mentions.shortDescription: Beyond reading metadata (already GA), users can now write metadata, create tables and schemas, and publish transactions via the Table API.
mentions.longDescription: The OneLake Table API exposes the same open-source APIs for both Delta Lake and Iceberg natively, so any application like Snowflake or Databricks that works with at least one of those formats can read all data in OneLake regardless of how it was written. While reading metadata through the Table APIs has been generally available, Microsoft now announces the ability to write metadata, create tables, create schemas, and update or publish transactions through the Table API, available today.

mentions.sessionTitle: From observability to ROI for AI agents on any framework
mentions.rawName: Open ecosystem support for tracing and evals
mentions.shortDescription: Foundry can trace and evaluate both Foundry and non-Foundry agents built with frameworks including LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI SDK [inferred], and Microsoft Agent Framework.
mentions.longDescription: Foundry provides open ecosystem support so you can trace and run evaluations not only on Foundry agents but also on non-Foundry agents built with any framework. This includes the most popular agent frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI SDK [inferred], and Microsoft Agent Framework, giving complete visibility into the full agent execution workflow and eval signals produced directly from the traces. Combined with Foundry's partnership with Azure Monitor, this delivers full-stack observability across apps, agents, and AI platform components, with data read back into Foundry for centralized observability.

mentions.sessionTitle: Your PC, Your Rules: AI Agents Meet Windows Personalization
mentions.shortDescription: A skill defined by a `skill.md` contract at a repo root declares available tools and parameters so any agent can interpret intent and call the tooling without an SDK or API service.
mentions.longDescription: An open-source Copilot skill that streamlines Windows personalization with agents, implemented as a repo with a skill.md at its root that acts as the contract with the agent. The markdown declares what tools are available, what commands to run, and what parameters they accept, so the agent reads it, reasons about the user's intent, and calls the tooling with no SDK to integrate and no API service to design. Skill commands map to real Windows APIs, letting an agent pick wallpaper, accent color, and taskbar color from a single natural-language request.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building WinUI Apps with C# First Patterns and AI Assisted Workflows
mentions.shortDescription: The team is moving to work primarily and almost exclusively in public repos, landing pull requests publicly so the community can see and contribute to the work; Phase 3 (running tests in public) is already complete.
mentions.longDescription: Chris Anderson outlined WinUI's open-source journey, noting Phase 3 (running tests in public, so anyone can grab the bits, compile WinUI, and run tests) is already complete. The big next phase, Phase 4, moves the team from internal source repos to working primarily and almost exclusively in public repos, landing all pull requests on the public side. This is aimed at reaching a place where Microsoft can accept changes from the community, engage with it, and let the community see the work instantly.

mentions.sessionTitle: Local models, developer control, and the future of AI runtimes
mentions.shortDescription: Compatibility plus Python and JavaScript SDKs for developers building applications on open models.
mentions.longDescription: For developers building applications on top of open models, Ollama provides OpenAI and Anthropic API compatibility. Developers with Python or JavaScript applications also have an SDK to build on top of. Ollama has been built for agents from the beginning, with specific testing for tool calling, structured outputs, and one-line agent setup.

mentions.sessionTitle: Agent supervision is the new senior engineering skill
mentions.rawName: OpenAI is merging Codex into ChatGPT
mentions.shortDescription: Presented as evidence that coding-world workflows are bleeding into general knowledge work.
mentions.longDescription: Swix cites as a 'fun fact' that the OpenAI team announced the day before that they are merging Codex into ChatGPT. He presents this as evidence that what happened to coding last year is now bleeding into general knowledge work, with developers getting to preview that future first.

mentions.sessionTitle: Understand and fix Agent Framework apps with observability and evals
mentions.rawName: OpenInference as the observability standard for agents
mentions.shortDescription: An open-standard extension to OpenTelemetry aligned with AI semantic conventions, noted as the standard used for Microsoft's new assert framework and agent control specification described in Sarah Bird's prior session.
mentions.longDescription: OpenInference is described as an open-standard extension for OpenTelemetry that works with the semantic conventions for AI, effectively making AI work with OpenTelemetry. It has been around for a few years and is used for gathering telemetry data from LLMs, while a separate GenAI standard remains in committee. The speaker notes that, per Sarah Bird's session the previous day, OpenInference is the standard being used for Microsoft's new assert framework and agent control specification. Adding this telemetry requires only a couple of lines of code to trace and send data to a backend.

mentions.sessionTitle: Secure agent workflows in GitHub Copilot with NVIDIA OpenShell
mentions.shortDescription: A project begun roughly eight months ago on 20% time, with roadmap, architecture, and code published on its GitHub repository
mentions.longDescription: OpenShell is an open-source, agent-native software stack that Alex and Ali started at NVIDIA on roughly 20% time about eight months ago. Its core thesis is that an agent world needs a different, stateful, long-running environment built for machine speed, rather than reusing existing stacks designed for human-paced work. The central goal is a trusted, secure-by-design runtime that gives people the confidence to run agents, models, and harnesses inside it, including the ability to approve large numbers of agent actions without depending on constant human input.

mentions.sessionTitle: Profile and optimize agentic AI on Windows
mentions.rawName: OpenVINO runtime fully instrumented for tracing
mentions.shortDescription: The OpenVINO runtime is fully instrumented with ITT markers, with additional layers such as Windows ML being added on top
mentions.longDescription: The OpenVINO runtime is fully instrumented with ITT tracing, and additional layers such as Windows ML are being added on top. Unified telemetry combines the software-side ITT tracing information with driver telemetry into a single, time-synchronized output, currently in JSON, with this being the first preview starting this week. Platform telemetry provides metrics such as memory reads/writes to DRAM, IP-block-to-IP-block bandwidth, power, and utilization, allowing AI model execution to be correlated with these metrics for optimization. Over time the output may gain a database—such as a columnar or vector database—to make queries more efficient.

mentions.sessionTitle: Data Science & Machine Learning with Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: An operational agent (distinct from the data agent) is available in preview to monitor real-time data and recommend business actions
mentions.longDescription: In addition to the data agent, there is another agent called the operational agent, which is under preview. It can be used to monitor real-time data and recommend business actions. In the demo the speaker instead proceeds with the sales data agent for generating insights from sales data tables.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scalable Applications Without Polyglot tax: Azure SQL Hyperscale
mentions.shortDescription: Relational context (e.g. locating "person Bob") narrows the vector search space, reducing cost versus a standalone vector database.
mentions.longDescription: Specialized vector databases that lack operational data context end up searching a large number of rows and vectors, which is costly. By using relational context—for example locating a specific person such as Bob in relational data and then selecting transactions similar to that—the search space is narrowed, acting as a pre-filter that reduces cost and is faster. Microsoft SQL also recently introduced updatable DiskANN indexes, further reducing the need for a separate vector database.

mentions.sessionTitle: Real-Time Intelligence: Building event-driven AI apps and agents
mentions.shortDescription: An autonomous virtual team member that observes, analyzes, decides, and acts 24/7, publishing into Microsoft Teams with recommended actions and root-cause analysis.
mentions.longDescription: The Operations Agent is now generally available, taking the observe, analyze, decide, and act stages and running that loop autonomously. It acts like a new virtual team member on the operations team that can reason, understand, and act to help the organization move at the speed of the business. It was presented as the point where the broader Real-Time Intelligence capabilities, including the Anomaly Detector, come together.

mentions.sessionTitle: Fabric IQ: Bringing enterprise intelligence into the developer workflow
mentions.rawName: Operations Agent generally available in Fabric IQ
mentions.shortDescription: An agent that monitors anomaly events, Eventhouse data, and the ontology in real time, then recommends and takes governed actions, operating within a team channel
mentions.longDescription: The Operations Agent in Fabric IQ is generally available, demonstrated as part of showing how AI works with ontologies. It is grounded on the real business context represented in the ontology and powered by real-time intelligence, integrating with Microsoft Foundry, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and out-of-the-box Fabric agents. The demo shows pairing it with an anomaly detector over Eventhouse data that uses data science to recommend the best model and emit anomaly events automatically as data streams in.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering the next AI frontier with a unified data platform
mentions.shortDescription: Autonomous virtual team members that monitor signals and act in the background, with new chat-based authoring, root cause analysis, and Microsoft Teams integration.
mentions.longDescription: Operations agents are now generally available. Unlike chatbots that answer questions, these are virtual team members that monitor signals and react autonomously in the background, constantly looking at what's going on and taking actions. They are configured entirely through natural language with no coding required, and new capabilities at GA include chat-based authoring, root cause analysis, and Microsoft Teams integration. A demo showed setting up an agent to monitor customer churn 24/7.

mentions.sessionTitle: Expand local AI reach with Windows ML
mentions.rawName: ORT Gen AI library performance updates
mentions.shortDescription: The Windows ML ORT Gen AI library received updates leading to faster local LLM inferencing on Windows.
mentions.longDescription: The Windows ML ORT Gen AI library has received a number of performance updates, leading to faster local LLM inferencing on Windows.

mentions.sessionTitle: Secure agent workflows in GitHub Copilot with NVIDIA OpenShell
mentions.shortDescription: Announced (per a Microsoft announcement "yesterday") as embedded in Windows native WSL, Azure, and GitHub, and available via Canonical on Ubuntu, Red Hat OpenShift, and Docker
mentions.longDescription: OpenShell is being taken to market through an ecosystem of partners, and per a Microsoft announcement the prior day it is embedded into Windows native WSL, Azure, and GitHub. It is also available via Canonical on Ubuntu, Red Hat on OpenShift, and Docker. Partners including SAP, Workday, and ServiceNow are running their agents inside OpenShell for trust, with the goal of embedding it as a trust layer that everyone can build on top of.

mentions.sessionTitle: Designing Reliable Multi‑Agent Apps with Azure Cosmos DB
mentions.shortDescription: Enables single-writer active-active failover at the partition level for five-nines availability with zero downtime, data loss, and touch
mentions.longDescription: Per-partition automatic failover is now generally available. It allows failover at the individual partition level rather than waiting for an entire region to become unavailable, letting the system react in a more agile way (a brownout versus a blackout). Healthy regions or partitions continue reading and writing from the primary write region while any partition experiencing issues fails over seamlessly, giving the active-active pattern with five-nines of availability without multiple writers. This delivers zero downtime, zero data loss, and zero touch because the SDK does the heavy lifting.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building WinUI Apps with C# First Patterns and AI Assisted Workflows
mentions.rawName: Performance and quality investments shipped to the public Git repo
mentions.shortDescription: Improved memory usage and a switch to a system compositor are available to try today, with WinApp SDK experimental preview branches incorporating the changes shortly.
mentions.longDescription: Chris Anderson described core investments in performance, fundamentals, and quality, including heavily improved memory usage and a switch to a system compositor that should yield better performance improvements. These changes have already hit the public Git repo and are available to play with today, with WinApp SDK versions incorporating them coming shortly through the experimental preview branches.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplify app dev with cloud-native PostgreSQL in Azure HorizonDB
mentions.shortDescription: HorizonDB claims 3x higher transaction throughput, 3x faster vector search, and support for up to 15 read-only replicas.
mentions.longDescription: HorizonDB claims 3 times higher throughput on transactions and three times faster vector search compared to standard Postgres. It can also scale to very large databases and enables up to 15 read-only replicas, providing a scalable and powerful engine. On top of this engine, AI features are built in.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplify app dev with cloud-native PostgreSQL in Azure HorizonDB
mentions.shortDescription: A new extension bringing Lucene-type full-text search to Postgres, combined with a DiskANN vector index to enable hybrid search.
mentions.longDescription: PGFTS is a new extension enabled on HorizonDB that brings Lucene-type full-text search functionality to Postgres, allowing full-text search and full-text search indexes on a product catalog. Combined with a provisioned DiskANN vector index—which offers better performance than pgvector—it enables fast hybrid search that combines the strengths of both vector and full-text search. A simple function is provided to perform these sophisticated hybrid search operations with minimal syntax.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build Apps w/ Local AI for Unmetered Intelligence on every Windows PC
mentions.shortDescription: The small language model now runs on GPU and already powers production features such as Outlook's summarize capability.
mentions.longDescription: Phi Silica, Microsoft's small language model, is newly running on the GPU. In the demo it was used to take unstructured order text sitting in a barista queue and extract the relevant information, structuring its output as JSON via a new API for structuring Phi Silica output. The task manager showed a GPU spike confirming the model ran locally on the GPU, returning the drink, size, modifiers, and quantities. The AI APIs use a similar calling pattern: checking the model ready state with a get ready state function, calling ensure ready async to install if needed, initializing with create async, and then generating a response.

mentions.sessionTitle: Fabric IQ: Bringing enterprise intelligence into the developer workflow
mentions.shortDescription: Real-time dashboards using OpenUSD scenes integrated with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for bidirectional 3D operational visualization
mentions.longDescription: Through a strategic partnership with NVIDIA, a physical AI solution is in preview that connects streams of data and embeds them in a real-time dashboard using OpenUSD scenes integrated with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries. This creates a 3D visualization showing in real time how systems operate, with bidirectional cross-highlight capabilities for a unified operational picture. It combines Fabric real-time intelligence to collect signals, Fabric IQ and the ontology studio for contextualized visuals, and NVIDIA Omniverse for 3D visualization and physical simulation, enabling operations across both digital and physical worlds.

mentions.sessionTitle: Create enterprise AI apps at scale with Bolt and Microsoft
mentions.shortDescription: An agent mode that previews what will be implemented before building, intended to save time and tokens.
mentions.longDescription: After selecting a model (Opus 4.7 [inferred, "modal" is a mishearing of "model"]), the user puts the request into plan mode and builds. Plan mode is a way to see what the agent wants to implement before it actually does so, often saving time and tokens. In the demo the Bolt Agent generates a plan to set up a database with authentication and a plan-a-trip modal; because it asks no clarifying questions, the user proceeds to implement.

mentions.sessionTitle: Fabric IQ: Bringing enterprise intelligence into the developer workflow
mentions.shortDescription: Announced at FABCON; enables what-if scenarios over trusted data for business and finance teams
mentions.longDescription: Planning in Fabric IQ, announced at FABCON, allows you to plan, understand, and run what-if scenarios over the same trusted data. This makes it powerful for enabling business and finance teams. It was presented as part of an overview of Fabric IQ capabilities alongside the graph analytics multi-hop analysis.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering the next AI frontier with a unified data platform
mentions.shortDescription: An end-to-end enterprise planning workload for budgets, forecasts, and scenarios, rolling out to remaining regions over the coming weeks.
mentions.longDescription: Planning in Fabric, a workload announced about three months ago in preview, is now generally available and will roll out to the rest of the regions over the next couple of weeks. It is an end-to-end enterprise planning tool that allows teams to manage budgets, forecasts, scenarios, and targets, serving as the source of truth for what should happen in the future. It is fully integrated with Fabric across the experience, security model, and OneLake configuration, with write-back to Fabric SQL databases.

mentions.sessionTitle: Secure agent workflows in GitHub Copilot with NVIDIA OpenShell
mentions.rawName: Policy Prover for formally verified policy
mentions.shortDescription: Policies written in OPA/Rego (or YAML) are translated into formal logic so an SMT-style solver can mathematically prove what an agent can still do, catching exfiltration paths a reviewing agent or human could be fooled into missing
mentions.longDescription: The Policy Prover is a unique OpenShell offering that not only enforces policies but can answer the question of what an agent can still do once a policy is applied. Policies written in standard languages like OPA and Rego (or YAML) are described in formal logic, drawing on technology that originally came from Microsoft, so that formal verification and SMT-style solvers can reason about them. In OpenShell's architecture the agent itself runs inside a sandbox where every input and output is enforced, allowing one policy language to work across any agent and catching exfiltration paths that a reviewing human or agent could miss.

mentions.sessionTitle: Discovering Power App Data with M365 Copilot using MCP
mentions.rawName: Power Apps MCP is in public preview
mentions.shortDescription: Available now through the preview Maker portal so developers can expose app data to M365 Copilot.
mentions.longDescription: The Power Apps MCP is currently in public preview, allowing developers to expose their Power App data for agentic and Microsoft 365 Copilot discovery. The session explains Power Platform as a suite of tools that enables business subject matter experts and pro developers to build mission-critical applications, automate and standardize processes, analyze app-captured data, and create AI-driven solutions over connected data without deep technical skills. Attendees are pointed to links to set up their own Power Apps and make data exposable in M365.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship safer code from your IDE with Aikido
mentions.shortDescription: Checks for any secrets before a commit is made.
mentions.longDescription: The Aikido plugin includes a pre-commit hook as one of its extra features. It checks whether there are any secrets present before you commit your code.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale agentic AI cost‑efficiently on Azure with Arm Cobalt VMs
mentions.shortDescription: Cobalt 200 is currently previewed in eight regions, with expansion planned at general availability
mentions.longDescription: Cobalt 200 is currently in preview in eight regions, with plans to expand to more regions at general availability (GA). The speaker highlighted that Cobalt 200 is well suited to agentic AI and cloud-native scenarios such as sandbox creation, request loops, and fitting many sandbox agents into a single VM. The session then transitioned to a demo presented by Pranay.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale enterprise .NET apps with AI‑assisted cross‑platform workflows
mentions.shortDescription: Build and validate UI components in isolation across responsive breakpoints, data context states, and themes.
mentions.longDescription: As part of Uno Platform 3.0's key building blocks, previews let developers build, preview, and validate UI components in isolation across responsive boundaries, data context states, and themes. They complement the specialized agent with skills and MCP tools, plus snippets and hot design/hot reload, where changes made anywhere across the console or GUI are reflected immediately.

mentions.sessionTitle: Secure agent workflows in GitHub Copilot with NVIDIA OpenShell
mentions.shortDescription: Inspects queries for PII and routes them to a local model, out to a frontier model, or rewrites them using differentially private techniques (low-epsilon DP) to preserve utility while keeping PII local
mentions.longDescription: The Privacy Router extends OpenShell's isolation beyond system, file, network, and memory to isolation around agentic behavior, borrowing heavily from the synthetic-data work Alex and Ali did at their company Gretel and from work Microsoft itself did. When an agent submits a query, the router inspects it for PII: if PII is present it routes the query to a local model for inference, and if there is no PII it lets the query route out to a frontier model for multi-turn orchestration, tasking, and reasoning. A third scenario combines the first two approaches to preserve utility while keeping PII local.

mentions.sessionTitle: From prototype to production: build and run agents at scale
mentions.shortDescription: Lets agents learn a playbook across sessions rather than relearning each conversation
mentions.longDescription: Procedural memory in Foundry Agent Service is now in public preview. It empowers the agent to learn the playbook across all sessions, so the agent doesn't have to start learning from scratch in every conversation. There is no manual rewrite of prompts or skills; the agent becomes smarter, safer, and cheaper the more it runs, all with the developer in control for every change.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build AI-powered collaboration on a visual canvas
mentions.shortDescription: A new conversational agent that ingests text, files, or voice-to-text, asks clarifying questions, and builds a first-draft flowchart with swim lanes.
mentions.longDescription: Lucid's brand new process agent, available from the AI jumping-off point under "Build A Process," offers a more conversational experience than traditional Lucid AI. Users describe their process by pasting text such as a standard operating procedure, adding files, or using voice-to-text to capture a rough-draft prompt, and the AI fills in the gaps. The process agent works through the supplied information, may ask clarifying questions about forgotten details, and helps generate a well-thought-out flowchart along with a summary of what it has done.

mentions.sessionTitle: Security for AI and Agent Augmented Coding on Windows
mentions.rawName: Process-level sandboxing in GitHub Copilot CLI
mentions.shortDescription: An experimental "sandbox enabled" mode runs each tool execution inside a kernel-enforced boundary, keeping the developer inner loop fast.
mentions.longDescription: Process isolation sits at the lighter-weight end of the containment spectrum and is a strong fit for coding agents and focused tool-execution scenarios where speed matters, keeping the developer inner loop fast while Windows applies platform-level boundaries to the riskiest operations such as running model-generated code. The demo shows GitHub Copilot CLI with an experimental feature enabled where Maya types "sandbox enabled" so every tool execution Copilot runs is contained in a sandbox. She asks Copilot to make a birthday card from cat photos; a blue dot next to "sandbox shell" indicates the PowerShell code is executing inside a kernel-enforced sandbox boundary that can only access what was explicitly granted.

mentions.sessionTitle: Supercharged profiling: Finding performance bugs with agents
mentions.shortDescription: A dedicated agent invoked via `@Profiler` that knows how to write benchmarks, run the profiler, and analyze traces directly within Visual Studio.
mentions.longDescription: A dedicated profiler agent can be invoked from Copilot chat in Visual Studio by typing @Profiler, giving access to an agent that knows about benchmarking, how to run the profiler, and how to write benchmarks. In the demo the presenter asks it to write a benchmark for writing a CSV file, and Copilot reads the existing benchmark in the project on its own (without being told) so it can write similar code. It recognizes there is no existing benchmark covering CSV writing, then proceeds to create one and prompts to install the required benchmark packages.

mentions.sessionTitle: Supercharged profiling: Finding performance bugs with agents
mentions.shortDescription: The agent uses profiling data rather than plain text search to identify which source lines consume the most time and steer its investigation.
mentions.longDescription: Rather than just grepping through the source base, the agent uses the profiler's "go to source" functionality and the profiling data to determine exactly which lines take the most time, then uses that to guide its investigation. After analyzing a trace, it identified hotspots such as expression compile, should-quote, and a dynamic multicast delegate; the presenter steered it to optimize the should-quote logic instead of the top item. The agent read the relevant source guided by profiling data, suggested combining the character checks into a single pass to avoid multiple iterations, and then recognized it needed to rerun the benchmark to measure the improvement.

mentions.sessionTitle: So you want to become an MVP?
mentions.shortDescription: The MVP program has run for over 30 years and now spans more than 4,000 award recipients across 96 countries and nearly 50 languages.
mentions.longDescription: The Microsoft MVP (Most Valuable Professional) program has been around for over 30 years and spans the globe. Today it includes more than 4,000 influencers covering 96 countries and a little over 49, almost 50, languages. The program looks for growing communities in every part of the world and invites locals to potentially become the next recipient.

mentions.sessionTitle: From zero to teammate in 25 minutes: Build a Teams agent live
mentions.shortDescription: Subcommands are revealed incrementally so an agent only loads context relevant to its current goal.
mentions.longDescription: When designing the Teams CLI for agents, the team employed progressive disclosure. Using the help command (e.g. `teams h`) reveals top-level commands such as `teams app` and `teams project`, and rather than exposing all subcommands at once, the CLI surfaces commands progressively based on the agent's goal—for example `teams app h` then `teams app update h` to reach the full list of flags. This ensures the agent only fills its context with information relevant to its current goal rather than unneeded details.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build the thing that builds the thing
mentions.shortDescription: Asks contributors' agents to attach a privacy-filtered transcript to PRs, giving maintainers a signal of effort invested.
mentions.longDescription: This is a skill for the project ("open claw" [inferred]) that solves the problem of not knowing how much effort went into a PR, since a one-line prompt can generate pages of content. Earlier contributor guidelines asking people to send their prompts failed because there was no good system, so now when a contributor's agent sends a pull request it offers to attach a privacy-filtered version of the prompt in exchange for a faster review. If the user agrees, the agent finds its own transcript on disk, cuts it to the interesting parts, and adds it to the PR, giving the maintainer a much better signal of effort invested.

mentions.sessionTitle: Modern resiliency from build to recovery through Agentic AI
mentions.rawName: Public preview of Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager
mentions.shortDescription: Lets customers manage zonal resiliency through application-level goals, Advisor-powered recommendations, resiliency drills, and recovery plans
mentions.longDescription: Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager entered public preview, allowing customers to manage zonal resiliency at an application level rather than per individual resource, using service groups. It introduces goals for setting resiliency targets, recommendations powered by Advisor, resiliency drills to simulate failures (powered by Chaos Studio), and recovery plans to orchestrate failover. The experience can be managed through Azure Portal, PowerShell CLI, and Azure Copilot, with intelligent guidance brought into developer workflows including GitHub Copilot.

mentions.sessionTitle: From prototype to production: build and run agents at scale
mentions.rawName: Publish to Microsoft 365 Teams and Copilot (GA soon); Autopilot agents (public preview)
mentions.shortDescription: Agents inherit identity, policy, and permissions, and Autopilot agents gain their own IDs, email addresses, and Teams presence, governed in Agent 365
mentions.longDescription: Publishing to Microsoft 365 Teams and Copilot is generally available soon, allowing developers to publish all their Foundry agents directly into Teams and Copilot where teams already work, with identity, policy, and permissions flowing through automatically. In addition, developers can now publish Foundry agents as Autopilot agents into Teams, now in public preview. These Autopilot agents can take on their own IDs, email addresses, and even Teams presence so they can initiate conversations or follow up on action items, all governed end to end in Agent 365.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship fast, stay secure: from code to runtime
mentions.rawName: Pull request annotations with contextual fixes
mentions.shortDescription: Findings such as XPath injection surface in the PR with a plain-language explanation and a Copilot-suggested parameterized fix.
mentions.longDescription: When code hits a pull request, the same finding the CLI caught locally surfaces directly in the PR with a plain-language explanation rather than just a red flag. For an XPath injection [inferred], Defender explains that the header value is injected directly into the XPath query, letting an attacker alter the predicate and disclose data they shouldn't see. Right below the finding, Copilot suggests a fix to parameterize the query and pass the input as a bound variable, and even prompts the developer to verify the fix works. This closes the developer security loop: the CLI catches it, the pipeline gates it, and the PR annotates it with enough context to fix in minutes.

mentions.sessionTitle: Safeguard data across you apps and agents development cycle
mentions.rawName: Purview SDK integrated into the Microsoft Agent Framework SDK
mentions.shortDescription: Developers can embed Purview compliance and data protection middleware directly into a custom agent's runtime with roughly 15-20 lines of code.
mentions.longDescription: The Purview SDK is now directly integrated into the Microsoft Agent Framework SDK, allowing developers to embed Purview compliance and data protection controls right into their agent runtime so the same enterprise-grade governance that protects Copilots extends to any custom agent. For pro developers building custom AI with Agent Framework SDK—whether with Langchain, OpenAI, Semantic Kernel, or any other framework—a Purview policy middleware can be added to the agent's workflow pipeline to intercept prompts and responses and enforce tenant security policies configured in Purview. Microsoft provides samples on GitHub in C#, Python, and Node.js, and the integration takes roughly 15 to 20 lines of code at max.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build persistent and scalable AI agent memory with TiDB
mentions.shortDescription: Installable via `pip install pytidb`, providing hybrid search and RRF in a few lines
mentions.longDescription: TiDB offers a Python SDK for Python developers, installable via "pip install pytidb". It provides hybrid search and RRF in three lines of code.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build agentic apps in minutes with Rayfin and Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: Provides a TypeScript SDK for defining data models, roles, and permissions in code, plus a CLI that streamlines local development and deployment to Fabric
mentions.longDescription: Rayfin [inferred] provides a code-first SDK that makes it easier to define your data models, roles, and permissions directly on the data itself. It also includes a CLI that streamlines local development and deployment to Microsoft Fabric. Because apps deploy to Fabric, they inherit Fabric's enterprise-grade security, governance, and other capabilities.

mentions.sessionTitle: Data, apps, and agents: the future of app dev with Rayfin
mentions.rawName: Rayfin, the backend for the AI coding era
mentions.shortDescription: An SDK and CLI for authoring a full backend (database, functions, storage, access policies) in code, deployable to Fabric with one command for out-of-the-box enterprise security and compliance.
mentions.longDescription: Rayfin (heard as "Rayfind" [inferred]) is positioned as the backend for the AI coding era, providing an SDK and CLI that let a human and an agent define an entire backend in code—including the database, functions, storage, and access policies. Because everything is defined in code, both agents and humans can understand and operate it. When ready, you deploy with a single CLI command directly to Microsoft Fabric, where resources are provisioned and managed for you with enterprise-grade security and compliance out of the gate.

mentions.sessionTitle: Safeguard data across you apps and agents development cycle
mentions.rawName: Real-time (inline) Data Loss Prevention for Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: Security admins can configure DLP policies in Purview that block prompts containing sensitive information from reaching the LLM, using out-of-box or custom-defined sensitive data sets.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft is introducing Realtime, or inline, Data Loss Prevention for prompts as part of the integration between Microsoft Foundry and Purview, enabled with the toggle of a button in the Foundry control plane. Security administrators can set up a DLP policy in Purview that triggers when an end user passes sensitive information into the LLMs, using either out-of-box sets that are part of Purview or custom-defined sets defined by the organization. When the Purview policy kicks in real-time, that particular prompt is blocked from entering the LLM or AI, preventing AI from learning on the organization's sensitive information.

mentions.sessionTitle: Fabric IQ: Bringing enterprise intelligence into the developer workflow
mentions.rawName: Real-time intelligence updates leading into Build
