mentions.shortDescription: GA of the SQL operator in Eventstream, Spark Structured Streaming support with Eventstream, DeltaFlow for event-driven apps, Copilot in real-time intelligence, and MCP plus skills
mentions.longDescription: A set of real-time intelligence updates were released leading up to Build, including the GA of the SQL operator in Eventstream for expressing custom business logic using SQL, and support for Spark Structured Streaming with Eventstream to stream process using Python via a connection between Eventstream and Spark Notebooks. New capabilities for event-driven applications with DeltaFlow make it easy to transform Debezium [inferred] feeds into analytics-ready events without customizing the Eventstream directly. Additional updates include Copilot capabilities in real-time intelligence and a set of MCP and skills to bring real-time data to agents.

mentions.sessionTitle: Modern resiliency from build to recovery through Agentic AI
mentions.shortDescription: Define an ordered workflow capturing interdependencies for failing over resources like databases and VMs during an actual outage
mentions.longDescription: Recovery plans address the challenge of failing over the many interdependent resources in an application during an actual outage, such as failing over a database and a VM in the correct order. They allow customers to create a workflow defining the order in which various resources need to be recovered. The capability is available in public preview as part of the Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager.

mentions.sessionTitle: From Test Kitchen to Table: A Demo-driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers
mentions.shortDescription: An adversarial evaluation feature that simulates malicious users using attack strategies like flip and tense attacks to probe agent vulnerabilities
mentions.longDescription: Red teaming is part of the Foundry evaluation suite and is used to assess how protected an agent is against malicious users. A red teaming run uses an adversarial agent that pretends to be a malicious user and attacks the target agent with prompts designed to trigger harmful behavior. Developers can configure the run by selecting attack types and risk categories—in the demo, the presenter assesses risks such as violence and task adherence on the retail agent. Results can be reviewed later to understand the agent's vulnerabilities.

mentions.sessionTitle: Faster AI Responses with Semantic Caching in Azure Managed Redis
mentions.rawName: Redis Search module at no extra cost
mentions.shortDescription: Enables vector similarity search over stored embeddings, powering both semantic caching and agent memory scenarios.
mentions.longDescription: The Redis Search module is described as the secret sauce that can be configured at no extra cost in Azure Managed Redis. It allows Azure Managed Redis to perform vector similarity search on embeddings stored inside Redis. This capability powers both cost savings through semantic caching and the memory/context scenarios for AI agents.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build secure and enterprise-ready agents with Agent 365
mentions.shortDescription: Ingests agents from connected third-party platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI into the registry for visibility, carrying over existing permissions like deletion.
mentions.longDescription: Registry Sync is a feature within connected agent platforms that ingests agents into the Agent 365 registry for visibility purposes. It takes your permissions and credentials across platforms such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI and brings those agents into the registry. Any governance capabilities or permissions you have across those platforms are also carried over and available inside Agent 365. This complements the SDK-based onboarding path used for custom agents built on frameworks like LangChain or AWS cloud solutions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build the thing that builds the thing
mentions.shortDescription: Tracks days since last release across many projects to flag which need a new release or attention.
mentions.longDescription: Release Bar is a dashboard for maintainers juggling many open source projects, letting the speaker filter specifically on how many days have passed since the last release. It helps decide when another release is needed and which projects need attention, since software that isn't constantly gardened effectively dies as dependencies and systems change. Like his other helper tools, it isn't system-critical, so he vibe-codes it without reading the code and iterates only if it proves useful.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Copilot Anywhere: From Remote Control CLIs to Cloud Sandboxes
mentions.shortDescription: Lets users take a local Copilot session on the go via github.com or the GitHub mobile app, steering and monitoring it in real time across the CLI, the new Copilot desktop app, VS Code, and JetBrains
mentions.longDescription: Remote control sessions let you take a local Copilot session on the go, steering and monitoring work running on your own machine from github.com or a mobile device. The capability applies across clients including the CLI, the new Copilot desktop app launched the prior day, Copilot in VS Code, and Copilot in JetBrains. It also works with any project structure, including GitHub repos, ADO repos, and CLI sessions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Data, apps, and agents: the future of app dev with Rayfin
mentions.shortDescription: Replit's browser-based agentic IDE can build and deploy apps into a Rayfin environment for non-technical users, announced on stage with Satya Nadella the prior day [inferred] and currently in private beta.
mentions.longDescription: Recognizing that not everyone works inside an IDE or CLI, the team announced a partnership with Replit, an agentic browser-based IDE where non-technical and semi-technical users can build apps. While Rayfin and Fabric target highly technical business users who want to get into the code, Replit serves users without coding experience who still want to build and deploy apps, inheriting the same enterprise-grade privacy and security properties. In the demo, a dashboard is built by giving the agent a Power BI semantic model, which it uses to generate the dashboard including underlying DAX queries, then deploys directly into a Rayfin environment.

mentions.sessionTitle: Modern resiliency from build to recovery through Agentic AI
mentions.rawName: Resiliency drills powered by Chaos Studio
mentions.shortDescription: Simulate failures such as an availability-zone outage to test an application's resiliency posture
mentions.longDescription: Resiliency drills let customers test configured resiliency by simulating real-life failure scenarios, such as a particular availability zone going down. Powered by Chaos Studio, the drills help simulate and test an application's resiliency posture before an actual outage occurs. The capability is part of the Azure Infrastructure Resiliency Manager public preview.

mentions.sessionTitle: Data, apps, and agents: the future of app dev with Rayfin
mentions.shortDescription: Upcoming support for functions, RBAC, additional OneLake and Blob storage connectors, OIDC and social login, real-time services, a perpetual free tier, and open-sourcing part of the Rayfin runtime for self-hosting.
mentions.longDescription: Wrapping up, the roadmap outlines what's coming after the current focus on core building blocks (database, enterprise auth out-of-the-box, and easy deployment to Fabric in a managed tenant). Very soon they will add support for functions, RBAC, and additional data connectors so you can connect to any data in OneLake and Blob storage. Looking toward the end of the year, they aim to support more B2B and B2C scenarios by moving beyond Entra auth to OIDC auth and real-time services, plus social login to get started without a company ID and a perpetual free tier. They also plan to open source part of the Rayfin runtime so applications can be self-hosted on various infrastructure.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplifying .NET Installs with dotnetup
mentions.shortDescription: Internal preview (stable SDKs, daily builds, one-shot A/B execution), public preview (self-update, update notifications, full signature verification, agent skills) before end of summer, then GA with official docs.
mentions.longDescription: Chet outlines the dotnetup roadmap beyond what was demoed (stable SDK management and manual runtime management). The internal preview will focus on managing SDKs, with a PR in the pipeline to manage daily/nightly SDKs — both the monthly stable previews (e.g. .NET 11 Preview 4/5) and individual hot builds from the unified build system — selectable via global.json or the command line, plus a one-shot A/B execution command for comparing behaviors. This is motivated partly by agent scenarios that work best without admin rights, in sandboxes, while staying up to date and expressing version constraints the way CI/CD tooling does today.

mentions.sessionTitle: Low-latency AI for developer workflows
mentions.shortDescription: The speakers state the current release is "v1" and that models on Cerebras will grow more intelligent, with future Spark versions absorbing tasks currently limited to full Codex.
mentions.longDescription: Jason Liu emphasizes that the current release is just v1 and that the models on Cerebras are going to get smarter. Sarah Chieng adds that tasks which are Codex-only today might become possible in Spark tomorrow, encouraging developers to learn the tools now ahead of future Spark v2 and v3 releases. Liu contrasts full Codex as a slower, smarter "bus for the mind" with Spark as a fast car that gets you there faster if you know what you're doing.

mentions.sessionTitle: Orchestrate special agents with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Foundry
mentions.rawName: Roughly 5x faster inference at frontier accuracy
mentions.shortDescription: Per third-party artificial analysis benchmarks, Nemotron 3 Ultra reaches frontier-level accuracy with about 5x faster inference speed versus the March release
mentions.longDescription: Using benchmarks from a third party called artificial analysis, which measures both model capabilities and output throughput, Nemotron 3 Ultra is shown to combine frontier-level accuracy with high speed. Plotted against an accuracy index on the Y axis and token generation speed on the X axis, Ultra sits in the upper right relative to the March Nemotron 3 release. NVIDIA states this delivers frontier-level accuracy with about 5x faster inference speed, and they expect to push this further over the next few weeks.

mentions.sessionTitle: From prototype to production: build and run agents at scale
mentions.shortDescription: Event-driven triggers that turn reactive agents into proactive, long-running ones via queued, tracked runs
mentions.longDescription: Routines in Foundry Agent Service are now in public preview. Routines are what make an agent go from reactive to proactive and make it long-running: the developer decides what needs to happen, and Foundry then queues, executes, and tracks every single run. This is how you turn a reactive one-off task into a proactive, continuous agent.

mentions.sessionTitle: Claw and agent harness in Microsoft Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: A trigger feature letting agents react to external stimuli or schedule recurring work, including agents creating their own routines to spin a shut-down sandbox back up for self-maintenance
mentions.longDescription: Routines is a new, in-preview capability on a Foundry agent endpoint, surfaced alongside the agent that the TUI connects to. In the demo, the Hermes agent uses a set of maintenance routines to curate and delete stale skills that accumulate on disk as it works. Because the speaker doesn't want the sandbox running forever, the agent shuts down after about 15 minutes of idle time, and these routines spin it back up when it's time to perform maintenance. A maintenance routine run was shown at the top of the terminal at launch, reflecting a prior execution.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: A multi-mode agent (advisor and critic) available in the Copilot CLI and Copilot app for getting a second opinion on work.
mentions.longDescription: Rubber Duck [inferred] (heard as 'Rover Duck') is an agent for getting a second opinion on your work, made possible because GitHub is multi-model, multi-agent, and multi-surface. It operates in two modes: as an advisor and as a critic, bringing the kind of collaboration developers normally do with other humans into human-and-agent collaboration. It is available in the Copilot CLI (heard as 'Caballo CLI' [inferred Cobalt]) and now also in the GitHub app, where the presenter says he uses it constantly, mainly in critique mode and sometimes in assistance mode to save tokens.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: Cross-model-family critique that, for example, invokes a GPT-5.5 [inferred] agent to critique a plan authored by a Claude model to combine differing model strengths
mentions.longDescription: Boyle introduces rubber duck, presented alongside slash review (code review) and slash security review, as a way to combine multiple models duking it out with each other. He kicks off a workflow using the Create Session tool to spawn two sessions—one for security review and one for code review—running Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.5, and Gemini in parallel sub agents, then uses Rubber Duck to critique the feedback and turn it into PR comments. Security review is powered by tech from GitHub Advanced Security and code review by Copilot code review. He also demonstrates a private "rubber duck" agent thread in PR review mode for quickly building context on a change.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build smarter AI systems in Foundry as models and costs evolve
mentions.shortDescription: A new evaluator type that auto-generates weighted, multi-dimension scoring rubrics from an agent's definition and trajectories
mentions.longDescription: Announced at the conference, rubric-based evaluators are a new evaluator type in Foundry alongside existing prompt- and code-based custom evaluators. When creating a rubric evaluator, you select a specific agent, and Foundry analyzes the agent's definition and seeding trajectories to automatically generate a weighted, multi-dimension scoring rubric (e.g., 7 dimensions for the concierge starter travel agent). Users can edit dimension weights, run the evaluation to see successes and failures across dimensions, and perform cluster analysis of results.

mentions.sessionTitle: From observability to ROI for AI agents on any framework
mentions.shortDescription: Auto-generates a multi-dimensional (e.g. 8-dimension, weighted) evaluator from a system prompt and agent, usable for both offline testing and online evaluation, even with no existing data.
mentions.longDescription: The Rubric Evaluator is now available in public preview, providing out-of-the-box and context-specific observability for agents. Whether you are creating a new agent with no data or have an existing agent that already has traces, you can use the Rubric Evaluator to auto-generate a multi-dimensional evaluator. That evaluator can be used both for offline testing and for online evaluation.

mentions.sessionTitle: From prototype to production: build and run agents at scale
mentions.shortDescription: Auto-generates context-aware, weighted scoring criteria for evaluation and optimization
mentions.longDescription: Rubric for custom evaluation is now in public preview. Rubric auto-generates context-aware criteria and weighted scoring to define what good looks like for both evaluation and optimization, so the developer doesn't have to start from scratch.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using AI tools to teach old apps new tricks
mentions.shortDescription: Centrally encode governance, security, and architecture standards so agents modernize with guardrails and auto-generate compliance reports
mentions.longDescription: Rulebooks, announced in Private Preview, are where you encode your policy and architecture standards so agents modernize with guardrails. You can create a Rulebook inside the Command Center or in the modernize CLI, starting from a markdown file where you write rules, policies, security requirements, and hard boundaries the agents should never cross. Once generated, the Rulebook produces a charter with high-level principles (such as cloud-native authentication via default Azure credential, observability with OpenTelemetry, and approved SKUs like Azure Container Apps) that the agent sticks to when generating a plan.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build secure and enterprise-ready agents with Agent 365
mentions.shortDescription: Automation for lifecycle actions such as reassigning ownerless agents to a manager or auto-blocking agents when risk is identified.
mentions.longDescription: Rules inside Agent 365 provide a simple way to set up automation for lifecycle management actions across agents, replacing otherwise manual processes. Examples include agent reassignment—when an individual leaves an organization, agents built in Agent Builder can be automatically reassigned to their manager—and automatically blocking an agent when risk is identified rather than blocking it manually. The team noted heavy investment in risk to make this as scalable and easy as possible, with more functionality planned over the coming quarters.

mentions.sessionTitle: .NET 11 in depth: Runtime, libraries, and SDK for the AI era
mentions.shortDescription: A compile-time optimization that removes compiler-generated state machines in favor of runtime-managed suspension/resumption; opt in via `Features` `runtime-async=on`, enabled in Preview 4 for the product, likely default in .NET 12
mentions.longDescription: Runtime Async is a new optimization for async code—not a new model, with no new keywords and no source changes required. It is a fast path decided at compile time when you compile with `dotnet build`, and it is completely compatible: old code can call new code and vice versa with no compatibility break in any direction. The big takeaway is that when you enable Runtime Async, there are no compiler-generated state machines. It is opt-in for .NET 11 and will likely be the default in .NET 12, though there is never a compatibility break.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship safer code from your IDE with Aikido
mentions.shortDescription: Bundled malware scanner for packages, included with the plugin.
mentions.longDescription: Safe Chain is a malware package scanner included with the Aikido plugin. It is bundled alongside other features such as the pre-commit hook and the Aikido MCP.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Agentic Workflows: Automation That Actually Reads the Room
mentions.shortDescription: The agent receives only read access to the repository; a separate post-run workflow step holds the permissions to create issues or pull requests, segregating responsibilities.
mentions.longDescription: For agentic workflows to be secure, the agent is not given any permissions besides read access to the repository. Instead, a mechanism called "safe output" runs after the agent completes, and that workflow step holds the access to perform actions such as creating an issue or a pull request, segregating those responsibilities from the agent. This ensures the agent cannot hallucinate, delete the code base, or remove files, keeping the developer in control of what gets merged or discarded.

mentions.sessionTitle: Idea to production-ready agent in seconds on AI-native runtime
mentions.rawName: Sandbox groups with inherited connectors, volumes, snapshots, and disk images
mentions.shortDescription: Settings such as credentials and connectors propagate automatically to sandboxes created within a group
mentions.longDescription: A sandbox group is a container that holds a set of entities such as connectors, volumes, snapshots, and disk images. Sandboxes created and run inside a sandbox group inherit the settings of that group, including credentials and connectors. This is part of the new ACA Sandboxes offering being launched into public preview as an agent-first platform.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building Agents You Can Trust on Windows
mentions.rawName: Sandbox shipping out-of-box in GitHub Copilot CLI and SDK
mentions.shortDescription: Built with the Windows team and currently behind an experimental flag, with general availability and default-on planned for the future.
mentions.longDescription: Through collaboration with the Windows team, the Copilot CLI and SDK can now ship a sandbox out of the box, currently available under an experimental flag and planned to become a default-on solution at GA in the future. This moves the agent to a fully isolated state where the entire agent can be placed inside safe environments and allowed to execute freely, enabling a wider range of jobs end to end without directly supervising the agent. Users can access slash sandbox commands to turn it on and off and to configure policy, including file system configuration that protects working directories. The demos show enabling file system protections so that a request to delete all desktop files triggers a permissions prompt.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure DevOps meets GitHub, the path to AI powered SDLC
mentions.shortDescription: Repos connectable per project per connection increased from 500 to 2,000, addressing customers wanting to connect tens of thousands of repos
mentions.longDescription: Investment in the integration between GitHub repos and Azure DevOps boards, pipelines, and test plans includes scale improvements to the number of repos connectable per project. The limit was originally about 500 repos connected to a project per connection and has now been raised to 2,000. This was driven by larger organizations moving repos into GitHub—examples cited include customers wanting to connect 30,000 and even 80,000 repos to a single project—and the team plans to keep improving it over time.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build persistent and scalable AI agent memory with TiDB
mentions.shortDescription: Idle agents incur no cost, and an isolated database can be spun up per agent in milliseconds
mentions.longDescription: TiDB provides scale to zero, meaning idle agents literally cost nothing and you only pay for the requests you actually run, so bursty traffic produces a bursty bill. It also offers database branching, letting you spin up an isolated database per agent in just a few milliseconds so every agent gets its own workspace separated from everyone else. Additional capabilities mentioned include resource control to cap each workload and fast scale-out, since compute and storage are separated so capacity can be added in seconds.

mentions.sessionTitle: .NET 11 in depth: Runtime, libraries, and SDK for the AI era
mentions.rawName: SDK payload size reduction via hard links
mentions.shortDescription: Automated deduplication in tarball layouts shaved roughly 80MB across platforms, benefiting downloads and SDK containers
mentions.longDescription: The team looked at reducing the on-disk size of the SDK, which is downloaded many times for end users and importantly for containers. They discovered that tarballs support hard links—pointers to files sharing identical content referencing one canonical resource—and found a way to inspect SDK layouts when producing tarballs and packages to do automated unification and deduplication. Over the .NET 11 previews so far, this has shaved roughly 80 megabytes across the various platforms from the SDK payloads, yielding faster downloads and less network IO, especially for SDK containers.

mentions.sessionTitle: Foundry IQ: Fuel agents with enterprise knowledge and agentic retrieval
mentions.shortDescription: The retrieval stack was revamped to exploit newer language models' tool-calling, showing material gains in recall, answer correctness, and completeness over BM25, hybrid search, and minimal mode
mentions.longDescription: Foundry IQ includes a built-in agentic retrieval pipeline that performs query planning—deciding which data sources to look at and how to decompose the query—then runs searches, evaluates results, and iterates based on the configured retrieval effort before producing a final result for the agent. The team is now on the second generation of agentic retrieval, having significantly revamped the stack to take advantage of newer language models' improved tool-calling capabilities since around October of the prior year. Charts showed material improvements across a composition of metrics including recall, answer correctness, completeness, and reduced false "don't know" responses, compared against lexical (BM25) indexes, hybrid (vector plus lexical) search, and a minimal mode with agentic retrieval off. The trade-off is latency, since agentic retrieval can take several seconds compared to instantaneous search indexes.

mentions.sessionTitle: Turn your agents into action: Connect tools, APIs, and documents
mentions.shortDescription: Documents can be split on logical section boundaries, not just page boundaries.
mentions.longDescription: Coming in July, Content Understanding classification will enable you to split documents not just on page boundaries but also on logical section boundaries. This addresses customer feedback that boundaries in documents often don't fall neatly on page boundaries. It builds on classification's ability to identify document types and break long documents or enterprise packages (like case files, application bundles, or tax submissions) into logical parts.

mentions.sessionTitle: Modernize intelligent apps and agents with .NET that scale as you grow
mentions.rawName: Secure RDP access via Azure Bastion
mentions.shortDescription: For the first time in Azure App Service, instances can be reached through Azure Bastion for troubleshooting with familiar tools like Event Viewer, Registry Editor, and IIS Manager
mentions.longDescription: For the first time ever within Azure App Service, you can now remote desktop directly to your instances using Azure Bastion. It uses a secure protocol throughout while giving full access to instances so you can use familiar tools such as Event Viewer, Registry Editor (Registry viewer), and IIS Manager for troubleshooting and investigation. All changes made during these sessions are temporary and must be backed up by changes to your installation script, because when the platform performs maintenance or replaces instances, those customizations need to be reapplied.

mentions.sessionTitle: What we learned shipping VS Code weekly (without breaking everything)
mentions.shortDescription: An agent scans telemetry for unhandled errors, identifies root causes across processes, opens issues, and proposes fixes for human review
mentions.longDescription: The self-healing error pipeline is an automation (run as Cron jobs many times a day) that scans VS Code telemetry for unhandled errors and tries to identify the root cause. When it finds an actionable cause it creates a GitHub issue, shares the stack trace, and is increasingly able to propose a fix and tag the correct owner for human review. The example shown was a regression from May detected from telemetry with little data beyond a stack trace, which the bot ran through and fixed. The bug spanned multiple VS Code processes—the extension host through to the main thread—involving serialization of data, and the agent was able to step back and understand the sequence of events causing the exception.

mentions.sessionTitle: Understand and fix Agent Framework apps with observability and evals
mentions.shortDescription: GitHub Copilot CLI or Claude can use skills to access the dataset and evals, spin up the app in a sandbox, run inputs, and iteratively tweak prompts, models, and tool descriptions to converge on ~90% effectiveness.
mentions.longDescription: Building on the dataset and evaluator, the speaker describes a self-improving software loop using coding agents such as GitHub Copilot CLI or Claude, which can have skills that access this data. Given the code (via a GitHub repo), the inputs, and the evaluations, the coding agent can spin up the application in a sandboxed environment, pump in inputs, run evaluations, look at results, and then tweak the prompt, change the model, or adjust tool descriptions before running again. Over roughly 4–6 cycles it converges on a much better solution, working toward about 90% effectiveness, since agents (like humans) will never be 100%.

mentions.sessionTitle: Faster AI Responses with Semantic Caching in Azure Managed Redis
mentions.shortDescription: Compares a standard LLM workflow against a cached experience, serving similar-intent prompts as cache hits with no new tokens generated.
mentions.longDescription: A live demo compares a regular LLM experience (left side, like Copilot, ChatGPT, or Claude) against the same workflow with semantic caching powered by an Azure Managed Redis instance (right side). Vector embeddings are stored in Redis, and as prompts come in, vector similarity search checks the cache against a configurable threshold to determine a cache hit. The approach aims to save on tokens, reduce response time, and improve consistency for prompts that share the same underlying intent, demonstrated with a Contoso e-commerce example.

mentions.sessionTitle: Develop faster on Windows with AI playbooks and local agents
mentions.shortDescription: Demonstrated keeping personal data (e.g. a Social Security number query) local while routing trivial or low-value queries off enterprise servers to cut cost.
mentions.longDescription: The vLLM router offers sophisticated semantic filtering, which can be heavy on the client, so an agentic layer can pass policies and rules into the same routing layer to make decisions based not just on modality but on quality, cost, or token usage. A demo showed entering a Social Security number and asking which state the user was born in; the rules identified it as personal information and kept the inference local on the GPU/NPU (and the local model even recognized it as a fake number). Another highlighted use case is cost, routing low-value or trivial queries to reduce expense, while semantic rules can be configured per use case, agent, or routing policy.

mentions.sessionTitle: Foundry IQ: Fuel agents with enterprise knowledge and agentic retrieval
mentions.shortDescription: A no-friction tier that provisions in 10–20 seconds, scales to zero, charges only for storage and usage, and is production-ready for dynamic workloads including agents that create and delete services on the fly
mentions.longDescription: Pablo Castro announced the public preview of a serverless version of Foundry IQ, which builds on the same state-of-the-art technology as the existing Foundry IQ stack but removes provisioning friction. The service takes 10-20 seconds to create, costs nothing until used, scales to zero when idle, and charges only for the storage the index consumes. It is production-ready and well-suited for dynamic workloads such as agents creating services, developer workflows, unit tests, and applications that create and delete services on the fly. This complements the existing dedicated capacity option, which remains better for steady, highly predictable workloads with isolated capacity.

mentions.sessionTitle: Idea to production-ready agent in seconds on AI-native runtime
mentions.rawName: Serverless GPUs for custom model inference
mentions.shortDescription: T4 and A100 GPUs scale to zero across 15 regions, used in the demo to run speech-to-text and text-to-speech models
mentions.longDescription: Azure Container Apps' serverless GPU offering is presented as the easiest way to run custom models from sources like Hugging Face via Llama [inferred] or any other model hosting container. It offers T4 GPUs and a series of A100s available across 15 different regions, billed only while the application runs with a scale-to-zero event when idle. In the demo, separate applications ran the speech-to-text (STT) and text-to-speech (TTS) services.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build smarter AI systems in Foundry as models and costs evolve
mentions.shortDescription: Launching at Build, giving control over rewards and hyperparameters while Foundry manages infrastructure
mentions.longDescription: Foundry is launching a serverless API at Build that gives users control over their rewards and hyperparameters while Foundry handles the underlying infrastructure with no cluster management required. It produces a set of low-rank weights (LoRA [inferred]) that are overlaid on top of existing deployments. This sits among Foundry's post-training options between managed fine-tuning and full-control RL, the latter allowing full ownership of code, distributed strategies, algorithms, and GPU clusters with frameworks like Slime [inferred].

mentions.sessionTitle: Under the hood of Microsoft AI models
mentions.rawName: Seven new MAI models across image, transcription, voice, coding, and thinking
mentions.shortDescription: Announced at the morning keynote and detailed here model by model
mentions.longDescription: Dave Citron maps out the seven models Microsoft AI announced at the morning keynote, spanning image, transcription, voice, coding, and thinking. Image 2.5 is the image generation/editing model, now #2 on the LMArena [inferred] leaderboard for image-to-image, with a Flash variant at a third of the cost. Transcribe 1.5 is described as the world's most accurate transcription model across 43 languages and 5x faster than rival models; Voice 2 is the most natural-sounding speech model preferred in 72% of blind tests with a sub-150ms Flash variant; Code 1 Flash is a 5-billion-active-parameter coding model shipping as default in GitHub inside VS Code; and Thinking 1 is the first reasoning model scoring 97% on AIME [inferred] and 53 on SWE-bench Pro.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Build opening keynote
mentions.rawName: Seven new MAI models and Frontier Tuning
mentions.shortDescription: MAI Image-2.5, Transcribe-1.5, Voice-2, Thinking-1, and Code-1-Flash, with a Mayo Clinic partnership to co-develop a healthcare frontier model.
mentions.longDescription: MAI announced a family of seven new models spanning Image, Voice, Transcription, and Coding, tuned for practical, efficient real-world use. MAI Image-2.5 and its Flash variant deliver a step change in quality, reaching number two on the leaderboard and surpassing Nano Banana 2 on image editing; they are live in PowerPoint, rolling out to OneDrive, and available on Foundry. MAI Transcribe-1.5 is positioned as the best transcription model in the world with state-of-the-art accuracy across 43 languages, beating Gemini and OpenAI flagship models and running five times faster, integrated into GitHub, Teams, and Copilot. The announcement frames these within MAI's pursuit of humanist superintelligence.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering the next AI frontier with a unified data platform
mentions.rawName: SharePoint and OneDrive shortcuts GA in OneLake
mentions.shortDescription: These join recently announced SAP and Oracle support, extending zero-ETL data access.
mentions.longDescription: SharePoint and OneDrive shortcuts are now generally available in OneLake, joining the recently announced general availability of SAP and Oracle support. These shortcuts extend OneLake's ability to create a single pane of glass across all data with zero ETL, zero effort, and zero cost, regardless of where the data resides—on-premises, in any cloud, in databases, apps, or files.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unify your entire data estate on a single, AI-ready data lake
mentions.rawName: SharePoint list mirroring and Excel shortcuts in OneLake
mentions.shortDescription: Mirror SharePoint lists and turn Excel sheets into first-class lakehouse tables without pipelines.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft announces SharePoint list mirroring, which lets users mirror a SharePoint Online list by creating a mirrored item, entering the site URL or selecting a connection, choosing a list, and clicking Create—replicating rows automatically with no pipelines or copy jobs, then surfacing the data in a lakehouse via a shortcut. Also announced are Excel shortcuts in OneLake, where Fabric detects an Excel file and lets you select a sheet and accept defaults to turn it into a first-class lakehouse table. The demo uses a fictional company, Zava, tracking new store readiness in a SharePoint list and budget data in an Excel workbook.

mentions.sessionTitle: Unify your entire data estate on a single, AI-ready data lake
mentions.shortDescription: Native AI enrichment with new schema preview/definition and detailed monitoring logs.
mentions.longDescription: Shortcut transformation, which enriches data with native AI capabilities in OneLake, is generally available; it lets you point to source folders on OneLake, add defined AI transformations, and continuously auto-track source changes to sync them to the destination while enriching with AI. New improvements include the ability to preview and define schemas (a top customer ask) and to manage transformations with detailed logs and enhanced monitoring. Possible transformations include format conversions like Parquet to Table or Excel to Table, and AI enrichment such as PII detection, translation, summarization, sentiment analysis, and name recognition.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplifying .NET Installs with dotnetup
mentions.shortDescription: Work with the .NET releases teams to sign all binaries and manifests for provenance and supply-chain safety.
mentions.longDescription: To bring the central management, auditability, and safety that system-level installers (like the one Visual Studio uses) have to user-level installs, the team has been working with the .NET releases teams to sign all of the binaries and all of the manifests involved. This provenance ensures the binaries you use are the ones the team intended to deliver, all the way down. The team also built a library around the tool so other tools that interact with installs can do so correctly and safely, with the hope that the manifests and bookkeeping become a shared resource for tools like Dependabot and Renovate and broader compliance infrastructure.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build collaborative agents into apps with APIs
mentions.rawName: Single cloud billing and inherited governance
mentions.shortDescription: The service appears as a line item on the existing Azure invoice and works with existing Azure Policy, Defender, and DDoS protection.
mentions.longDescription: Omniagent delivers single cloud billing, where the line item shows up on your existing Azure invoice with no separate purchase, vendor, or bill. Existing governance policies just keep working, so the same Azure Policy, Defender, and DDoS protection you already have applies to it. It is provisioned directly from the Azure portal the same way you'd create a Cosmos DB or any other Azure resource.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Dataverse plugin: unleashing coding agents on the enterprise
mentions.shortDescription: Plugin skills such as DBQuery and DVData encode best-practice knowledge and generate tools on the fly, using the Python SDK behind the scenes to parse Excel files and run generated scripts.
mentions.longDescription: The Dataverse plugin for coding agents has skills that encode best-practice knowledge of how to address a particular use case or task, including the ability to use tools behind the scenes such as the Python SDK and to generate on-demand tools that achieve the user's requirements. In the demo this lets the agent parse real Excel files (not CSVs) from a reference data folder and import them into the newly created tables, resolving lookups via business keys rather than GUIDs and reporting any failures. Kent notes it behaved more like a data pipeline than a sample generator, handling lookup dependencies correctly.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale enterprise .NET apps with AI‑assisted cross‑platform workflows
mentions.rawName: Skills and plugins for external agents
mentions.shortDescription: Usable from GitHub Copilot, Codex, and Claude Code, so any agent can be grounded in Uno best practices.
mentions.longDescription: Uno Platform 3.0 ships skills and plugins that can be used from external agents including GitHub Copilot, Codex, and Claude Code [inferred], so any agent can be grounded in Uno best practices. The tooling is powered by MCP, allowing developers to call their own MCP servers or external services, and is model-agnostic—the demo used GPT-5 mini but any model can be chosen. The intent is to let developers start anywhere and lower the barrier to entry.

mentions.sessionTitle: Stop routing docstrings to 70B models with on-device AI on Snapdragon
mentions.shortDescription: An 80 TOPS NPU offering roughly 43% greater compute than the prior generation, up to ~128 GB memory [inferred], and high memory bandwidth supporting multiple data types.
mentions.longDescription: The Snapdragon X2 Elite is positioned as a new generation product with 80 TOPS capacity, providing about 43% greater compute capacity than the previous generation. It offers up to 122 GB of memory [inferred] with memory bandwidth up to 225 GB/s in the Stream edition and 152 in the Elite edition, and supports common data types. The speaker notes a precision/efficiency tradeoff, where integer quantization can roughly halve weight memory versus floating point.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scalable Applications Without Polyglot tax: Azure SQL Hyperscale
mentions.shortDescription: Because page servers write to Azure storage, backups use storage snapshots without consuming compute to read pages, unlike traditional BACKUP DATABASE operations.
mentions.longDescription: In Hyperscale, page servers continuously write back into Azure storage as a durable tier, which allows backups to use Azure storage's snapshot technology. Because of this, the compute layer is not involved in taking backups—no pages need to be read to perform a backup. This contrasts with traditional SQL, where BACKUP DATABASE reads all the data into compute and writes it back to the .bak file; that work is no longer needed with Hyperscale snapshot backups.

mentions.sessionTitle: Idea to production-ready agent in seconds on AI-native runtime
mentions.shortDescription: An entire sandbox disk can be snapshotted and used to spin up an exact new instance
mentions.longDescription: Because agents do work that constantly has to be undone and redone, the platform allows snapshotting of an entire sandbox disk to replay it or use it as a reference point to move forward from. In the demo, a snapshot was created trivially and then used to spin up a new sandbox instance. The resulting new sandbox was an exact copy of the original agent (Aria) including its sessions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale enterprise .NET apps with AI‑assisted cross‑platform workflows
mentions.rawName: Specialized Uno Platform agent backed by 60+ skills
mentions.shortDescription: A purpose-built agent, grounded by skills and MCP tools, that knows how to build Uno Platform apps and validate UI in a loop; skills cover areas like navigation and Material toolkit theming.
mentions.longDescription: A purpose-built Uno Platform agent grounded by documentation search/fetch and MCP-based app interactivity tools (click, screenshot) so it can work in a loop until the UI is correct. The same MCP tools work across the Uno IDE flow and GitHub Copilot inside Visual Studio, VS Code, or other editors. The agent is backed by 60+ skills released as of that day for areas like navigation and Material toolkit theming, helping the agent do the right thing as part of the Uno Platform Studio 3.0 push.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scalable Applications Without Polyglot tax: Azure SQL Hyperscale
mentions.rawName: SQL MCP server via Data API Builder
mentions.shortDescription: A REST endpoint from Data API Builder can be exposed as an MCP server, enabling natural-language interaction with Hyperscale data.
mentions.longDescription: SQL has its own MCP server, built with Data API Builder (DAB). You create a DAB to get a Data API REST endpoint, and that REST endpoint can be pointed to an MCP, which can come from Hyperscale. This enables talking to your data—even 128 TB of data with agents and writes—using natural language, such as updating a person's last name or changing a salary, all through MCP.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and deploy an Azure app with your agent team
mentions.rawName: Squad multi-agent framework for GitHub Copilot
mentions.shortDescription: An open-source tool Gaster built with Tamir [inferred] that spins up a team of specialized Copilot agents, each with a distinct job, to reach results faster than single-threaded conversation.
mentions.longDescription: Squad is a tool Brady Gaster developed with his friend Tamir, a multi-agent framework for GitHub Copilot. It spins up multiple agents talking at the same time, which uses a lot of tokens but reaches the endpoint quicker than a single-threaded conversation directly with Copilot. It can be used in a brand new or existing repo, brownfield or greenfield; running "squad init" (with a no-workflows option) drops a bunch of files on disk, and a squad agent can then be selected as a GitHub Copilot agent to create a new squad with descriptive names.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using autonomous SRE to move from alerts to action
mentions.rawName: SRE Agent endpoint as an MCP server
mentions.shortDescription: The agent can be accessed as an MCP server to view analyses or configure it outside the Azure Portal
mentions.longDescription: The SRE Agent endpoint can be accessed as an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, allowing developers to connect to it to either view the analysis the agent performed or configure things outside of the Azure Portal. The presenter uses Copilot CLI with a locally running MCP to connect to the newly created agent, checking the JSON configuration file and applying the deployment URL. This capability has been available for a while now.

mentions.sessionTitle: What we learned shipping VS Code weekly (without breaking everything)
mentions.shortDescription: Replaces the previous all-at-once deployment, letting the team freeze a build after catching a problem at 8% rollout
mentions.longDescription: The team now does staged, incremental rollouts of VS Code through their update server, replacing the previous approach of deploying to 100% all at once. This lets them observe effects in the wild across their 40+ million users, which differs greatly from internal Insiders usage, and the same data drives both the live dashboard and the update server. The capability to freeze a build and fall back to previous builds is built into their build site; in the example shown a build was frozen after reaching 8% rollout because a problem was caught, letting them stop it before it affected most users. This incremental rollout and freeze tooling is relatively new and has grown substantially as the team's needs expanded.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplifying .NET Installs with dotnetup
mentions.shortDescription: `dotnetup runtime install 8.0 9.0 10.0` fetches multiple runtimes for multi-targeted test runs without installing full parallel SDKs.
mentions.longDescription: dotnetup makes it easy to install just the runtimes needed to run an application, rather than installing entire parallel SDKs as is commonly done in CI/CD setups. Running `dotnet runtime install 8.0 9.0 10.0` fetches the latest release of each of those bands and installs them all at the same time, and specific versions can be requested if needed. This lets developers run multi-targeted tests without installing full SDKs at hundreds of megabytes apiece, and other specifiers such as ASP.NET Core (and Windows desktop on Windows) are also supported.

mentions.sessionTitle: Azure Storage for AI workloads​
mentions.shortDescription: A centralized hub for file, block, and object storage that provides a unified view of the storage estate and launch points into storage-for-AI experiences.
mentions.longDescription: Storage Center is a centralized hub for file, block, and object storage in one place, giving a unified view of the storage landscape including usage, performance, and redundancy tiers, plus tools like lifecycle management and storage mover with rich visualizations. It is positioned as the best place for both admins and developers to land their data—starting with Blob—and then connect it to AI, with launch points into the storage-for-AI experiences covered in the session. Microsoft announced a limited preview of this experience, with a QR code on the slide to sign up.

mentions.sessionTitle: Develop faster on Windows with AI playbooks and local agents
mentions.shortDescription: A headless always-on PC using the same processor as the demo laptops, designed to run background agent teams overnight; available to order in June.
mentions.longDescription: The Halo box is a forthcoming headless appliance PC built around the exact same Strix Halo [inferred] processor found in the demo laptops, positioned as the future of AMD's agentic AI work. In a plug-in, completely headless form factor, it is designed to run always-on teams of agents non-stop overnight—scraping GitHub issues, social media, and the competitive landscape so a Notion dashboard to-do list is ready in the morning. It is not out yet but can be seen at the booth, with a big announcement coming in June.

mentions.sessionTitle: Secure agent workflows in GitHub Copilot with NVIDIA OpenShell
mentions.shortDescription: The prover runs in single-digit milliseconds, avoiding the doubled token cost and latency of using a second agent to review every action
mentions.longDescription: Rather than relying only on an if-statement check, the prover creates a mathematical proof of what an agent can do, such as whether it can access the Internet or write to a repository. Unlike using a second trusted agent to review each sandbox change—an approach OpenAI and Anthropic [inferred] are starting to discuss—the prover cannot be fooled (assuming the policy logic is described correctly) and will flag, for example, a newly opened hole that lets an agent write to a new GitHub repo. It can run in single-digit milliseconds, avoiding the doubled token cost and latency of having another agent review every call, so the second-level review is often not even required.

mentions.sessionTitle: Idea to production-ready agent in seconds on AI-native runtime
mentions.shortDescription: Sandboxes wake from sleep in roughly a second or two, retaining running scripts and context to avoid the environment setup tax
mentions.longDescription: ACA Sandboxes support a fast resume capability where a sleeping sandbox wakes in roughly a second or two while retaining its memory and disk state. In the demo, a sandbox running a behind-the-scenes script was left to sleep for about 20-25 minutes, then woken up to continue running the script exactly as it was before sleeping. Sandboxes can be configured to capture either disk and memory or just disk when they go to sleep.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Build opening keynote
mentions.shortDescription: A developer "dream machine" with one petaflop of AI compute, 20 CPU cores, and 128 GB unified memory, available on a waitlist in the fall; Windows is also coming to NVIDIA's DGX station [inferred].
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft announced the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box, a developer "dream machine" that maxes out compute and memory on the new architecture. It delivers one petaflop of AI compute, 20 CPU cores, and 128 GB of unified memory access. It is coming in the fall, and attendees can join a waitlist. This follows the earlier Surface Ultra device that pairs NVIDIA power with Surface design, featuring 128 GB unified memory, a 2,000-nit display, and all-day battery life.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and ship faster with a developer-optimized Windows experience
mentions.shortDescription: A developer-first GPU machine with the NVIDIA RTX Spark [inferred] offering up to 1 petaflop of AI compute and 128GB of unified memory, preconfigured with the developer tools by default
mentions.longDescription: The Surface RTX Spark Dev box is a developer-first GPU machine featuring the new NVIDIA RTX Spark [inferred], providing up to 1 petaflop of AI compute and 128GB of unified memory. It comes optimized with Microsoft's developer tools already available by default. It was introduced alongside the software optimizations available to all Windows 11 devices.

mentions.sessionTitle: From Test Kitchen to Table: A Demo-driven Tour of Foundry Portal for AI Developers
mentions.rawName: Synthetic data generation for batch evaluation
mentions.shortDescription: The portal can generate synthetic test prompts to run batch and continuous evaluations against an agent
mentions.longDescription: Because a new agent in the test kitchen has no real user prompts to test against, the Foundry portal can generate synthetic data to use for evaluation. The demo sets up a batch evaluation targeting a specific agent version and generates a small synthetic dataset (e.g., 10 test prompts), optionally also generating candidate responses, using a chosen model. The prompts are described broadly—customer support queries for a DIY home-improvement retailer covering single and multi-turn conversations and edge cases like out-of-stock or returns. Batch evaluations can be run manually or in continuous evaluation form against a large dataset.

mentions.sessionTitle: From zero to teammate in 25 minutes: Build a Teams agent live
mentions.rawName: Teams dev agent skill for GitHub Copilot
mentions.shortDescription: A Copilot skill that can call the Teams CLI and read the Teams docs to integrate an existing app into Teams from a single prompt.
mentions.longDescription: Instead of manually downloading the Teams SDK packages and reading the docs to integrate an app, the presenter runs Copilot in YOLO mode in a session scaffolded with the Teams dev agent skill, giving it the simple prompt to integrate the application into Microsoft Teams and return the installation link. The skill can do two things: talk to the Teams CLI and read the Teams docs. Copilot picks up the skill automatically and uses it to complete the integration.

mentions.sessionTitle: From zero to teammate in 25 minutes: Build a Teams agent live
mentions.shortDescription: The previously separate Teams AI Library and tooling are unified into a single streamlined Teams SDK developer experience.
mentions.longDescription: Following last year's release of the Teams AI Library in TypeScript and C#, this year the team is introducing the Teams SDK, which consolidates all the libraries and tools developers use into one streamlined developer experience. It also adds many new group UX features to make agents shine within a group, building on prior one-on-one agentic features such as streaming, feedback loops, follow-up citations, and starter prompts. The team has been working with partners including Cursor, Linear, Perplexity, Datadog, and Atlassian, who are building on the Teams SDK to benefit from 320 million daily active users.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build modern .NET apps with Uno Platform, AI, and visual tools
mentions.rawName: Teased Build theater session with partner Kahua
mentions.shortDescription: A live joint session promising a "very big announcement and a surprise," plus an Expo booth presence.
mentions.longDescription: Sam Basu extends an open invitation to a live Microsoft Build theater session featuring Uno Platform and partner Kahua onstage together, where they will show more of what was previewed. He teases a "very big announcement and a surprise" waiting on the cards. He also mentions a booth presence in the Expo area where attendees can discuss the latest tech, AI, and grab swag.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build agentic apps in minutes with Rayfin and Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: A single command picks a starter template that pre-bakes dependencies and the agent "skills" needed to work seamlessly with coding agents
mentions.longDescription: A simple application can be created by running an npm create command, which prompts you to start from a template and pick the one you want. Because you start from a template, dependencies are pre-baked, so setup takes a while but a lot of configuration is handled for you. The templates also include the skills and context needed to work seamlessly with any coding agent, so the agent can build the application the way the SDK expects.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build secure and enterprise-ready agents with Agent 365
mentions.shortDescription: A "hero" feature aggregating custom policies across Entra, Defender, Purview, and SharePoint into reusable templates applied during agent approval.
mentions.longDescription: Templates, described as one of Agent 365's hero features, aggregate custom policies from across Entra, Defender, Purview, and even SharePoint into one reusable template that can be applied to agents in a consistent and comprehensive way. Default templates are provided and custom ones can be created, including configuration of access packages, conditional access, and default policies such as DLP protection and lifecycle management protections. The template is then leveraged as part of the agent approval flow, where an IT admin team approves a published agent and applies the appropriate template.

mentions.sessionTitle: Discover, govern, and scale Azure resources with HashiCorp Terraform
mentions.rawName: Terraform Search via the `terraform query` command
mentions.shortDescription: Available in the Terraform CLI since Terraform 1.14 (released November 2025), it inverts the import workflow: instead of writing import blocks by hand, you define a query, run it, and let Terraform discover matching unmanaged resources.
mentions.longDescription: Terraform Search is a feature available in the Terraform CLI since Terraform 1.14 (released November 2025) that inverts the traditional import workflow. Instead of hand-writing import blocks (which requires already knowing the resource ID and that the resource exists in Azure), you define a search query, run the `terraform query` command, and let Terraform authenticate to Azure and query the remote API for matching unmanaged resources. The process is three steps: define a search query (e.g. all unmanaged MS SQL servers in a subscription's build resource group), run the query command, and generate code.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build AI-powered collaboration on a visual canvas
mentions.shortDescription: The Lucid AI Prompt Editor turns pasted prompts into diagrams placed inside assisted-layout containers that auto-rearrange arrows as shapes are moved.
mentions.longDescription: Lucid's AI tool lets users create diagrams straight from text prompts via the Lucid AI Prompt Editor at the top left, where pasted context generates a logical flowchart with if/then branches. The output is placed in a default assisted-layout container so shapes can be edited and moved while arrows rearrange themselves automatically. A toolbar also lets users add, remove, or change nodes and decision branches without manual work.

mentions.sessionTitle: From the Field: Accelerate Your Development for Microsoft Marketplace
mentions.rawName: The Azure Marketplace is now the Microsoft Marketplace
mentions.shortDescription: the rebranded marketplace serves ISVs (visibility and go-to-market support), partners (private offer selling and reselling), and end customers (ease of deployment and Azure consumption commitment credit)
mentions.longDescription: The Azure Marketplace has been rebranded as the Microsoft Marketplace, positioned as the way to transform infrastructure-as-code templates into trusted, deployable products for customers. The speaker, a Microsoft MVP working for an ISV, frames the marketplace as beneficial to all parties: for ISVs it provides visibility and go-to-market support for their solutions. The session's goal is to walk through taking BICEP templates and turning them into deployable Marketplace products.

mentions.sessionTitle: Run AI SREs without burning token budgets
mentions.rawName: The "naive" cost of AI SREs is roughly $730,000/year for a typical Fortune 500
mentions.shortDescription: At ~1,000 alerts per day and ~$2 per investigation (a midpoint within a $180k–$1.8M range), the cost often exceeds that of human triage and becomes a non-starter.
mentions.longDescription: Natan Yellin explains that a typical Fortune 500 sees at least a thousand alerts per day across teams, and running an AI SRE naively on all of them is too expensive. At roughly $2 per investigation and a thousand alerts per day, the cost rapidly reaches about $730,000 a year, a figure that matches what they see enterprise after enterprise. This is usually more expensive than having humans triage alerts manually, making it a non-starter.

mentions.sessionTitle: Imagine Cup World Championship
mentions.rawName: Three finalists selected from over 1,000 submissions
mentions.shortDescription: Copy Flag, Spoilsafe, and Revora Health advanced to the world championship.
mentions.longDescription: Dona Sarkar announced that three startups rose to the top from over 8,000 submissions to advance to the Imagine Cup World Championship, where they pitched to a panel of judges. This year's journey was shaped by Microsoft for Startups along with partners at GitHub Education and Replit, and founders were matched with industry-leading mentors. The judges were Dr. Irina Raicu, Bakari Brock, and Thea Myhrvold.

mentions.sessionTitle: Using autonomous SRE to move from alerts to action
mentions.shortDescription: Interactive (Copilot-style), reactive (alert-driven response via Azure Monitor, PagerDuty, ServiceNow), and proactive (scheduled cron-based health, compliance, and security checks)
mentions.longDescription: The Azure SRE Agent can be used in three ways designed to span the full operational lifecycle. Interactive mode lets you chat directly with the agent in the Azure portal, ask diagnostics questions, perform natural language operations, and upload task or HAR files for trace analysis—essentially a Copilot mode that assumes a human is driving. Reactive mode is the alert-driven response mode where the agent responds automatically to Azure Monitor alerts and integrates with PagerDuty and ServiceNow, performing automated triage, initial root cause analysis, and triggering mitigation with approval. Proactive mode runs autonomously on a schedule using cron expressions for continuous health and compliance checks, anomaly detection, security posture assessment, and resource optimization recommendations.

mentions.sessionTitle: So you want to become an MVP?
mentions.shortDescription: To pursue the award: be an expert, do what you love, and let the program know, since nomination must come from a Microsoft employee or an existing MVP.
mentions.longDescription: The session wraps up by summarizing three simple steps to become an MVP: be an expert, do what you love, and let the program know. To be awarded MVP status, you have to be nominated either by a Microsoft employee or by an existing MVP. The closing advice is to do what you love, share that, and contribute to the community.

mentions.sessionTitle: Stop routing docstrings to 70B models with on-device AI on Snapdragon
mentions.shortDescription: Route simple/medium prompts to an on-device model (≤13B), medium-to-high tasks to an on-prem workstation (14B–34B, with up to ~100–120B on larger boxes), and only complex/security work to the cloud (70B+).
mentions.longDescription: A three-tier routing model distributes AI workloads by complexity: simple-to-medium queries (about 30% of workload, scored low on a 1-4 complexity scale) run locally on a Snapdragon X2 Elite, medium-to-high tasks go to a more capable on-prem workstation or headless machine, and the remaining complex 20-30% that the X2 Elite cannot run are sent to the cloud. The tiers map to your personal/desk computer, an on-prem workstation, and the cloud. The speaker frames this as a cost-saving distribution (contrasting with someone spending $1,000,000 a month) that can justify on-premises hardware to a CIO.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building Agents You Can Trust on Windows
mentions.rawName: Three Windows agent primitives: identity, containment, manageability
mentions.shortDescription: Windows treats agents as a new class of user with a distinct security principal, an enforced isolation boundary, and IT-governable policies.
mentions.longDescription: As the definition of a "user" expands to include agents acting on a person's behalf, Windows is introducing three key platform capabilities so agents can be treated as a new class of user and run safely and reliably. The first is agent identity, giving the agent an identity distinct from the human user. The second is containment, running agents in a controlled environment where their blast radius is limited rather than granting full access to all files and data. The third is manageability, allowing an IT admin to deploy, monitor, govern, and enforce policies dictating what an agent can and cannot do.

mentions.sessionTitle: Profile and optimize agentic AI on Windows
mentions.rawName: Time-correlated platform telemetry across IP blocks
mentions.shortDescription: Data from multiple drivers operating in different time domains is unified into one time domain, removing the burden of manual correlation previously required of tooling
mentions.longDescription: A capability called unified telemetry puts data from multiple drivers—which often operate in different time domains—into the same, time-correlated time domain. It collects platform telemetry from CPU, GPU, NPU, and power (and can incorporate OS-specific data via ETW), and combines it with application-side software tracing through ITT (Intel Instrumentation and Tracing Technology), an open-source project used to instrument much of the Intel AI stack such as OpenVINO and oneDNN [inferred]. Previously, getting data from different drivers at different rates and time domains required a tool chain to align them manually, which was always a complex problem; unified telemetry, available starting this week, removes that burden.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering modern data analytics in Fabric Data Warehouse
mentions.rawName: Time travel on SQL analytics endpoint
mentions.shortDescription: Query data as it appeared at any prior point, governed by the lakehouse retention period.
mentions.longDescription: Time travel is being extended from the warehouse to the SQL analytics endpoint, letting you query data exactly as it looked at any prior point in time. This addresses common day-to-day data team needs such as audits to prove what numbers were on a specific date, point-in-time comparisons to see how a metric drifted, and recreating data when a downstream report looks wrong. It eliminates the need to create snapshots or copies of data for these scenarios, and how far back you can go is governed by the retention period configured in your lakehouse.

mentions.sessionTitle: Turn your agents into action: Connect tools, APIs, and documents
mentions.shortDescription: A protocol/tool inside a toolbox that searches tool metadata at runtime and loads only the tool required for a task, conserving tokens instead of loading everything into the context window.
mentions.longDescription: Tool search is a tool within Toolbox that searches for the specific tool needed by leveraging and pulling all the tool metadata to find the right one at runtime. Instead of loading everything into the context window, it loads only the tool required to complete the task, conserving tokens. In the demonstrated flow, an agent that needs GitHub directly picks the GitHub toolbox as the only one loaded into the context window. This replaces manually wiring every tool to an agent with attaching a toolbox exposed through a unified endpoint.

mentions.sessionTitle: Turn your agents into action: Connect tools, APIs, and documents
mentions.shortDescription: A reusable, Foundry-managed bundle of tools that agents consume through one consistent interface and a single unified MCP-compatible endpoint, regardless of underlying tool type.
mentions.longDescription: Toolbox is a reusable bundle of tools managed in Foundry that agents can consume through a single consistent interface regardless of the underlying tool type—whether MCP, OpenAI API spec, skill, or connector. It addresses the problem that integrating many tools (each with its own identity, protocols, and credential management) consumes more developer time than building agents. Foundry handles the lifecycle, and a single unified endpoint with one OAuth and one experience can be integrated into any agent. The four pillars are build, configure/publish, and govern, enabling tool creation, discovery, and governance while minimizing token bloat in the context window.

mentions.sessionTitle: Turn your agents into action: Connect tools, APIs, and documents
mentions.shortDescription: Shipped in 2025, a single place for custom and ecosystem tools, with the option of a private registry via Azure API Center and Azure API Management.
mentions.longDescription: The tools catalog, shipped in 2025, provides a single place where developers and the broader ecosystem can find all tool types—including OpenAPI, MCP, A2A, Logic App connectors, skills, CLIs, hooks, and plugins. Foundry hosts a set of custom and ecosystem-built tools in one location. For those needing their own private registry, it can be done with Azure API Center and Azure API Management for additional governance. The catalog solves tool discovery, though integrating tools remains a separate problem.

mentions.sessionTitle: Supercharged profiling: Finding performance bugs with agents
mentions.shortDescription: An analyze button and generate-top-insights feature surface known bad patterns in .NET and C++ (such as calling `Contains` on a list) and suggest concrete optimizations.
mentions.longDescription: The profiler offers an analyze button that asks Copilot to suggest optimizations for a trace by looking at the top functions, the hot call path, and the caller/callee data. A top insights feature fires on known bad patterns in .NET and C++, such as calling IndexOf on a linked list or Contains on a regular list, and suggests concrete fixes like using a set for hashed direct access. If no insights fire automatically, a "generate top insights" button has Copilot read the trace and propose ideas such as removing repeated null checks, avoiding boxing an enumerator by using a concrete type with IEnumerable, and constructing the StreamWriter with a larger buffer.

mentions.sessionTitle: From observability to ROI for AI agents on any framework
mentions.rawName: Traces to data sets with smart filtering
mentions.shortDescription: Selected production traces can be fed back into data sets to expand inner-loop test coverage and enable regression testing.
mentions.longDescription: With traces-to-data-sets and smart filtering capabilities, you can select production traces and feed them back into your data sets to improve test coverage in the inner loop. Because initial test coverage (e.g. 20 test cases) cannot cover everything seen in production, this lets you continually expand coverage and regression-prove changes using real signals generated by the agent.

mentions.sessionTitle: Understand and fix Agent Framework apps with observability and evals
mentions.shortDescription: The free, open-source telemetry backend from Arise [inferred] renders OpenInference data as a trace tree showing system/user prompts, tool calls, token counts, and every decision the agent framework makes.
mentions.longDescription: Phoenix is a free, open-source backend for telemetry data made by Arize [inferred], who invented OpenInference, and is the standard default out-of-the-box way of rendering OpenInference data. It provides a complete breakdown of what the agent is doing, presenting a tree diagram starting from a top-level process run down through each LLM call and tool call. The developer can see the system prompt, user prompt, the request to do tool calls, token counts in and out, and the inputs and outputs of every part of the system. This gives granular visibility into everything the Agent Framework decides to do, such as calling the check-policy tool and receiving its response.

mentions.sessionTitle: Simplifying .NET Installs with dotnetup
mentions.rawName: Tracking, updates, and uninstalls via a manifest
mentions.shortDescription: `dotnetup list` tracks installed components and the channels being followed; `dotnetup update` installs new releases and removes out-of-date installs no longer needed.
mentions.longDescription: `dotnetup list` tracks what is currently installed along with the explicit runtime requests being followed, and supports the component name @version pattern (e.g. `dotnetup runtime install aspnetcore@8.0`). When new versions of runtimes release, a simple `dotnetup update` installs them and brings out-of-date installs up to the requested state. This works because dotnetup keeps a manifest — an installation tracker in a data directory in the user directory — acting like a lock file for the declared/desired state of the system, while global.json remains the way to describe development requirements across repos and developers.

mentions.sessionTitle: Under the hood of Microsoft AI models
mentions.shortDescription: Described as the world's most accurate transcription model across 43 languages and up to 5x faster than rival models
mentions.longDescription: Transcribe 1.5 is presented as the best transcription model in the world, with state-of-the-art accuracy across 43 languages, beating Gemini and OpenAI's flagship transcription models on head-to-head accuracy benchmarks. Beyond benchmark accuracy, it is optimized for real-world use including noisy environments, accents, domain-specific terminology, and multiple speakers. On artificial analysis speed benchmarks it is up to 5x faster than rival models while also being more accurate. It is already integrated across the Microsoft stack—Copilot, Teams, GitHub, Dynamics 365—and is available on Foundry now.

mentions.sessionTitle: Orchestrate omnichannel AI agents with Foundry and Twilio
mentions.shortDescription: A newly launched open-source SDK with two connectors—one to Twilio, one to Foundry—that handles real-time conversation management, persistent memory, and multi-channel orchestration to create a single agent across all channels
mentions.longDescription: Twilio Agent Connect is a new product launched a couple of weeks before the session that bridges Microsoft Foundry and Twilio to create a single AI agent across all channels. It is one open-source SDK with two connectors—one to Twilio and one to Foundry—where Twilio handles real-time conversation management, persistent memory, and multi-channel orchestration, while Foundry provides the intelligence, voice live API, foundational models, and agent framework SDK. The goal is to move from conception to production with less engineering effort and a production-ready, omnichannel agent. It was first deployed via Azure Container Apps connecting Twilio channels over WebSockets, with Azure Cosmos DB for state management and Foundry for model calls.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build modern .NET apps with Uno Platform, AI, and visual tools
mentions.shortDescription: Uno MCP grounds AI agents in current documentation, while Uno App MCP gives agents "eyes and hands" to screenshot, click, and validate running app UI.
mentions.longDescription: Uno Platform offers two MCP servers out of the box, wired up automatically via an mcp.json file when a Uno Platform project is detected. The first, Uno MCP, brings the context of the latest documentation to the AI agent so it can search, fetch pages, summarize, and initialize with best practices. The second, Uno App MCP, gives AI agents "eyes and hands"—described as Playwright for cross-platform .NET apps—so the agent can screenshot, click, inspect the visual tree, paste text, and key press to validate the running app's UI.

mentions.sessionTitle: Apply orchestration patterns for production AI agents
mentions.rawName: UiPath conversational agents now run in Microsoft Teams
mentions.shortDescription: agents built in UiPath via integration service connectors can be deployed through standard Teams packaging for one-on-one chats or channel-based workflows.
mentions.longDescription: UiPath agents, built and deployed in UiPath using its extensive integration service connectors, can now run inside Microsoft Teams. Once built, an agent is deployed via a standard Teams packaging process, after which employees can use it in one-on-one chats or in channel-based workflows. Employees can submit information, check process status, and receive updates all without leaving Teams.

mentions.sessionTitle: Run AI SREs without burning token budgets
mentions.rawName: Underlying investigation cost runs 50 cents to $5, driven almost entirely by input tokens
mentions.shortDescription: Agents ingest large volumes of logs, metrics, and observability data, while output token costs remain minimal; observability vendors typically mark this up to around $25 per investigation.
mentions.longDescription: Yellin notes that the underlying cost of an SRE agent investigation is in the 50-cent to $5 range across the industry, depending on how complex the alert is, with simple investigations pulling little data costing 50 cents and complex ones reaching $5. This cost is driven almost entirely by input tokens, since the agent pulls large volumes of logs, metrics, and observability data, while output token costs remain minimal. Observability vendors typically charge a markup, around $25 per investigation. Taking the two ranges yields a 180k to 1.8 million span, with a $2 midpoint giving $730k.

mentions.sessionTitle: Orchestrate special agents with NVIDIA Nemotron models on Foundry
mentions.shortDescription: A single downloadable checkpoint runs in NVFP4 on Blackwell and falls back to run on Hopper, eliminating separate per-precision files
mentions.longDescription: Nemotron 3 Ultra introduces a single unified checkpoint rather than separate files for different precision formats. Previously, different hardware required different formats (BF16/FP8 on Hopper, BF16 on Ampere [inferred], NVFP4 on Blackwell). With Ultra, one checkpoint file—for example downloaded from Hugging Face—runs in NVFP4 on Blackwell but can also fall back and run well on Hopper. This reduces the number of options and makes it much easier to select the right checkpoint.

mentions.sessionTitle: Taking your AI to the edge with .NET MAUI
mentions.shortDescription: A new property (none, soft input, etc.) settable per page or layout to handle notches, dynamic island, and Android camera cutouts on iOS and Android
mentions.longDescription: The new unified SafeArea edges API handles the varied unusable screen regions across devices, such as the iOS notch, dynamic island, bottom swipe gestures, and Android camera cutouts. The property can be set to values like none or soft input to control whether content draws under these areas or reserves space, and can be applied per content page or per layout. It works on Android and iOS, and pairs well with effects like iOS liquid glass to achieve designer-intended looks.

mentions.sessionTitle: Union types in C#
mentions.rawName: Union types are coming to C# 15, shipping November
