mentions.shortDescription: the feature is already available in preview for developers to try.
mentions.longDescription: Mads Torgersen (lead designer of C#) and Dustin Campbell announce that Union Types are being added to C# 15, which is coming out in November. They note the feature is already available in preview, with details on how to try it promised at the end of the session. They describe C#'s unions as their own "Goldilocks" / compromise version, distinct from unions in TypeScript or functional languages' discriminated unions.

mentions.sessionTitle: Union types in C#
mentions.rawName: Unions can be generic and carry function members
mentions.shortDescription: a `result<T>` union can wrap `success<T>` and `error`, and unions may declare computed properties and methods, though additional instance state is disallowed.
mentions.longDescription: Unions can be generic, demonstrated with a `result<T>` union that brings together a `success<T>` (carrying a generic data payload) and an `error` record, gluing existing records together so the compiler knows they are related. A method can return `result<T>` and return either of the two cases, and because the cases are records, the data can be deconstructed directly out of them in a switch. The demo models reading values off the wire as a queue of results, dequeuing and switching on success or error.

mentions.sessionTitle: Union types in C#
mentions.rawName: Unions enforce exhaustiveness in switch expressions
mentions.shortDescription: once a value is typed as a union, the compiler warns when not all case types (including null where applicable) are handled.
mentions.longDescription: Once a value is typed as a union (e.g. a union of pets), the compiler can prove whether a switch expression is exhaustive, removing the earlier warning once all case types are covered. Commenting out one of the case types brings the warning back, demonstrating that the compiler ensures all cases—and nothing but the cases—are handled. The system is smart enough that if the union includes a nullable case (e.g. a nullable bird), null must also be handled for the switch to be exhaustive.

mentions.sessionTitle: Beyond REST: .NET Apps That Talk to Hardware
mentions.shortDescription: The speaker noted Uno's new studio is "agent first" with predefined skills and an MCP server for development that can build cross-platform apps from a design
mentions.longDescription: The speaker highlighted a new release of Uno Platform's studio, describing it as "agent first" with a set of predefined skills and an MCP server for development. Running the studio gives you MCP and skills, and you can point it at a design and have it build a robust app that runs across multiple platforms and the web. The speaker is using Uno alongside .NET MAUI [inferred] in his code base because they run everywhere — Win UI on Mac, iOS, and Android out of the box — and provide access to phone hardware like accelerometers and geolocation. He referred attendees to Uno's booth for more detail.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale enterprise .NET apps with AI‑assisted cross‑platform workflows
mentions.shortDescription: The evolution of Uno's AI and design tooling into an agentic workflow with skills, plugins, MCP tools, previews, and snippets.
mentions.longDescription: Uno Platform Studio 3.0 is presented as the evolution of Uno's AI and design tooling into an agentic workflow with skills, plugins, MCP tools, previews, and snippets. It includes a specialized agent that knows how to build Uno Platform apps, backed by 60+ skills and MCP tools so agents can look at docs and validate the UI in efficient agentic loops. To remove cross-platform .NET setup barriers (iOS, Android, Windows, Mac SDKs), it ships as the zero-install Uno Platform Studio app that runs on desktop, web, and mobile, spinning up a full .NET app in the browser with visual UI editing and export to an IDE or CLI.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build modern .NET apps with Uno Platform, AI, and visual tools
mentions.rawName: Uno Platform Studio AI and design tools
mentions.shortDescription: A collection of productivity tools layered on the Uno Platform foundation, including the Hot Design runtime visual designer and a custom AI agent.
mentions.longDescription: Uno Platform Studio is a collection of AI and design tools built on top of the Uno Platform foundation, meant to supercharge developer productivity. It includes Hot Design, a runtime visual designer for cross-platform .NET apps that provides a design canvas to tweak UI while the app is running, plus a custom AI agent to build UI. With Hot Reload, the running app, design surface, and code in the IDE all stay in sync.

mentions.sessionTitle: Scale enterprise .NET apps with AI‑assisted cross‑platform workflows
mentions.shortDescription: A zero-install app running on desktop, web, and mobile that spins up a full cross-platform .NET app from a prompt, with visual editing and export to an IDE, GitHub, or local environment.
mentions.longDescription: The Uno Platform Studio app is a zero-install application that runs seamlessly on desktop, web, and mobile, removing the cross-platform .NET setup barrier of depending on iOS, Android, Windows, and Mac SDKs. From the browser at platform.uno, a user types a prompt (e.g., "build a weather app") and an agent spins up a full cross-platform .NET app, visually building it so the UI can be tweaked. Once happy, the user exports and drops down into their IDE or CLI for a full cross-platform .NET experience. It is positioned against tools like Lovable and Bolt but produces a real .NET cross-platform app rather than vibe coding.

mentions.sessionTitle: Shipping custom models at scale from fine-tuning to inference
mentions.rawName: Unsloth has reached 300 million total downloads on Hugging Face
mentions.shortDescription: Han cites the milestone while describing Unsloth's work fixing model bugs and speeding up training.
mentions.longDescription: Daniel Han from Unsloth [inferred] describes how the team helps large labs release models and fixes bugs in them, noting they just reached 300 million total downloads on Hugging Face. He mentions Unsloth makes training faster and more memory efficient, also supports reinforcement learning, has a GitHub package, and offers a UI.

mentions.sessionTitle: Shipping custom models at scale from fine-tuning to inference
mentions.shortDescription: Han references a joint blog post ("LoRA Without Regret" [inferred]) showing that even a LoRA rank of 1 works well for specific use cases like math and coding.
mentions.longDescription: Daniel Han explains LoRA as a fine-tuning approach where, instead of updating every weight, you add a small sliver of weights (an A matrix times a B matrix) added to the large model, updating only about 1% of weights for much less memory usage. He references a collaboration with Thinking Machines on a blog post ("LoRA Without Regret" [inferred]) showing that even a LoRA rank of 1 works well for specific use cases like math and coding. He cautions that hyperparameters must be chosen carefully, such as a learning rate 10 times larger than normal (2E-4) and an adjusted alpha/scaling.

mentions.sessionTitle: From observability to ROI for AI agents on any framework
mentions.shortDescription: Automatically generates realistic multi-turn conversations to bootstrap evaluation when multi-turn data is unavailable.
mentions.longDescription: User simulation is a feature shipping alongside multi-turn evaluation that automatically generates realistic conversations. If you do not have multi-turn data available to run your first evaluation, user simulation helps you get started by producing that conversational data.

mentions.sessionTitle: Supercharged profiling: Finding performance bugs with agents
mentions.rawName: Visual Studio integration with benchmark.net diagnosers
mentions.shortDescription: A Visual Studio diagnoser package published on NuGet (benchmark.net Diagnosers) lets the profiler pull diagnostic data from a benchmark while it runs.
mentions.longDescription: When generating the benchmark, the agent installs benchmark.net Diagnosers (a diagnostics hub package). BenchmarkDotNet [inferred] has a concept of diagnosers that allow different tools to pull diagnostic information from a benchmark while it is running. Visual Studio publishes one of these diagnoser packages on NuGet that lets it interact with the profiler and pull that data, providing the integration between the Visual Studio profiler and benchmarks.

mentions.sessionTitle: Under the hood of Microsoft AI models
mentions.shortDescription: Most natural-sounding speech model yet, preferred in 72% of blind listening tests, with fine-grained emotional control, voice cloning from a few seconds of audio, and a sub-150ms Flash variant for voice agents
mentions.longDescription: Voice 2 is Microsoft AI's latest speech generation model, distinguished by its naturalness through deep work on prosody—the rhythm, stress, and intonation that make speech sound human rather than like a text-to-speech engine. Its headline new capability is fine-grained emotional control, letting users tune not just what the voice says but how it feels (warm, urgent, conversational, joyful), available today in 15 languages with more coming. It also performs high-fidelity voice cloning from just a couple seconds of source audio. A Flash variant designed for voice agents with very low latency is also planned, and the model can be tried on the MAI Playground or in Foundry.

mentions.sessionTitle: From prototype to production: build and run agents at scale
mentions.rawName: Voice Live integration with Foundry Agent Service
mentions.shortDescription: GA for prompt agents and public preview for hosted agents
mentions.longDescription: Voice Live integration with Foundry Agent Service is generally available today for prompt agents and in public preview for hosted agents. It supports speech and voice scenarios for agents.

mentions.sessionTitle: Why your AI code doesn’t ship: Closing the gap to production
mentions.shortDescription: Dictation-driven agent control, which Boyle uses with a hot-keyed remote to direct the agent while walking around
mentions.longDescription: Boyle notes that voice mode just shipped in the CLI, enabling dictation-driven control of the agent. He describes using it at home with a hot-keyed remote plugged into his computer so he can walk around his office with headphones on, clicking the remote to think out loud and direct his agent. He frames this as a highly productive way to work since he thinks while he walks.

mentions.sessionTitle: What we learned shipping VS Code weekly (without breaking everything)
mentions.rawName: VSC bench, a purpose-built offline evaluation stack
mentions.shortDescription: Runs many daily evaluations of models and prompts against custom cases, plotting total tokens against resolution rate to inform reasoning-effort and shipping decisions
mentions.longDescription: VSC bench [inferred] (heard as "BSE bench") is the team's purpose-built offline evaluation stack for VS Code, created because publicly available evaluation infrastructure and benchmarks were found insufficient for making objective product decisions. It uses the team's own cases and infrastructure to run many evaluations every day with different variations, measuring the impact of changes on metrics like total tokens and resolution rate. Sample plots of total tokens over resolution rate show trade-offs, for example that higher reasoning efforts (overlaid on the plot) do not always yield the best resolution rate and can cost significantly more tokens. These results inform pre-launch decisions about prompts and which reasoning effort to ship.

mentions.sessionTitle: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio: Agents That Debug, Profile, and Test
mentions.rawName: Web Forms to Blazor app modernization
mentions.shortDescription: A modernization agent can convert legacy Web Forms apps, including user controls and server controls, into Blazor, optionally layering in Aspire and cloud readiness.
mentions.longDescription: Recent breakthroughs in app modernization allow a modernization agent to convert legacy Web Forms applications—including user controls and server controls components—into Blazor [inferred]. This lets old apps, such as ones running on older .NET versions, be moved completely onto a modern stack. Optionally, Aspire can be layered on and the app can be upscaled to run in the cloud, all handled by the modernization agent.

mentions.sessionTitle: Foundry IQ: Fuel agents with enterprise knowledge and agentic retrieval
mentions.shortDescription: Announced the prior day, providing web search grounding that can be added to a knowledge base as an MCP knowledge source
mentions.longDescription: To enable agents to access the web, the speaker referenced Web IQ, which had been announced the prior day, as part of the broader IQ platform that also includes Work IQ (for M365 tenant data) and Fabric IQ (for analytics data such as data lakes and warehouses). Each IQ component works fine in isolation, so if data lives in a single place, that one component can be used directly. Foundry IQ supports integrating and connecting to the entire spectrum of the IQ platform out-of-the-box, making it easy to combine an agent's own application data with M365 content, analytics data, and web access.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Build opening keynote
mentions.shortDescription: Model-agnostic, MCP-native web grounding plus a unified IQ layer (Web IQ, Fabric IQ, Work IQ, Foundry IQ) for grounding agents in enterprise context.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft announced Web IQ, a web-grounding capability built on its global infrastructure serving over a billion users but re-architected for LLM and agentic workflows. It is model-agnostic and MCP-native, plugs into any agent runtime, and spans web, news, images, and video so agents can ground responses in fresh, verifiable content, leading in quality, speed, and cost. Above the data tier, Microsoft is building a unified IQ layer that brings together Foundry, Fabric, and Microsoft 365 for a continuously updated understanding of an organization. This structured context aims to deliver the right grounding to make models more token-efficient.

mentions.sessionTitle: Japan Wrap-up Session
mentions.rawName: Web IQ and Work IQ API GA
mentions.shortDescription: Adds web grounding optimized for agents to the existing Work/Public/Foundry IQ family, with the Work IQ API reaching general availability
mentions.longDescription: In addition to the existing Work IQ, Public IQ, and Foundry IQ family, Microsoft presented Web IQ, an engine optimized for agent processing that supports web grounding, doing so faster and at lower cost than previously possible. The transcript also notes that customers want to use this capability in their own applications, and a key point is that the Work IQ API actually reaches general availability (GA).

mentions.sessionTitle: Build Apps w/ Local AI for Unmetered Intelligence on every Windows PC
mentions.shortDescription: Brings native Windows ML hardware acceleration to web apps in Chromium-based browsers via experimental flags.
mentions.longDescription: WebNN is available in preview with a few experimental flags in any Chromium-based browser such as Edge or Chrome, bringing native Windows ML hardware acceleration to web apps. It sits as a layer on top of native ML APIs like Windows ML, providing near-native access to GPUs, NPUs, and CPUs through framework APIs, so even websites can benefit from hardware acceleration without racking up token costs or sending sensitive enterprise data to the cloud. In the demo, a sentiment analyzer web app used the ONNX Runtime web APIs, which under the hood use WebNN working with Windows ML, and passed in models previously optimized through the Windows ML CLI.

mentions.sessionTitle: Expand local AI reach with Windows ML
mentions.rawName: WebNN now backed by Windows ML
mentions.shortDescription: On Windows, WebNN uses Windows ML for faster hardware-accelerated inferencing in Edge or Chrome browsers (currently in developer preview).
mentions.longDescription: WebNN is being updated to use Windows ML when running on Windows, as demonstrated earlier in the session. This leads to faster hardware-accelerated machine learning model inferencing when using the Edge or Chrome browsers.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build the thing that builds the thing
mentions.rawName: Weekly re-runs of triage across all issues
mentions.shortDescription: Re-evaluates every open issue and PR at least weekly, notifying original reporters via Discord when their problem was already fixed on main.
mentions.longDescription: Because triage is not a static process and a fix landing on main can resolve issues that were never read among many thousands of open ones, Clause Reaper [inferred] is re-run on every issue and pull request at least once a week (and could be run daily depending on token budget). A Discord integration then reports when an old issue has been closed, and the person who originally wrote the issue gets a response telling them it was fixed on main. The speaker emphasizes this is fully automated so he does not have to deal with it manually.

mentions.sessionTitle: Your PC, Your Rules: AI Agents Meet Windows Personalization
mentions.shortDescription: A theme module downloads themed wallpapers, writes accent colors to the Explorer accent registry path, and applies light/dark mode in a single pass, shipping with real Microsoft MSIX package themes.
mentions.longDescription: The theme module goes beyond RGB lighting: when the user says something like "ocean theme," the skill orchestrates everything in a single pass. It can download themed wallpapers, write accent colors to the Explorer accent registry path, and more. The skill ships with a library of real Microsoft MSIX package themes, treating a single expressed intent as one coherent action executed directly against Windows.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and ship faster with a developer-optimized Windows experience
mentions.rawName: Win UI agents and skills plugin
mentions.shortDescription: A plugin bringing skills and agents (packaging, code review, design, templates) for Win UI/Windows development to GitHub Copilot or Claude Code, reportedly saving over 70% of measurable tokens
mentions.longDescription: A new set of agents and skills for Win UI and Windows development, delivered as a plugin (called Win UI) that can be installed into GitHub Copilot or Claude Code [inferred]. The plugin includes skills and agents for tasks like packaging, code review, and design, going beyond simple markdown skills by providing tools that agents can use to develop Windows applications end to end. Through this process the team reports saving over 70% of measurable tokens, reducing the cost of using AI tools to build Windows apps.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and ship faster with a developer-optimized Windows experience
mentions.shortDescription: A CLI installable via WinGet that packages apps as MSIX, runs applications with package identity, and works with frameworks like Rust without Visual Studio; previously announced earlier this year
mentions.longDescription: The WinApp CLI, announced earlier this year, is a command-line tool installable via WinGet ('winget install winapp') that lets developers and agents package applications and run them with package identity without Visual Studio. It can package an app from a folder as an MSIX or run an application directly with identity, enabling use of APIs like notifications and AI APIs. It works with existing frameworks—for example running a Rust console application—so developers can keep their current framework and extend it with Windows APIs.

mentions.sessionTitle: Accelerating developer productivity with Windows 365
mentions.rawName: Windows 11 developer configuration image in public preview
mentions.shortDescription: A developer-optimized marketplace image that arrives pre-loaded with Visual Studio, Git, GitHub CLI, Python, Node.js, GitHub Copilot, and WSL with Ubuntu already configured.
mentions.longDescription: Windows 365 now supports a new Windows 11 developer configuration image in public preview, delivering a developer-optimized Cloud PC that is ready to go on sign-in rather than a vanilla machine. Tools like Visual Studio, Git, GitHub CLI, Python, Node.js, and GitHub Copilot are already installed, and WSL with Ubuntu is set up so developers can work across both Windows and Linux workflows. It also includes developer-focused settings and Windows configurations to cut down setup friction and get to a first commit faster. The environment can be further customized with the exact SDKs, CLIs, packages, and build tools a project requires while staying within enterprise guardrails.

mentions.sessionTitle: Powering enterprise-grade AI agents with Windows 365 for Agents
mentions.rawName: Windows 365 for Agents is generally available
mentions.shortDescription: the platform giving first- and third-party AI agents their own managed Cloud PCs is now GA.
mentions.longDescription: Windows 365 for Agents is announced as generally available, giving AI agents their own Cloud PCs—full Windows environments that can see, interact with apps, and operate the way a real person would. It addresses the problem that agents can reason, plan, and call APIs but get stuck when they need to actually open applications, fill out forms, or navigate legacy systems. The platform bridges the GUI gap, the legacy gap (Win32 applications), and the scale gap by providing enterprise-grade execution environments for agentic workloads at global scale with security and governance.

mentions.sessionTitle: Accelerating developer productivity with Windows 365
mentions.rawName: Windows 365 for Agents is generally available
mentions.shortDescription: Gives AI agents their own Cloud PCs with full Windows environments so they can see, interact with apps, and operate as a person would.
mentions.longDescription: Windows 365 for Agents is generally available, giving AI agents their own Cloud PC with a full Windows environment so they can see, interact with apps, and operate the way a person would. It addresses three problems agent builders face: the GUI gap (work that happens in graphical line-of-business apps and browser portals built for humans, not APIs), the legacy gap (mainframe terminal emulators and desktop-only tools that can be automated as-is without API wrapping or screen-scraping), and the scale gap (managing images, security, and lifecycle when going from one agent to many). The platform provides pooled Cloud PCs managed at scale and governed by IT, the same way an organization manages a fleet of employee machines.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build Apps w/ Local AI for Unmetered Intelligence on every Windows PC
mentions.rawName: Windows AI APIs expanded beyond NPUs to CPUs and GPUs
mentions.shortDescription: Many of the task-specific APIs now run across a broader hardware spectrum in response to customer feedback, reaching non-Copilot+ devices.
mentions.longDescription: In response to extensive customer feedback, Microsoft is expanding support for many of the Windows AI APIs to run on CPUs and GPUs, not just NPUs. When the AI APIs first launched they targeted the NPU and ran best on Copilot+ PCs, but the broadened hardware support lets developers reach a wider set of devices and customers, including non-Copilot+ devices. This was demonstrated with a drive-through application using the new speech recognition API to convert spoken orders to text.

mentions.sessionTitle: Microsoft Build opening keynote
mentions.shortDescription: Intelligent Terminal with GitHub Copilot, 75+ Linux command-line utilities (grep, curl, tar, sudo), Homebrew/Starship/Zsh support, vertical taskbar, and first-class WSL containers.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft announced a range of Windows developer experience updates aimed at making Windows the best place to build, whether on laptop, desktop, or cloud. These include a distraction-free dev environment, an intelligent terminal with built-in GitHub Copilot, and extensive Linux support with 70-plus command-line utilities (such as grep) now available on Windows. It also brings Mac-loved tools like Starship, Z Shell, and native Homebrew, and introduces first-class WSL containers to ease environment management. Windows 365 also gains a developer distribution optimized for cloud productivity.

mentions.sessionTitle: Expand local AI reach with Windows ML
mentions.shortDescription: Updated to bring ONNX Runtime 1.24 with performance and stability improvements plus newly updated plugin-based execution providers usable across different runtime versions.
mentions.longDescription: Windows ML has been updated to version 2.0, bringing ONNX Runtime 1.24, which includes a number of performance and stability updates. It also adds newly updated plugin-based execution providers that have performance improvements and allow execution providers to be used across different runtime versions more easily.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build Apps w/ Local AI for Unmetered Intelligence on every Windows PC
mentions.shortDescription: Includes ONNX Runtime improvements, new hardware-vendor plug-in execution providers, and up to 2.6x throughput for generative AI workloads.
mentions.longDescription: Windows ML 2.0 has shipped and is currently available in preview, including ONNX Runtime improvements and support for new hardware-vendor plug-in execution providers, which together mean support for new models, fundamentals improvements, and improved compatibility between releases. Generative AI experiences using LLMs or other generative workflows can see up to 2.6x throughput depending on the model, and the default CPU execution provider also gains performance speed-ups. Apps built using Windows ML benefit from innovation across the silicon ecosystem—AMD, Intel, NVIDIA, and Qualcomm—including support for newest devices like AMD Ryzen AI 400 series processors, Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors, upcoming NVIDIA RTX Spark and DGX Station devices, and Qualcomm Snapdragon X2 Elite processors.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build Apps w/ Local AI for Unmetered Intelligence on every Windows PC
mentions.shortDescription: A one-stop toolchain for model conversion, optimization, and benchmarking, with agent skills, available at ak.ms/winmlcli.
mentions.longDescription: Microsoft announced the brand new Windows ML CLI, now available in preview on GitHub, intended to cater to all model optimization needs. It provides a one-stop tool chain and set of agent skills so developers can take a model through conversion, optimization, and benchmarking in one flow, with the flexibility to run each stage manually via primitive commands or run the whole pipeline end to end using a prebuilt config. It is built to integrate with AI workflows and agents, for example using GitHub Copilot, and developers preferring UI can use the Foundry Toolkit extension in VS Code. It is available at aka.ms/winmlcli.

mentions.sessionTitle: Expand local AI reach with Windows ML
mentions.shortDescription: A new command-line tool for converting and optimizing models to run locally on Windows across CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs, including `hub`, `export`, and optimization commands.
mentions.longDescription: The Windows ML CLI is a new command-line tool that helps developers convert and optimize models to run locally on Windows across CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs. It was highlighted as part of what's new with Windows ML in 2026.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and ship faster with a developer-optimized Windows experience
mentions.shortDescription: A public, forkable GitHub repo with an opinionated WinGet config that installs developer tools (Python, Node, NVM [inferred], PowerToys, Git) and applies settings like dark mode and File Explorer tweaks, removing the need to manually enable developer mode; generally available today
mentions.longDescription: A WinGet configuration file, published as a public and forkable GitHub repo, that installs developer tools through a single run rather than manual setup. It takes an opinionated approach to what developers need, installing apps like PowerToys, Python, Node, NVM [inferred], and Git, while also applying settings such as dark mode and File Explorer tweaks. It removes the need to manually turn on developer mode, and is flexible so developers can configure or add other tools. It ships by default on some newly announced devices and can also be used to set up existing devices.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building WinUI Apps with C# First Patterns and AI Assisted Workflows
mentions.rawName: WinUI drops its version number, signaling long-term commitment
mentions.shortDescription: WinUI 3 will now be referred to simply as "WinUI" to convey there is no intention of building yet another new framework or a massive breaking change.
mentions.longDescription: In response to community questions about whether Microsoft is serious about sticking with the framework, the team announced that WinUI 3 (now four years old) will be referred to simply as "WinUI," dropping the version number to signal there is no intention of building yet another new framework or making a massive breaking change. The team is pushing to stretch WinUI to be accessible for any use case and is integrating it into the shell at a faster rate, with many first-party Microsoft features being built on top of WinUI. They emphasized commitment to moving WinUI forward and hope to see broader third-party and enterprise adoption.

mentions.sessionTitle: Building a Multi-Agent Workflow in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.rawName: Work IQ exposed as MCP servers
mentions.shortDescription: Specialized Work IQ endpoints (mail, Teams, calendar, Word, Copilot) wake up based on the user's natural-language query, callable from Copilot, Foundry, and Copilot Studio
mentions.longDescription: Work IQ is exposed as MCP servers, with different specialized endpoints for Copilot, Teams, calendar, mail, Word, and so on. Depending on the user's natural-language query, the relevant Work IQ MCP wakes up—for example, asking to send or summarize an email activates the Work IQ Mail MCP, which then returns the information. The presenter demonstrates calling it from Copilot and from Foundry, where an IQ agent uses Work IQ Mail as a tool and a human-in-the-loop approval prompt appears because the Foundry agent is treated as external to the company's identity.

mentions.sessionTitle: Ship safer code from your IDE with Aikido
mentions.shortDescription: A full workspace scan lists all files with detected issues, and a dependency scan surfaces vulnerable open-source dependencies with autofix capability in the IDE.
mentions.longDescription: While other scans are running, you can also run a dependency scan and a full-on workspace scan across an entire repo loaded in VS Code. A workspace scan runs through the entire workspace and lists all of the files where an issue was detected, letting you click through each one. A dependency scan surfaces open-source dependencies and their issues, with the ability to fix them using Aikido AI or report false positives.

mentions.sessionTitle: Securing, scaling, and sustaining your data estate in Microsoft Fabric
mentions.shortDescription: Outbound access protection, trusted workspace access, Azure Private Link, customer-managed keys, and workspace-level IP firewall rules
mentions.longDescription: Workspace admins can secure workspaces end-to-end by layering identity, permissions, and network controls: Entra Conditional Access ensures only managed devices reach the workspace, workspace roles define what contributors and viewers can do, and inbound networking can block public access and restrict connections to a corporate IP range via firewall. Outbound access protection blocks all outgoing connections unless explicitly allowed, with trusted rules and managed private endpoints opened only after the resource owner approves. When a user tries to connect a notebook to a personal storage account, Fabric blocks it outright so data never leaves the building.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and ship faster with a developer-optimized Windows experience
mentions.shortDescription: A built-in way to create, run, and interact with Linux containers natively on Windows, shipping with the standard WSL update and exposed as an API for use inside native applications, plus enterprise management controls
mentions.longDescription: WSL containers is a built-in way to create, run, and interact with Linux containers directly on Windows, so containers just work natively out-of-the-box for local development, AI/ML workflows, and containerized testing. It ships with the standard WSL update with no extra configuration, and includes WSLC, a binary for creating, running, and interacting with containers without third-party tools. Usage is as simple as listing containers (e.g., 'WSLC container LS'), attaching to a running container's Linux shell, and detaching when done.

mentions.sessionTitle: Taking your AI to the edge with .NET MAUI
mentions.shortDescription: Opt-in feature compiling XAML to readable, debuggable C# with cited gains of ~1,000% faster inflation, 99% less debug memory, and reduced app memory; default in .NET 11
mentions.longDescription: XAML source generation is an opt-in feature that uses Roslyn to generate readable, debuggable C# source from XAML, rather than the current XAML-C compilation to intermediate language. It delivers faster debug and release performance by flipping one bit, with cited gains of 1,000% faster inflation, 99% less debug memory, faster release, and less app memory, with the biggest improvement in debug builds. It also eliminates differences between debug and release builds (such as trimmed APIs breaking at runtime). It is opt-in in .NET 10 and will become the default in .NET 11.

mentions.sessionTitle: Build and deploy an Azure app with your agent team
mentions.shortDescription: A team of four agents (classifier, enrichment, triage, aggregate) that analyzes customer feedback sentiment and triggers actions such as drafting replacement emails.
mentions.longDescription: A demo system built for Zava, an online retailer, to help understand customer feedback and take actions on it. It is a team of agents fronted by a website connected to a back end running in Microsoft Foundry that understands and analyzes customer feedback to give insights on customer sentiment. Examples shown include mixed feedback (price reasonable but delivery slow) and a report of an app crash, with the system able to trigger actions such as drafting replacement emails.

mentions.sessionTitle: Agentic infrastructure needs agentic observability
mentions.shortDescription: The observability layer instruments automatically because humans cannot keep instrumentation current in AI-generated systems
mentions.longDescription: Zero instrumentation and zero friction is groundcover's second architectural bet, where the observability layer instruments automatically. The speaker argues you cannot depend on humans to manually keep instrumentation current in AI-generated systems.
